sections.name: add_block
sections.invariant: on the extend branch the four consensus trees (output_index, height_index, state, tx_index) move together via `Database::commit_block_atomic`; in-memory tip never lands ahead of a failed disk commit (commit failure PANICS rather than diverging). Supply/burn use `checked_add` + panic (symmetry with the reorg-rollback `checked_sub`).
sections.threat: torn write leaving height index ahead of state → post-crash double-spend / inflation.

sections.name: inner.tip.hash != tip_hash
sections.invariant: if the tip advanced between the read and the apply, the extend is abandoned and the block falls through to the fork path, never double-applied to a stale tip.
sections.threat: concurrent-writer TOCTOU that applies the same block twice / onto the wrong parent.

sections.name: calculate_fork_cumulative_work
sections.invariant: genesis contributes a fixed base of 1 (not `dft(genesis)`) so an equal-work fork is never spuriously heavier; strictly-greater work switches, exactly-equal work breaks deterministically by lexicographic tip hash (`fork_tip < current_tip` wins) — network-deterministic, no timestamp tiebreak.
sections.threat: selfish-miner / equivocation split from a nondeterministic or timestamp-gameable tiebreak.

sections.name: find_fork_point
sections.invariant: fork walks bound their steps and return `None`/partial on a cycle or missing parent (never loop forever); `recompute_total_difficulty` = `1 + Σ dft(1..=h)` and agrees with the fork walk.
sections.threat: crafted prev_hash cycle → hang / corruption-driven acceptance.

sections.name: apply_reorg_atomic
sections.invariant: the whole switch (output removals/adds, height sets/removals, state, tx add/remove) commits atomically or not at all; losing-fork work never leaks into `total_difficulty`; orphaned non-coinbase txs are returned for mempool restore.
sections.threat: partial reorg commit → hybrid tip / inflation.

sections.name: 6 C1 fork vs active UTXO validation + double spend defense  (con
sections.invariant: a fork sharing a real non-coinbase tx / double-spent key image with the active branch is rejected; tip unchanged, key image stays unspent, supply unchanged.
sections.threat: reorg-driven double-spend / inflation.

sections.name: reorg_error
sections.invariant: when a fork block fails mid-reorg, rollback restores pre-reorg tip/stats/UTXO/output_index exactly. H3 FIX: path-A removal is now bounded by the highest fork height so a failed reorg no longer leaves stale `height_to_hash` entries above the restored tip; path A and path B are mutually exclusive (`!rolled_back` fires path B only when path A did not, e.g. a triggering-block difficulty recheck failure).
sections.threat: stale height→hash mapping after a rejected reorg → later reads resolve a ghost block.

sections.name: rollback_to_height
sections.invariant: refuses to roll back below the persisted `last_checkpoint` (FINALITY VIOLATION → `Err`, no mutation); disconnects DB-only blocks past the ~200-block cache window via DB fallback; unwinds supply/burn through the same disconnect site as connect (symmetric); `target >= height` is a no-op.
sections.threat: deep rollback past finality; silent under-disconnect when the body is only on disk.

sections.name: fork_point
sections.threat: latent inflation / stuck-spent key image near the cache boundary.

sections.name: checked_sub
sections.invariant: every supply/burn move uses checked arithmetic and PANICS (halts) on under/overflow rather than silently clamping — a clamp would mask corruption/inflation; `total_supply` is `u128` (survives the old `u64` ~18.4M-CYNC ceiling). L2: `total_burned` and the block/tx counters move in lockstep with `total_supply` (`checked_sub` None → logs `STATS INVARIANT VIOLATION` and floors, not panic, for the telemetry counters).
sections.threat: silent underflow → phantom supply / inflation (ring-size determinism, 1d27d3c8).

sections.name: load_from_database
sections.invariant: a load either yields a fully-consistent chain or errors — never a half-state mistaken for fresh; genesis/tip/height/network are cross-checked and the UTXO set + block/tx counters are reconstructed (not reset to 0) on reopen.
sections.threat: a drifted/partial DB booted as canonical → fork from the network.

sections.name: init_genesis
sections.invariant: genesis hash must equal the expected network genesis (mismatch → `Err`); on init supply = `reward(0)`, burned = 0, and genesis+height+state are persisted; `verify_tip_integrity` reloads from DB when the in-memory tip disagrees with `state.tip_hash`.
sections.threat: wrong-network / forged genesis silently adopted.

sections.name: is_spent
sections.invariant: `is_spent` returns the in-memory hit, then the DB fallback, and on a DB *error* returns `true` (fail-CLOSED) — a lookup failure must never let a key image be treated as spendable; `max_reorg_depth` uses the runtime network, not the compile feature.
sections.threat: DB error opening a double-spend window; feature/runtime network mismatch loosening the reorg cap.

sections.name: checkpoint_phase2_stores
sections.invariant: the three phase-2 stores checkpoint and rewind together in lockstep with block connect/disconnect; a rewind past an empty checkpoint stack hits the loud error branch rather than silently desyncing.
sections.threat: phase-2 root divergence across a reorg → shielded/MW state inconsistent with the transparent chain.

sections.name: total_fees
sections.invariant: sums fees of the non-coinbase txs ONLY (coinbase excluded), via `saturating_add` so an attacker-crafted fee sum past `u64::MAX` saturates rather than wrapping/panicking.
sections.threat: coinbase fee counted → miner over-claims; fee-sum overflow wrap → understated total lets an oversized coinbase pass the reward check.

sections.name: coinbase
sections.invariant: returns the first tx, or `None` on an empty tx list (never panics / indexes out of bounds).
sections.threat: empty-block panic (DoS); mis-identifying the coinbase slot.

sections.name: non_coinbase_transactions
sections.invariant: iterates every tx except the first; empty when only a coinbase is present. This `skip(1)` is the single definition of "non-coinbase" reused by §1 and §4.
sections.threat: off-by-one that leaks the coinbase into, or drops a real tx from, fee/key-image accounting.

sections.name: all_key_images
sections.invariant: collects key images from non-coinbase inputs ONLY; a coinbase carrying an input contributes nothing.
sections.threat: coinbase-sourced key image poisoning the double-spend set, or a missed key image letting a double-spend through the block-level check.

sections.name: verify_merkle_root
sections.invariant: recomputes the root over the txs in order and compares to `header.tx_root`; empty tx list is valid iff the committed root is `Hash::zero()`. Because the root is recomputed from the actual tx order, tampering, wrong root, or REORDERING all diverge.
sections.threat: tx tampering after PoW; tx REORDERING / duplication malleability (CVE-2012-2459-class — the duplication defense proper lives in `primitives::merkle_root`; this method's job is to bind the committed root to the exact tx list & order, so a reordered or mutated set is rejected).

sections.name: size
sections.invariant: `200 + Σ tx.size()` folded with `saturating_add` so a crafted set of huge txs cannot overflow `usize` and understate size.
sections.threat: size-underflow wrap slipping an over-cap block past `check_block_size`.

sections.name: hash
sections.invariant: each returns the header-derived value verbatim; `is_genesis` iff `header.height == 0`; `hash` delegates to `header.hash()`.
sections.threat: accessor drift from the header it mirrors.

sections.name: calculate_difficulty
sections.invariant: output stays inside the per-block clamp `[tip/2, tip*2]` AND never exceeds `max_t = u128::MAX / MIN_DIFFICULTY` (the consensus floor is enforced for every input, emergency path included); integer-only and deterministic.
sections.threat: difficulty manipulation / block production outrunning P2P propagation once target drifts past the floor.

sections.name: apply_asert
sections.invariant: canonical aserti3-2d — the exponent denominator is `halflife` (in seconds) ALONE, so one halflife of time_error exactly doubles/halves the target; `height_diff == 0` returns the current target; exponent overflow saturates and the integer exponent clamps at ±`MAX_INT_EXPONENT`.
sections.threat: **S1 unit-confusion — caused a TESTNET WIPE**; the bugged `halflife*target_time` denominator made ASERT ~120× too weak.

sections.name: needs_emergency_drop
sections.invariant: triggers only when `time_diff` strictly exceeds `expected × EMERGENCY_TIME_MULTIPLIER`; the bootstrap guard (`current_height < EMERGENCY_DIFFICULTY_BLOCKS*2`) and the short-history guard suppress it; the drop still respects the MIN_DIFFICULTY floor.
sections.threat: false emergency easing during startup or a benign stall.

sections.name: get_anchor
sections.invariant: never anchors ASERT on the genesis block (height 0) while it is inside the window, but uses it when it is the only block; deterministic across nodes.
sections.threat: a stale genesis timestamp making the chain look catastrophically slow and collapsing difficulty to the floor.

sections.name: safe_mul_u128
sections.invariant: a u128 product overflow saturates at `u128::MAX` (= easiest target / minimum difficulty), never wraps or panics.
sections.threat: R-4 — the old shift-fallback lost low bits and produced a wrong (too-small) target in the consensus-critical overflow path.

sections.name: decompose_fixed_point
sections.invariant: integer u128 fixed-point `2^x` approximation, error < 0.1% across `[0, RADIX)`; handles `i128::MIN` without panic.
sections.threat: H-1 — f64 is non-deterministic across CPU architectures and would fork consensus.

sections.name: target_to_u128
sections.invariant: roundtrip preserves the upper 16 bytes; an all-zero target maps to `1` via `.max(1)` so downstream division never divides by zero; `calculate_difficulty_from_target` is an exact alias.
sections.threat: div-by-zero DoS on a crafted zero target.

sections.name: max_target
sections.invariant: `max_target` is all-`0xFF`; the dual-window weights satisfy `SHORT_WEIGHT + LONG_WEIGHT == WEIGHT_SCALE`.
sections.threat: a mis-set weight constant silently skewing the short/long blend.

sections.name: calculate_fee
sections.invariant: `fee == size·MIN_FEE_PER_BYTE·mult/100`, integer-exact with the block validator (no f64 boundary drift).
sections.threat: wallet estimate vs validator divergence → honest txs rejected.

sections.name: congestion_multiplier
sections.invariant: integer buckets match the validator exactly; `congestion > 100` collapses to ×3.

sections.name: calculate_congestion
sections.invariant: u64 saturating fold (no 32-bit overflow); empty ⇒ 0; capped at 100.
sections.threat: A7-CONG-01 (overflow hides real congestion).

sections.name: calculate_priority_fee
sections.invariant: priority clamped `[0,100]`; NaN / negative saturate, never panic.

sections.name: distribute_fee
sections.invariant: `to_miner + burned + to_protocol == total` with ZERO rounding loss (last bucket = exact remainder).
sections.threat: A8-DIST-01 (triple truncation loses ≤2 atomic units).

sections.name: block_fee_stats
sections.invariant: u64 saturating folds; no overflow on 32-bit / extreme fees.
sections.threat: A9-STATS-01.

sections.name: FeeCalculator
sections.invariant: estimate matches the free `distribute_fee`; non-finite fee falls back to unscaled base.

sections.name: max_reorg_depth_for
sections.invariant: the hard-finality cap is chosen from the RUNTIME `NetworkType` (Testnet/Regtest = 1000, Mainnet = 100), never from a compile-time feature.
sections.threat: F31 (SEV-A) — a testnet-configured binary built without `--features testnet` using the mainnet 100-cap, the 2026-07-04 partition trap.

sections.name: max_reorg_depth
sections.invariant: the legacy no-arg form falls back to the SAFER Testnet=1000 interpretation, so a pre-audit caller never silently gets the tighter mainnet cap.
sections.threat: cfg/runtime divergence re-introducing the F31 trap.

sections.name: evaluate_reorg_acceptability
sections.invariant: any depth strictly beyond the network cap is rejected outright (absolute finality); depth == max_depth is still accepted (off-by-one guarded). The error cites the cap.
sections.threat: deep-reorg double-spend past finality (ETC/BTG/Horizen-class).

sections.name: depth <= REORG_UNCONDITIONAL_DEPTH
sections.invariant: shallow reorgs (≤ 10) accept EQUAL-or-more work (`>=`) — the monotonic hash-lex tiebreak upstream makes equal-work acceptance a deterministic convergence rule; strictly-less work is rejected; depth 11 is the first to enter MESS.
sections.threat: normal jitter mis-rejected, or a low-work fork accepted.

sections.name: 5 Tier 2 MESS (exponential work multiplier)
sections.invariant: a fork at depth d needs `2^((d-10)/20)` more work; the exponent is capped at 40 so the `1u128 << e` shift cannot overflow, and `required_work` uses `saturating_mul` so honest_work near `u128::MAX` cannot wrap.
sections.threat: rented-hashrate deep reorg made economically infeasible; overflow/wrap defeating the gate.

sections.name: current_height < BOOTSTRAP_MESS_HEIGHT
sections.invariant: below the bootstrap height MESS is skipped (plain longest-chain, equal work accepted) so independently-booted young forks can converge; the Tier-3 hard cap is STILL enforced during bootstrap.
sections.threat: parallel young forks permanently locked by an unsatisfiable multiplier.

sections.name: bits
sections.invariant: every CIP occupies a distinct bit, `MUST_SET` (bit 31) is always OR'd in by `SignalBits::new`, and `signals()` reports exactly the set bits.
sections.threat: a bit collision makes one coinbase appear to signal two CIPs, corrupting both activation machines.

sections.name: Deployment
sections.invariant: every Phase-2 deployment (halo2 / lelantus-spark / mw-cutthrough) and the v1.0.12 bundle ship DORMANT — all three height fields `u64::MAX` — until an operator enables them (M-5).
sections.threat: a non-MAX height lets the BIP-9 state machine begin transitioning a pre-audit privacy upgrade silently against the live chain.

sections.name: DeploymentState
sections.invariant: the state machine has exactly the BIP-9 states Defined → Started → LockedIn → Active, plus Failed on timeout; `signaling_pct` is a 0..=100 UI value only.
sections.threat: an unrepresentable or skipped state misreports activation to explorers/validators.

sections.name: extra
sections.invariant: `SignalBits(0)` encodes to the byte-identical 8-byte legacy layout; a real signal appends 4 LE bytes; `decode_signal_bits` never panics on short/attacker-controlled input and ignores trailing bytes beyond 12 (forward-compat).
sections.threat: block-hash drift for no-signal coinbases, or a panic in the validator on a crafted `extra`.

sections.name: ForkSignaler::state
sections.invariant: `count >= SIGNAL_THRESHOLD` (an ABSOLUTE block count, not a percentage) locks in; past `timeout_height` without a recorded lock-in is Failed; a recorded lock-in becomes Active at `max(next_window_start, min_activation_height)`; the UI `pct` is clamped to ≤100 at a window boundary.
sections.threat: the pre-fix `pct >= SIGNAL_THRESHOLD` comparison could never be true, silently breaking all soft-fork activation.

sections.name: record_lock_in
sections.invariant: once locked in, the observation is persisted so re-querying in a later window (even with signals dropped) stays LockedIn/Active; `state_and_record` is idempotent.
sections.threat: the "forgot to record" bug class where read-only `state()` re-counts a fresh window and reverts LOCKED_IN, violating BIP-9's persistent-lock-in semantics.

sections.name: BlockHeader
sections.invariant: the field set is the complete consensus commitment; `network_magic` is FIRST so it is checked before any crypto. `supply_commitment` is RESERVED / not yet enforced (see field doc) — do not treat it as an integrity control until it is both validated and PoW-bound.
sections.threat: a silently-added/omitted field escaping the hash preimage.

sections.name: hash
sections.invariant: EVERY field feeds the preimage, so mutating any one changes the hash. A field omitted from the preimage would be malleable after a valid PoW is found.
sections.threat: header-hash malleability / post-PoW field grinding.

sections.name: hash
sections.invariant: `checkpoint_vote` is length-tagged so `Some` vs `None` and two distinct `Some` values never collide; `spark_set_root` / `mw_kernel_root` are hashed unconditionally (zero pre-fork); repeated calls are deterministic.
sections.threat: ambiguous serialization letting two headers share a hash.

sections.name: HEADER_HASH_DOMAIN_TAG
sections.invariant: each preimage is prefixed with a distinct domain tag, so the header hash can never collide with the PoW binding (or any other protocol digest — tx signing, anchor, CLSAG, bulletproof).
sections.threat: cross-protocol hash collision / preimage reuse.

sections.name: pow_binding
sections.invariant: covers EXACTLY the fields not otherwise bound by the PoW (version, miner_pubkey, supply_commitment, checkpoint_vote, spark/mw roots) and EXCLUDES those already bound (nonce/tx_root via `compute_pow_hash`; prev_hash/height/timestamp via the anchor seed; target/algorithm via direct `verify_pow` checks; anchor itself to avoid circularity).
sections.threat: audit §1 — reusing one PoW solution with an unbound field mutated (block-hash malleability + tie-break grinding).

sections.name: meets_target
sections.invariant: delegates to `Hash::meets_difficulty`; `pow_hash <= target` passes (equality is the inclusive boundary), strictly-greater fails.
sections.threat: off-by-one at the target boundary accepting/rejecting a block wrongly.

sections.name: compute_full_anchor
sections.invariant: the anchor is a deterministic pure function of `(prev_hash, height, timestamp, binding)`; the cache is keyed on all four (binding included) so two headers sharing `(prev,height,ts)` but differing in a bound field get DISTINCT anchors and never collide; a cache hit is byte-identical to a cold compute; re-insert of an existing key is a no-op.
sections.threat: audit §1 PoW/anchor malleability — folding `pow_binding` into the anchor seed binds the otherwise-unbound header fields to the proof of work.

sections.name: verify_pow
sections.invariant: recomputes the anchor from `binding` and rejects `AnchorMismatch` / `AlgorithmMismatch` / `TargetNotMet`; a mutated bound header field changes the binding → the claimed anchor no longer matches → rejected BEFORE any RandomX hashing.
sections.threat: audit §1 block-hash malleability — reusing a valid PoW with a mutated bound field (e.g. `miner_pubkey`).

sections.name: PowAlgorithm
sections.invariant: single RandomX variant; `from_index` / `at_height` always RandomX; `from_str_opt` parses `randomx`/`rx`/`0` case-insensitively and returns `None` on unknown; `is_available` is true iff the `randomx` feature is built.
sections.threat: a stray second algorithm silently parsed/accepted.

sections.name: randomx_key_for_height
sections.invariant: the epoch key is constant within an epoch (`height / RANDOMX_KEY_EPOCH`) and changes at the boundary, bound to the network's genesis; the public seed wrapper equals the internal derivation; binding is write-once — a conflicting second call is ignored and warns, the same genesis is idempotent.
sections.threat: **R-2 mainnet-vs-testnet genesis binding divergence** (the rc3 incident) — deriving PoW from the wrong genesis makes the whole chain look like network-wide invalid PoW.

sections.name: compute_pow_hash
sections.invariant: RandomX-only (hard error when the feature is disabled); the batched miner path is bit-identical to the single-shot validator path; empty nonces short-circuit to an empty vec.
sections.threat: miner/validator hash divergence, or a RandomX-less build silently proceeding.

sections.name: prewarm_next_epoch_if_near
sections.invariant: no-op far from a boundary, triggers within `LOOKAHEAD_BLOCKS` (64) of the next epoch; a promoted prewarmed dataset is byte-identical to a synchronous build (same seed → same dataset), so promotion changes only WHEN work happens, never any hash.
sections.threat: an epoch-boundary dataset rebuild stalling the mining / IBD validation hot path.

sections.name: work_from_target
sections.invariant: `max_target/target` over the upper 128 bits; a zero upper-128 target returns `u128::MAX` (no div-by-zero); monotonic — a smaller target never yields less work; `meets_difficulty` delegates to `Hash::meets_difficulty`.
sections.threat: fork-choice work miscount or a div-by-zero on a crafted target.

sections.name: randomx_cache
sections.invariant: per-thread VMs built from one shared dataset produce identical hashes across N threads; an epoch rotation rebuilds each thread's VM; full-mem and light modes are bit-identical.
sections.threat: a cross-thread VM sharing bug or a full-mem/light mode divergence forking consensus between miners and light verifiers.

sections.name: pow_preimage_key
sections.invariant: a domain-separated key over EXACTLY the fields that determine the RandomX input (`prev_hash, height, timestamp, nonce, tx_root, binding`); target-independent, deterministic, and each of those input fields changes the key.
sections.threat: caching one output across two genuinely different solutions (a false-accept).

sections.name: pow_preimage_key
sections.invariant: a different header `binding` changes the key, so malleated variants that share `(prev,height,ts,nonce,tx_root)` but differ in a bound field do NOT collapse to one cache entry.
sections.threat: audit §1 PoW/anchor malleability — a mutated bound field riding another solution's cached RandomX output.

sections.name: PowVerifyCache
sections.invariant: FIFO-bounded at `POW_VERIFY_CACHE_MAX`; an existing entry is never overwritten.
sections.threat: unbounded cache growth (memory DoS).

sections.name: 4 amplification collapse (target variants)
sections.invariant: the key omits `target`, so every target-variant of one solution derives the SAME key and shares a single cached RandomX run.
sections.threat: amplification-collapse — one mined solution mutated into unlimited hash-distinct blocks forcing unbounded memory-hard RandomX across the network.

sections.name: pow_hash_cached
sections.invariant: recomputes and binds the anchor first, so a forged `claimed_anchor` or `claimed_algo` is rejected free, BEFORE any RandomX hashing.
sections.threat: a forged anchor/algorithm poisoning the cache or wasting a RandomX run.

sections.name: pow_hash_cached
sections.invariant: a cold miss computes and caches the RandomX output; a second call for the same preimage key is a hit returning the identical output with no recompute.
sections.threat: redundant memory-hard RandomX per variant of one solution.

sections.name: enforce_privacy_policy
sections.invariant: every `TxType::Coinbase` tx is skipped; every other tx is passed through `check_tx_privacy`, and the first violation short-circuits the block.
sections.threat: a transparent/naked transfer smuggled into an otherwise-valid block, or the coinbase (legitimately transparent) being wrongly rejected.

sections.name: MANDATORY_CONFIDENTIAL
sections.invariant: every output commitment must decompress to a non-identity Ristretto point; identity OR non-decompressable ⇒ `TransparentOutputForbidden`.
sections.threat: M-6 non-canonical-identity commitment — a non-`[0;32]` byte pattern that maps to the identity point (or is not a curve point at all) would slip past the old all-zeros byte check and commit to no amount.

sections.name: MANDATORY_STEALTH
sections.invariant: every stealth address must decompress to a non-identity Ristretto point; identity OR non-decompressable ⇒ `RawPubkeyForbidden`.
sections.threat: M-3 — a non-zero but invalid/low-order stealth encoding (raw pubkey) would evade the old all-zeros check and expose the recipient.

sections.name: UnshieldedForbidden
sections.invariant: a non-coinbase tx must carry ≥1 privacy-preserving input (`tx.inputs` non-empty); zero inputs ⇒ `UnshieldedForbidden`.
sections.threat: an input-less "mint" tx with no ring signature de-anonymizing the sender (or forging value). Rule 1 is evaluated before Rule 3 by construction.

sections.name: check_block_network_magic
sections.invariant: a block is bound to THIS node's network and cannot contradict a hardcoded (height, hash) checkpoint; both run before any crypto.
sections.threat: cross-network contamination (FIX #43); reorg past a consensus checkpoint (CIP-009 Path B).

sections.name: validate_header
sections.invariant: version stays in `[min, MAX_BLOCK_VERSION]`, height/prev_hash/ timestamp are strictly monotonic vs parent, votes point to past heights, timestamp is within `MAX_TIMESTAMP_DRIFT` (genesis exempt).
sections.threat: H1 version-cap chain-brick; version-downgrade; timestamp warp.

sections.name: validate_difficulty_target
sections.invariant: every non-genesis block gets full `verify_pow` unless the compile-time `insecure-fast-sync` feature is on AND it is below checkpoint; target sits within loose sanity bounds (~32x / ~256x) paired with strict ASERT at the chain level.
sections.threat: silent PoW-skip DoS (below-checkpoint flood in a normal build); artificially-easy targets.

sections.name: check_block_size
sections.invariant: byte size ≤ `MAX_BLOCK_SIZE`, ring-sig weight ≤ 4×`MAX_BLOCK_SIZE` (runs even under fast-sync, FIX #46), tx count ≤ `MAX_TXS_PER_BLOCK`.
sections.threat: CPU-exhaustion / block-flood DoS.

sections.name: max_coinbase
sections.invariant: coinbase claims EXACTLY reward+miner-share; each output commits to `commit(declared, 0)` on-curve; sums use `checked_add`; reward stays in `[TAIL_EMISSION, reward(0)]`.
sections.threat: coinbase inflation — per-output blinding-cancellation (C19-FIX), output-sum overflow (#41), max_coinbase overflow (M4); post-year-12 tail chain-halt.

sections.name: check_block_merkle_root
sections.invariant: recomputed merkle root equals `header.tx_root`; every non-coinbase tx is committed + stealthed + shielded (Constitution Art. III).
sections.threat: tx substitution/reorder; transparent-output leakage.

sections.name: check_block_duplicate_tx_hashes
sections.invariant: no tx hash, key image, or stealth address repeats anywhere in the block.
sections.threat: in-block double-spend; cross-tx duplicate-stealth lookup-poisoning (cfc680b7).

sections.name: 8 dynamic congestion fee (inline)
sections.invariant: each non-coinbase tx pays ≥ `size·MIN_FEE_PER_BYTE·congestion_multiplier/100`, computed with `checked_mul` and the SHARED `fee_market::congestion_multiplier` table.
sections.threat: below-market block stuffing; overflow-clamp reject-all (FIX #42); validator/wallet multiplier drift.

sections.name: check_tx_version_range
sections.invariant: `1 ≤ version ≤ MAX_TX_VERSION` (before coinbase early-return); V2 only at/after activation; non-empty, bounded in/out; post-activation Transfer/Churn is 2-in/2-out or 2-in/3-out.
sections.threat: unknown-version fork injection; malformed/dust shapes reducing the anonymity set (M6).

sections.name: check_output_curve_points
sections.invariant: `stealth_address`, `tx_public_key`, and `commitment` are each non-identity and on the Ristretto curve (explicit all-zero reject + `from_bytes`).
sections.threat: H-19 unspendable/burn outputs, stealth-ECDH deanonymization, balance-equation break.

sections.name: check_tx_no_double_spend
sections.invariant: no in-tx/chain key-image reuse; every ring member exists on chain with a matching commitment, mature coinbase, and satisfied time-lock.
sections.threat: double-spend; forged-commitment inflation (CRIT-R4-1); immature/ locked-decoy anonymity leak; per-output stealth collision (5aeb27dd).

sections.name: check_tx_ring_size_and_unique_members
sections.invariant: ring length equals `effective_ring_size`, keyed (post v1.0.12) on the DETERMINISTIC `total_outputs_ever() − reorg_disconnects_total()`; members unique.
sections.threat: ring-size determinism fork in the bootstrap window (1d27d3c8); duplicate-member privacy/forgery degradation.

sections.name: check_tx_ring_signatures
sections.invariant: `input.key_image == signature.key_image` BEFORE the cache; every ring member / pseudo-output / commitment is on-curve; range proofs verify; `Σ pseudo == Σ outputs + fee` with NO identity pseudo-output.
sections.threat: C-2 key-image↔signature unbinding (supply inflation); FIX #44 identity pseudo-output balance collapse; poisoned-cache false-accept.

sections.name: SupplyState::apply_block
sections.invariant: `circulating() == total_minted − total_burned`, tracked in `u128` so supply above `u64::MAX` is preserved, and `apply_block` accumulates mint/burn with `checked_add` so totals never silently wrap.
sections.threat: an overflow wrap or lossy accumulation quietly inflating circulating supply.

sections.name: SupplyCommitment
sections.invariant: `supply_commitment` is a domain-separated hash bound to `total_minted` and `total_burned`, recomputed on every `apply_block`.
sections.threat: tampered supply figures circulating without a matching commitment.

sections.name: SupplySnapshot::from_state
sections.invariant: `from_state` yields a snapshot whose circulating/minted/burned mirror the source state and whose `proof_hash` is the domain-separated checksum — a self-consistent checksum, not an authenticated proof (issue #252).
sections.threat: a consumer mistaking the snapshot for chain-authenticated supply evidence.

sections.name: SupplySnapshot::verify
sections.threat: an attacker shipping a snapshot with an arbitrary `circulating` value that still passes the hash.

sections.name: audit_block
sections.invariant: `supply_after.circulating()` must equal `supply_before.circulating() + emission − burn%` with tolerance exactly 0, and a height mismatch is recorded as a separate issue from `supply_valid`.
sections.threat: hidden supply inflation or a wrong-height block passing the audit as valid.

sections.name: SupplyAuditResult
sections.invariant: `BlockAudit::is_valid()` (aliased as `SupplyAuditResult`) is true only when supply, fees, and emission all pass and the issues list is empty.
sections.threat: a block carrying recorded issues being treated as audited-clean.

sections.name: BlockSupplyDelta::new
sections.threat: a silent `i64` clamp masking upstream input corruption of emission/burn.

sections.name: BatchVerifier::add
sections.invariant: `add`/`add_all` only enqueue signatures and `pending_count` reflects the queue; no verification runs until `verify_all`.
sections.threat: a signature silently dropped from the batch and never verified.

sections.name: BatchVerifier::verify_all
sections.invariant: the batch result equals per-signature verification — `total == valid + invalid`, an empty batch is `all_valid`, and the parallel and single-threaded paths agree.
sections.threat: the batch path masking one invalid signature (fail-one must fail-all — that index must appear in `invalid_indices`).

sections.name: BatchVerifier::verify_single
sections.invariant: a signature verifies here iff CLSAG verify accepts it, and an identity `pseudo_output` is rejected defensively (R-29 fix).
sections.threat: R-29 — an identity `pseudo_output` collapses the `mu_c · (C_i − C')` balance term and enables inflation.

sections.name: SignatureData::cache_key
sections.invariant: `cache_key` binds message, signature, ring_data, and pseudo_output together so a cached result cannot be reused across statements.
sections.threat: cache poisoning — reusing a valid result for a different ring or pseudo-output.

sections.name: BatchVerifyResult
sections.invariant: `all_valid()` is true iff `invalid == 0`, and `success_rate() == valid / total` (1.0 on an empty batch).
sections.threat: mis-reporting a batch that contains an invalid signature as all-valid.

sections.name: ParallelTxValidator::validate_transactions
sections.invariant: `validate_transactions` returns exactly the indices failing the predicate; empty input short-circuits without touching rayon.
sections.threat: a parallel-order race dropping or misindexing an invalid transaction.

sections.name: ParallelTxValidator::filter_valid
sections.invariant: `filter_valid` keeps exactly the subset of transactions passing the predicate, in order; empty input short-circuits.
sections.threat: a parallel filter admitting an invalid transaction or dropping a valid one.

sections.name: VerificationStats::record
sections.invariant: `record` atomically increments total/hits/misses/valid/invalid, and `snapshot`/`hit_rate` read a consistent tally under concurrent updates.
sections.threat: lost or torn counter updates corrupting reported verification stats.

sections.name: verify_commitment
sections.invariant: `commit`/`verify_commitment` implement the Monero-convention Pedersen commitment `C = v·H + r·G` with an independent value generator `H` (crypto H1), so a commitment binds to exactly one `(value, blinding)` opening and is homomorphic under addition.
sections.threat: a corrupted/swapped `H` (≡ G or identity) collapses hiding+binding and lets an attacker forge openings; `verify_commitment` uses constant-time compare to deny a timing oracle.

sections.name: create_range_proof_bp_plus
sections.invariant: a proof produced for amount `v` (via BP+ `create_range_proof_bp_plus`) attests `v ∈ [0, 2^RANGE_BITS)` and is byte-reproducible for fixed inputs + RNG seed (KAT, crypto C1).
sections.threat: without a sound range proof a miner mints money via out-of-range / negative amounts (value overflow inflation).

sections.name: verify_range_proof_bp_plus
sections.invariant: verification accepts a proof ONLY against the exact commitment it was created for and rejects an empty proof or a wrong/non-canonical commitment.
sections.threat: accepting a proof against a mismatched or malformed commitment breaks binding and admits forged/inflated outputs into the chain.

sections.name: create_aggregated_range_proof_bp_plus
sections.invariant: an aggregated proof over N outputs (zero/identity padded to the next power of two) verifies iff every real committed amount is in range, for non-power-of-two N too.
sections.threat: mis-padding or an unsound aggregate lets an out-of-range output hide among valid ones, enabling inflation.

sections.name: verify_range_proofs_dispatch
sections.threat: without gating a miner includes a BP+ proof in a pre-fork block (or a stale v2 post-fork), splitting the chain between updated and legacy nodes.

sections.name: verify_coinbase_output
sections.invariant: a coinbase output must commit to the exact expected subsidy under a ZERO blinding factor, checked in constant time.
sections.threat: accepting a random-blinded or wrong-amount coinbase commitment lets a miner pay themselves more than the consensus subsidy (coinbase inflation).

sections.name: batch_verify_range_proofs
sections.invariant: `batch_verify_range_proofs` accepts a set iff every `(commitment, proof)` pair verifies, and aggregation refuses length mismatch and any batch exceeding `MAX_AGGREGATION`, with `RANGE_BITS` fixing the 64-bit proving width.
sections.threat: an oversized/mismatched batch is a DoS or padding-abuse vector, a lenient batch check lets one bad proof slip through, and a wrong bit width would prove the wrong range.

sections.name: from_bytes_checked
sections.threat: the `from_bytes_unchecked` footgun creates an "invalid but stored" wedge (passes bytewise dedup, fails validation) and an unchecked point op panics the node from the consensus path (crash DoS).

sections.name: check_bulletproof
sections.invariant: presence in the cache means "verified valid" (only positive results are inserted), and both hit and miss paths do the same `Instant::now()` + atomic bump so wall-clock time is uniform (R-28).
sections.threat: R-28 — an attacker timing RPC latency across a targeted `proof_hash` learns a cache-hit oracle ("we've seen this proof before"), leaking a hit-map of a private-mempool/RPC operator's prior work.

sections.name: cache_bulletproof
sections.invariant: only `valid == true` results are stored; negatives are dropped before insertion.
sections.threat: cache poisoning — seeding `false` for a proof that would verify, so a later honest check short-circuits to a wrong negative verdict.

sections.name: check_ring_sig
sections.invariant: presence == valid for the ring-sig map, mirroring `check_bulletproof`; a hit bumps `last_access` for LRU.
sections.threat: treating an absent entry as valid would let an unverified ring signature skip verification during block sync (note: this path lacks the R-28 uniform-timing hardening applied to `check_bulletproof`).

sections.name: cache_ring_sig
sections.invariant: only `valid == true` ring-sig results are inserted; negatives dropped, and eviction fires at `MAX_CACHE_SIZE`.
sections.threat: cache poisoning — seeding `false` for a ring signature that would verify, forcing a later wrong negative verdict.

sections.name: evict_old
sections.invariant: entry count never grows unbounded — an age pass drops >1h-old entries and a size pass drops the 10% oldest, keeping the cap; the age pass uses `checked_sub` so it cannot panic.
sections.threat: unbounded memory growth (DoS) under proof flooding, or an "overflow when subtracting duration from instant" panic when the process has been alive < 1h on a process-start-origin monotonic clock.

sections.name: proof_cache_key
sections.invariant: the key is a domain-separated BLAKE3 hash binding both the proof bytes and the commitment bytes; distinct proofs yield distinct keys, identical inputs yield identical keys.
sections.threat: a key collision would return a cached verdict for the wrong proof, accepting an unverified proof as valid.

sections.name: ring_sig_cache_key
sections.invariant: domain-separated BLAKE3 over message plus signature bytes produces the ring-sig cache key.
sections.threat: cross-domain key reuse or collision returning a cached verdict for a different (message, signature) pair.

sections.name: ring_sig_statement_cache_key
sections.invariant: the key length-prefixes and commits to every CLSAG verification input — message, signature, ring, and pseudo-output — so no two distinct statements collide.
sections.threat: a generic caller whose `message` does not already commit to the ring and pseudo-output could otherwise share a cache slot across distinct statements, accepting a ring signature verified against different inputs.

sections.name: clsag_sign
sections.invariant: a signature is producible only by the holder of the secret for `ring[real_index]`, and binds the key image `I = x·Hp(P)`, the commitment image `D`, the whole ring, the `pseudo_output`, and the message; ring size `< 2`, an out-of-range `real_index`, or a secret not matching the ring member are rejected before any curve work.
sections.threat: forged spend authorization / signing on behalf of an output the attacker does not own.

sections.name: clsag_verify
sections.invariant: the challenge chain closes back to `c1` (checked in constant time) only for a genuine signature; identity key image, identity commitment image, identity ring public keys / commitments (R-1), non-canonical response / `c1` scalars, and a zero `c1` challenge (A6-ZERO-CHALLENGE) are all rejected.
sections.threat: forged ring signature accepted → unauthorized spend / double spend; identity inputs collapse the aggregate key (R-1 small-subgroup-style forgery).

sections.name: compute_aggregate_coefficients
sections.invariant: both aggregation coefficients `mu_p` and `mu_c` are independent random-oracle evaluations that bind the *entire* public statement, including the commitment image `D` (C-1 fix).
sections.threat: C-1 key-image malleability — if `D` is unbound an attacker can attach an arbitrary key image `I'` and solve for a matching `D'`, minting distinct key images for one output → double spend / supply inflation.

sections.name: key_image
sections.invariant: the key image is the deterministic `x·Hp(x·G)`, unique per spending key and identical across messages, so it is a stable linking tag for double-spend detection.
sections.threat: colliding or malleable key images defeat double-spend dedup → double spend.

sections.name: simple_ring_sign
sections.invariant: the simple (commitment-free) ring signature authorizes only the real signer who knows the secret; ring size `< 2` and an out-of-range `real_index` are rejected.
sections.threat: unauthorized spend via a forged basic-authorization ring signature.

sections.name: simple_ring_verify
sections.invariant: rejects identity key image, any identity ring member (R-1 parity), non-canonical response scalars, and a zero `c0` challenge (A6-ZERO-CHALLENGE); closes the chain under constant-time comparison.
sections.threat: forged simple ring signature accepted → unauthorized spend.

sections.name: clsag_hash
sections.invariant: every per-round challenge is domain-tagged (`CLSAG_`) and the ring size and message are length-framed, so the transcript is unambiguous and the message is bound into the challenge.
sections.threat: cross-instance / boundary-shift collision letting a signature be replayed under a different ring or message.

sections.name: ClsagSignature::to_bytes
sections.invariant: serialization is `Result`-typed with no silent empty-`Vec` variant (H3 2026-06-30), and a serialized signature round-trips back to one that still verifies; the wire format is frozen by a golden digest.
sections.threat: H3 — a silently-empty encoding fed into hashing / cache keying (\"empty signature accidentally cached\"), or an undetected wire-format change.

sections.name: 1 module scope (design only)
sections.invariant: this module is DESIGN-ONLY; no production code path routes through it, and the practical threshold CLSAG that ships is the Reconstruct-Sign-Zeroize path in `crate::wallet::multisig::clsag_sign_multisig`.
sections.threat: mistaking this design scaffold for a shipped distributed-signing feature, over-trusting an unimplemented protocol.

sections.name: integration_status
sections.invariant: the status string is truthful — it names each subsystem's real location, marks the fully-distributed variant `NOT IMPLEMENTED`, and points at `wallet/multisig.rs::clsag_sign_multisig`, never claiming the distributed variant is `COMPLETE` (R-27 fix).
sections.threat: R-27 — an over-stated \"COMPLETE\" status misleads an auditor into believing distributed threshold signing is shipped and reviewed when it is not.

sections.name: ClsagThresholdParams
sections.invariant: a `#[allow(dead_code)]` design-only type that documents the coordinator's data flow at the type level; nothing in the shipped code constructs or consumes it.
sections.threat: treating the design scaffold as a live parameter path for distributed signing.

sections.name: _protocol_documentation
sections.invariant: a zero-body stub that carries the fully-distributed CLSAG-FROST math for `cargo doc`; explicitly NOT IMPLEMENTED and not pinned to a fragile source line (the prior note mis-cited a `clsag.rs` line).
sections.threat: a v2 implementer building from stale or incorrect math preserved here.

sections.name: generator
sections.invariant: `generator()` (Ristretto basepoint) and `generator_h()` (the hardcoded bulletproofs value generator) are fixed, independent, and never the identity, so `C = v*H + r*G` is binding.
sections.threat: a swapped/identity generator makes commitments non-binding or lets a forged `H` cancel the value term (inflation).

sections.name: hash_to_point
sections.invariant: a deterministic, domain-separated map (`from_uniform_bytes(Sha3-512("CoinCync_hash_to_point_v1"||data))`) whose output is a valid non-identity point pinned by a frozen golden vector.
sections.threat: a drifted/undomain-separated hash breaks key-image `Hp(P)` and lets two contexts collide.

sections.name: hash_to_scalar
sections.invariant: deterministic, domain-separated, and unbiased (`from_bytes_mod_order_wide` over Sha3-512), pinned by a golden vector.
sections.threat: biased or non-domain-separated challenges weaken Fiat-Shamir soundness.

sections.name: SecretScalar
sections.invariant: `from_bytes` reduces mod the group order `l` (documented reducing constructor) while `from_canonical_bytes` rejects non-canonical input; entropy is zeroized and `Debug` is redacted.
sections.threat: treating a `>= l` encoding as canonical enables scalar malleability; raw entropy in a crash dump enables cold-boot key recovery.

sections.name: PublicPoint
sections.invariant: every decode path (`from_bytes`, serde, Borsh) accepts only canonical, on-curve Ristretto encodings and round-trips exactly; identity is representable but never smuggled in as a valid key.
sections.threat: small-subgroup / non-canonical / identity-point decode enables point-forgery and equality-confusion attacks.

sections.name: KeyImage
sections.invariant: `I = x*Hp(P)` with `P = x*G`, deterministic per secret and pinned to the Monero construction by a golden vector; decode rejects non-curve bytes.
sections.threat: zero/identity or non-canonical key images enable double-spend / key-image forgery (Monero 2017 zero-key-image class).

sections.name: Commitment
sections.invariant: `C = v*H + r*G` (Monero convention) is binding and additively homomorphic (`commit(v1,b1)+commit(v2,b2) == commit(v1+v2,b1+b2)`); `from_bytes` rejects invalid points.
sections.threat: a non-homomorphic or non-binding commitment breaks the balance equation and enables value inflation.

sections.name: create_balance_proof
sections.invariant: the Schnorr nonce `k` and the blinding difference `d = r - r'` never outlive their use — both are wiped (R-18/R-19), so no secret material is left on the stack; refuses to prove when `value < threshold`.
sections.threat: nonce leakage recovers the blinding/private key (BIP-340 "any leakage of k is fatal"; Sony PS3 / MtGox ECDSA nonce disasters).

sections.name: verify_balance_proof
sections.invariant: accepts iff the Schnorr blinding- difference proof AND the range proof on `C'` both hold; Schnorr R is decoded canonically and non-identity, `s` is a canonical scalar (no mod-order reduction), and the final compare is constant-time (C11-FIX).
sections.threat: forged/tampered commitment, non-canonical or identity R nonce, or a timing side-channel accepting a value below threshold (SEC 2026-09-07).

sections.name: create_ownership_proof
sections.invariant: rejects a secret that does not match the stealth address; the challenge binds `tx_hash`, `output_index`, stealth address and `message`.
sections.threat: replay of the bearer token (M1 — freshness rests entirely on a verifier-chosen `message`), or attempting to prove under a wrong key.

sections.name: verify_ownership_proof
sections.invariant: the Schnorr identity `s*G == R + c*P` holds only if the prover knows the one-time secret; R must be non-identity; `s` canonically decoded; compare is constant-time (C11-FIX).
sections.threat: a tampered message (challenge changes) or an identity R nonce (SEC 2026-09-07) forging ownership.

sections.name: create_sum_proof
sections.invariant: the total is a checked (no-overflow) sum, output refs are unique, the height range is well-ordered, and the transcript challenge binds every field.
sections.threat: R-20 — `sum_blinding` (r_sum) is transmitted in cleartext, so a duplicate output or silent overflow could let a prover misstate a total or double-count an output.

sections.name: verify_sum_proof
sections.invariant: accepts iff `sum(C_i) == commit(claimed_total, r_sum)` (homomorphic opening) AND the transcript is valid (version, ordered height range, unique refs, matching challenge); constant-time compare.
sections.threat: a tampered claimed total, mismatched/reordered commitments, or duplicate output refs inflating the sum.

sections.name: create_source_proof
sections.invariant: rejects unless `P = x*G` AND the key image `I = x*H_p(P)` both derive from the given secret; the challenge binds R1, R2, P, I and `message`.
sections.threat: producing a source proof for a key image not derived from the prover's own key, or an M1 replay of the bearer token.

sections.name: verify_source_proof
sections.invariant: the dual-base checks `s*G + c*P == R1` AND `s*H_p(P) + c*I == R2` are both constant-time and ANDed WITHOUT short-circuit (R-21), proving one secret `x` underlies both P and I; R1/R2 must be non-identity.
sections.threat: a tampered message, an identity R1/R2 nonce, or a timing leak distinguishing which check failed (R-21 / SEC 2026-09-07).

sections.name: verify_balance_proof_anchored
sections.invariant: returns `Valid` only when the crypto holds AND the proof's `original_commitment` equals a `ChainAnchor` commitment the verifier resolved from its own trusted chain view.
sections.threat: H1 (issues #252/#253) — a prover produces a sound range proof over a commitment they invented; unanchored acceptance is not a sound trust decision. Forgery (`CryptoInvalid`) is distinguished from `AnchorMismatch`.

sections.name: verify_ownership_proof_anchored
sections.invariant: returns `Valid` only when the crypto holds AND the proof's output ref AND stealth address both equal the trusted on-chain anchor.
sections.threat: H1 (#252/#253) — a valid proof for a key the prover controls but that was never the on-chain stealth address of that output, or a wrong output ref.

sections.name: verify_sum_proof_anchored
sections.invariant: every output ref must uniquely resolve to an anchor whose height falls in the declared range and whose commitment is a valid curve point, before the homomorphic sum is checked against those anchors.
sections.threat: H1 (#252/#253) — a cryptographically sound sum over outputs never mined, a missing/duplicate ref, or an out-of-range height.

sections.name: verify_source_proof_anchored
sections.invariant: returns `Valid` only if the crypto holds AND the key image is actually in the chain's spent set.
sections.threat: H1 (#252/#253) — the prover proved they *could* generate a key image, not that a real spend on chain ever used it.

sections.name: verify_internal_consistency
sections.invariant: the deprecated unanchored `verify()` entry point hard-fails to force callers onto an anchored verifier; `verify_internal_consistency` performs only the offline crypto check and errors for Sum (needs on-chain commitments); expiry is advisory only.
sections.threat: H1/H2 — treating unanchored consistency as a trust decision, or relying on unauthenticated `expires_at` container metadata as a control.

sections.name: generate_with
sections.invariant: `generate`/`generate_with` draw 64 CSPRNG bytes and reduce mod the ed25519 group order, so every produced offset is a canonical scalar.
sections.threat: a non-canonical or biased offset would fail decode downstream or leak signing-key structure.

sections.name: aggregate
sections.invariant: `KernelOffset::aggregate` is scalar addition mod l — commutative and equal to the sum of the two operand scalars — returning `None` on any non-canonical operand.
sections.threat: order-dependent or non-canonical aggregation would make block-level offset totals irreproducible across nodes, splitting consensus.

sections.name: add_offset
sections.invariant: folding per-tx offsets onto a running `AggregateOffset` is associative/commutative, so the block aggregate is independent of tx ordering (`ZERO` is the identity element).
sections.threat: an order-sensitive fold yields a different on-chain aggregate offset per node, breaking block validation agreement.

sections.name: verify_against
sections.invariant: Schnorr verification accepts `(R,s)` iff it was signed by the holder of the unblinded excess given the published offset, re-adding `offset·G`; identity excess and identity `R` are rejected (SEC 2026-09-07 defense-in-depth).
sections.threat: accepting an identity point or a wrong-offset signature would let a peer forge a kernel or unblind another's excess, defeating the unlinkability layer.

sections.name: as_scalar
sections.invariant: decoding an offset/aggregate scalar uses `from_canonical_bytes` and returns `None` on non-canonical encodings, so no operation proceeds on malleable input.
sections.threat: accepting non-canonical scalar bytes enables encoding malleability of published offsets.

sections.name: to_point
sections.invariant: `AggregateOffset::to_point` maps the aggregate scalar to `aggregate·G` for verifiers to add to the aggregate kernel excess, `None` on non-canonical bytes.
sections.threat: a wrong aggregate point would make block-level excess verification reject valid blocks or accept invalid ones.

sections.name: spark_commit
sections.invariant: `C = v*G + s*H + r*K` is deterministic in `(v, s, r)` over three independent nothing-up-my-sleeve generators, so the commitment is binding.
sections.threat: a non-deterministic or non-binding commitment lets a coin open to two different `(v, s, r)` (inflation).

sections.name: spark_pubkey
sections.invariant: `P = C - v*G - r*K` equals `s*H`, the residue on the serial generator, so the prover's Schnorr key is exactly the discrete log of the real opening.
sections.threat: a mis-derived residue lets a prover ring-sign against a key it does not own.

sections.name: spark_serial_tag
sections.invariant: `T = s*G` is deterministic and globally unique per coin, so double-spends collide on `T` without revealing `s`.
sections.threat: a forgeable or non-unique tag defeats double-spend detection or deanonymizes the serial.

sections.name: prove_spark_spend
sections.invariant: an honest prover holding the real opening at any ring position `l` (n = 1, 2, 3, 5) produces an AOS ring-signature proof the verifier accepts (completeness).
sections.threat: a position-dependent gap would break honest spends or leak `l`.

sections.name: verify_spark_spend
sections.invariant: the ring/serial-tag equations must close and every peer scalar decodes canonically through `PeerScalar` (rejecting non-canonical `from_bytes_mod_order` malleability, Monero non-canonical-scalar class); the n=1 degenerate ring is checked as a plain Schnorr proof.
sections.threat: any tampered field, wrong message, or wrong pubkey vector must be rejected — else forged spends / inflation.

sections.name: batch_verify_sparks
sections.invariant: the batch agrees exactly with the per-proof `verify_spark_spend` — an all-valid batch (and the empty batch) passes, and one tampered proof rejects the whole batch.
sections.threat: crypto M1 — a batch verifier that accepts a proof the single verifier rejects is an inflation surface.

sections.name: build_anon_set
sections.invariant: returns a set that always contains the real index, is clamped to `[SPARK_ANON_SET_MIN, SPARK_ANON_SET_MAX]`, and errors (never panics or silently shrinks) when the pool is below `SPARK_ANON_SET_MIN`; decoys drawn from `OsRng` (AUDIT 2026-07-02).
sections.threat: a smaller-than-minimum set silently weakens anonymity; correlated decoy draws deanonymize the spender.

sections.name: derive_memo_key
sections.invariant: the AEAD key is `BLAKE3("COINCYNC_MEMO_v1" ‖ shared_point)`, domain-separated from every other key derived from the same ECDH secret.
sections.threat: cross-protocol key reuse (the same shared point deriving colliding keys for different uses).

sections.name: encrypt_memo
sections.invariant: a fresh random 12-byte nonce is drawn per encryption and written to the wire, and the ECDH `shared_point`, its bytes, and the AEAD key are all zeroized before return (R-16 / R-17 / R-80).
sections.threat: ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce reuse — deriving the nonce from the shared point made two calls with the same `(tx_secret, view_pub)` reuse `(key, nonce)`, letting an attacker XOR ciphertexts to recover plaintext and forge the Poly1305 MAC; plus key/secret heap residue.

sections.name: MAX_MEMO_SIZE
sections.invariant: an empty memo returns empty, and a memo over `MAX_MEMO_SIZE` (256) bytes is rejected before any crypto runs.
sections.threat: unbounded plaintext / oversized-memo resource abuse.

sections.name: decrypt_memo
sections.invariant: the nonce is read from the wire, the key is re-derived from `view_secret·tx_public` ECDH, and the AEAD key is zeroized on both success and failure paths (R-16 / R-17 / R-80).
sections.threat: shared-secret / key residue on the stack after decrypt.

sections.name: 5 AEAD authentication
sections.invariant: decryption of a wrong-key, truncated, or bit-flipped memo fails via the Poly1305 tag rather than returning forged plaintext.
sections.threat: ciphertext malleability / integrity bypass.

sections.name: 6 curve point validation
sections.invariant: a non-curve recipient view key (encrypt) or tx public key (decrypt) is rejected before the ECDH multiply.
sections.threat: invalid-point / small-subgroup attacks against the ECDH shared secret.

sections.name: verify_cut_through
sections.invariant: a cut-through pair matches only if both commitments decompress to valid Ristretto points AND those points are equal — a point-equality check, never a byte compare.
sections.threat: two distinct byte encodings of the same point (or undecodable bytes) would falsely pass/fail a byte compare, pruning an output that was never actually spent.

sections.name: compute_kernel_excess
sections.invariant: excess = `(Σ r_out − Σ r_in) · G` on the base generator, so a balanced blinding set yields identity and the excess equals the manual sum.
sections.threat: a miscomputed excess would make a balanced transaction fail (or an unbalanced one pass) kernel-set verification.

sections.name: verify_kernel_set
sections.invariant: the pruned kernel set is valid only when `Σ excess_points == (Σ fees) · H` on the value generator, every excess decompresses, and the fee sum does not overflow.
sections.threat: value inflation (excess encoding more than the declared fee) or a stray `G` blinding component would let a pruned set hide unbalanced value.

sections.name: MwKernel::excess_point
sections.threat: a kernel with non-canonical excess can survive gossip+storage yet fail aggregation on some nodes, risking a partition.

sections.name: MwKernel::validate
sections.threat: per-caller "must call excess_point() first" discipline is easy to forget, admitting an unvalidated kernel into a consensus path.

sections.name: CutThroughEngine::register_spend
sections.invariant: a candidate is enqueued only when its spent/input commitments actually cut-through-match (`verify_cut_through`), never on a bare commitment pair.
sections.threat: registering a non-matching pair would schedule pruning of an output that was never spent.

sections.name: CutThroughEngine::process
sections.invariant: a candidate is pruned only once `current_height >= spent_at + MW_CUTTHROUGH_DEPTH`, keeping the kernel behind; others stay pending.
sections.threat: pruning before the reorg-protection depth would delete an output/input pair that a reorg could still need, corrupting the UTXO set.

sections.name: ProofTask
sections.invariant: a task carries the commitment bytes and raw proof bytes intact, and `cache_key` is a pure function of both so identical proofs hit the same cache slot.
sections.threat: a mismatched or mutable cache key would let a poisoned/aliased result stand in for a different proof.

sections.name: verify_all
sections.invariant: the parallel batch result agrees byte-for-byte with the per-proof (`verify_single`) ground truth and reports exactly the invalid indices; it also CONSUMES the pending queue (R-30) so a second call sees an empty set rather than silently re-reporting success.
sections.threat: a batch that accepted a proof the single verifier rejects (crypto M2) would let an inflating output pass block validation; the R-30 side effect could mask an unverified re-submission.

sections.name: verify_single
sections.invariant: a proof is valid only if its range proof parses AND its commitment passes checked Ristretto decode (A6-COMMITMENT) AND the range proof verifies against that commitment.
sections.threat: unchecked point decode would accept non-Ristretto bytes, breaking the homomorphic balance equation and enabling inflation.

sections.name: ParallelVerifyResult
sections.invariant: `all_valid()` is true iff `invalid == 0`, and `invalid_indices` lists precisely the failing positions.
sections.threat: an all-valid verdict that hid a failing proof would admit an invalid output into a block.

sections.name: verify_block_proofs
sections.invariant: every (tx_hash, idx, commitment, proof) output in a block is verified through the same parallel engine and gated on the aggregate result.
sections.threat: an unverified block output would let an inflating tx confirm.

sections.name: AggregatedProofVerifier
sections.invariant: a single aggregated proof verifies only when a proof is set, the commitment list is non-empty, and every commitment passes checked decode (A6-COMMITMENT) before `verify_range_proofs`.
sections.threat: accepting an empty set or a non-canonical commitment would forge a balanced-looking aggregate.

sections.name: VerifierStats
sections.invariant: total-verified / cache-hit / time counters are monotonic atomic accumulators, correct under the parallel `par_iter` path.
sections.threat: torn or racy counters would corrupt operational telemetry, not consensus.

sections.name: PeerScalar::decode
sections.invariant: a `PeerScalar` is constructible only from canonical curve25519 bytes (via `from_canonical_bytes`); non-canonical encodings are rejected with a typed error.
sections.threat: `from_bytes_mod_order` silently reduces distinct byte strings to the same scalar, letting an attacker mint two txids/cache-keys for one spend — txid-confusion double-spend or cache poisoning.

sections.name: PeerPoint::decode
sections.invariant: a `PeerPoint` decodes only from bytes that form a valid Ristretto element (identity admitted here).
sections.threat: `CompressedRistretto` accepts arbitrary bytes at construction; skipping the decompress check would admit non-points into curve math.

sections.name: PeerPoint::decode_non_identity
sections.invariant: the default point decoder also rejects the identity element (a valid Ristretto encoding).
sections.threat: an identity public key / commitment / challenge point breaks CLSAG distinguishability, ECDH secrecy, and Pedersen balance (forgery).

sections.name: PeerScalar
sections.threat: a raw-bytes serde/borsh fallback would let a non-canonical scalar re-enter through a container field, regressing §1 structurally.

sections.name: PeerPoint
sections.threat: a raw-bytes fallback would admit identity/non-Ristretto points into any struct holding a `PeerPoint`.

sections.name: PeerScalar
sections.threat: a new proof struct silently reverting to `[u8; 32]` fields would reopen the non-canonical-input class the wrapper was built to close.

sections.name: RingSelectionPool
sections.invariant: the pool deduplicates candidates by full public key, so no output can appear twice in one anonymity set.
sections.threat: repeated pool entries give one output multiple inclusion chances, shrinking the effective anonymity set and biasing the ring.

sections.name: RingSelectionConfig
sections.invariant: decoy eligibility is bounded by a configured `[min_decoy_age, max_decoy_age]` window with a default ring size of 11.
sections.threat: an unbounded/ancient decoy window or a tiny ring weakens the privacy set an observer must defeat.

sections.name: select_decoys
sections.invariant: `ring_size >= 2` is enforced before `decoy_count = ring_size - 1`, and decoys are sampled uniformly from the already policy-shaped pool without re-imposing an age bias.
sections.threat: T3F1 — `ring_size = 0` underflows `ring_size - 1` to `usize::MAX` in release wrapping arithmetic; a second age bias here would re-expose the real spend the upstream gamma policy hid.

sections.name: is_eligible_decoy
sections.invariant: BUG-5 — a real output younger than `min_decoy_age` relaxes `effective_min_age` so it is not the sole young ring member; the real output is never eligible as its own decoy; ages stay within the configured window.
sections.threat: BUG-5 — a lone young real member is trivially deanonymized by age analysis (R-22 emits the loud advisory for this).

sections.name: verify_ring_quality
sections.invariant: per-ring structural audit flags a real output that is a statistical age outlier and any duplicate commitment; distribution conformance is deliberately not judged from one ring.
sections.threat: an age-outlier real member or a duplicated commitment identifies the real spend to a chain analyst.

sections.name: RingSelectionStats
sections.invariant: A4-CR-04 — the age-bucket histogram handles `age == 0` explicitly (no `log2(0) = -inf`) and clamps the bucket to 9, so no out-of-bounds index or UB on cast to `usize`.
sections.threat: A4-CR-04 — an `age == 0` decoy casting `-inf` to `usize` corrupts the stats array / triggers undefined behavior.

sections.name: with_ring_size
sections.invariant: the `RingSelector` constructors bind a ring-size policy to `RingSelectionConfig` defaults, so a caller-chosen ring size still inherits the audited age bounds; an invalid size is caught only at `select_decoys` (§3), never silently accepted here.
sections.threat: a constructor that dropped the default age bounds would let an under-constrained selector assemble low-anonymity rings.

sections.name: ct_eq
sections.invariant: byte-equality via the `subtle` crate (CR-002), running in time independent of where the first difference lies; unequal lengths return false.
sections.threat: a data-dependent early-exit comparison leaks MAC/hash/secret bytes through timing.

sections.name: ct_cmp
sections.invariant: returns the correct three-way `Ordering` for equal-length inputs with no secret-dependent branch; the `1 + gt - lt` index maps the three reachable (gt,lt) states to {Less,Equal,Greater} without a clamp (R-26 fix of the buggy `2*gt+(1-lt)` formula; R-25 documents the hand-rolled slice compare).
sections.threat: an off-by-one index or a timing-variable compare corrupts canonicity ordering (used by `PeerScalar::decode`) or leaks bytes.

sections.name: ct_select_u8
sections.invariant: selection is by arithmetic mask, not a branch — `true` yields `a`, `false` yields `b`, in constant time.
sections.threat: a branch on the condition bit leaks which secret operand was chosen.

sections.name: ct_copy_if
sections.invariant: conditionally copies `src` into `dst` via an arithmetic mask (no if/else), constant time regardless of the condition.
sections.threat: a branchy copy leaks whether the guarded write happened.

sections.name: is_zero
sections.invariant: reports all-zero by OR-accumulating every byte, so timing is independent of contents; empty input is zero.
sections.threat: an early-exit zero check leaks the position of the first nonzero byte of a secret.

sections.name: secure_random
sections.invariant: output is drawn from `OsRng` OS entropy, fills the whole buffer, and is non-zero / distinct across draws.
sections.threat: a short-filled or predictable buffer yields guessable keys/nonces.

sections.name: secure_zero
sections.invariant: sensitive buffers are wiped (with a compiler fence for `secure_zero`) and the secure wrappers zeroize on drop; Debug never prints contents.
sections.threat: leftover key material in freed memory is recoverable by a later read or a crash dump.

sections.name: verify_hash
sections.invariant: authentication tags are compared with the constant-time `ct_eq`, never `==`.
sections.threat: a timing-variable tag compare enables a byte-by-byte MAC forgery.

sections.name: generate_stealth_address_checked_ext
sections.invariant: the one-time key is `P = H(r·view_pub ‖ idx)·G + spend_pub`; main addresses publish `R = r·G` and subaddresses publish `R = r·D_i` so `a·R` matches the recipient's published view key, keeping every output detectable and spendable.
sections.threat: wrong tx-pubkey form yields unspendable outputs or cross-output address reuse / linkage.

sections.name: is_output_ours
sections.invariant: ownership detection validates every curve point, computes `a·R` ECDH, compares in constant time, and zeroizes the shared-secret buffer (R-7 class).
sections.threat: timing side-channel leaking which outputs are ours, plus invalid-point / small-subgroup attacks on malformed inputs.

sections.name: owns
sections.threat: R-8 latency distinguisher ("was that output well-formed?") and forged-tx-public ownership claims.

sections.name: compute_one_time_secret
sections.invariant: the spend key `x = H(shared ‖ idx) + spend_secret` satisfies `P = x·G`; the ECDH `scalar_input` buffer is zeroized after derivation.
sections.threat: derivation mismatch producing unspendable outputs, or ECDH secret residue on the heap.

sections.name: subaddress_scalar
sections.invariant: `m = hash_domain("COINCYNC_SUBADDR_v1", view_secret ‖ account_le ‖ index_le)` is the single, account-aware, domain-separated source of truth shared by wallet and audit derivation, and the raw-view_secret input buffer is zeroized before drop (R-10, R-11, #26).
sections.threat: audit vs wallet derivation divergence so the audit key cannot scan wallet subaddresses (#26); unversioned-domain collisions (R-11); view_secret heap residue (R-10).

sections.name: coinbase_stealth_address
sections.invariant: `tx_secret = H(miner_secret ‖ height)` is unique per height and unpredictable to outsiders, and the buffer holding `miner_secret` is zeroized.
sections.threat: precomputable `H(height)` coinbase linkage (anyone with the view key links all future coinbases) and stealth_index collisions breaking maturity validation.

sections.name: to_scanner
sections.threat: R-9 audit blind spot (outputs to subaddresses go undetected) and the #26 multi-account gap.

sections.name: generate_stealth_outputs
sections.threat: index wraparound produces duplicate output indices, breaking one-time-key uniqueness.

sections.name: from_bytes_checked
sections.threat: invalid-point attacks feeding non-curve bytes into downstream ECDH.

sections.name: derive
sections.invariant: `key_data = H("COINCYNC_VIEWKEY_v2", view_secret‖epoch)` is deterministic in the inputs and distinct across epochs; R-12 — the scratch buffer holding `view_secret` is zeroized after hashing.
sections.threat: R-12 — un-wiped `view_secret` bytes linger in freed allocator memory; R-13 — the deterministic watermark links two exported keys of one origin.

sections.name: ViewKeyScope
sections.invariant: the scope defines the exact scanning envelope of a view key — EpochOnly, TimeRange, AmountCapped, SingleUse — and authorization must respect it.
sections.threat: a scope that authorizes beyond its bound lets a view key scan epochs or amounts it was never granted.

sections.name: is_valid_for_epoch
sections.invariant: M2 — the read-only check gates only the stateless EpochOnly / TimeRange scopes and fails closed (returns `false`) for the stateful AmountCapped / SingleUse variants.
sections.threat: M2 — a read-only gate that authorized a budgeted key would never consume the budget, granting unlimited scans.

sections.name: authorize_scan
sections.invariant: R-14 — the stateful authorize+consume path decrements the AmountCapped budget (denying once exhausted) and fires SingleUse exactly once; an epoch mismatch is rejected without consuming state.
sections.threat: R-14 — scanning past the cap or reusing a SingleUse key escalates a scoped view key into an unbounded scanner.

sections.name: ViewKey
sections.invariant: A6-VIEWKEY — `key_data` is excluded from Serialize, redacted in Debug, and zeroed on drop (no `zeroize(skip)` on the secret).
sections.threat: A6-VIEWKEY — `key_data` leaking into logs, JSON, or RPC hands an attacker scan authority; the historical `zeroize(skip)` bug left it un-wiped.

sections.name: Deserialize
sections.invariant: R-15 — a deserialized ViewKey carries the all-`0xEE` sentinel `key_data` (never usable key bytes) so re-derivation is mandatory, while non-secret metadata round-trips and consumption state resets.
sections.threat: R-15 — a caller that skipped re-derivation would silently scan with wrong-but-plausible key material; the sentinel makes that failure loud.

sections.name: insert
sections.invariant: blocks are stored by hash only; the height→hash index uses big-endian keys so lexicographic order equals numeric order and `last()` returns the true tip; a non-8-byte height key surfaces as `DatabaseError`, never a silent height-0 tip (M-1: `insert` no longer touches the height index).
sections.threat: a fork block overwriting the main-chain height index; corruption masquerading as a legitimate genesis tip.

sections.name: set_height_hash
sections.invariant: `remove_heights_above` removes EVERY stale height above the cutoff exactly once by collecting keys under the iterator first, THEN deleting — no skip, no duplicate.
sections.threat: R-39 — the pre-fix mutate-during-iteration (delete_cf inside a live `range(..)` scan) skipped/duplicated keys, leaving stale height→hash mappings that survived a reorg (the 2026-06-04 testnet cascade).

sections.name: delete
sections.invariant: removing a block for a reorg deletes the block body AND its height entry in ONE transaction, and only clears the height entry when it points at THIS block's hash; returns the prior block.
sections.threat: C12 — a crash between two separate removes leaving an orphaned height mapping or block body.

sections.name: get_range
sections.invariant: `get_range` is inclusive on both bounds and silently skips missing heights; `is_empty` tracks the `blocks` tree specifically, while `has_any_chain_data` is true if ANY block-related tree is non-empty (the fresh-vs-legacy DB signal for schema stamping).
sections.threat: mis-classifying a legacy DB as fresh and auto-stamping it.

sections.name: store_pruned_header
sections.invariant: `store_pruned_and_remove` writes the compact header AND removes the full block body in ONE WriteBatch (both or neither); the height index is preserved so the pruned header stays locatable.
sections.threat: the two-call form crash-windows to a header-stored-but-body-still-present state that wastes disk indefinitely (the pruning loop never revisits the height).

sections.name: DbConfig
sections.invariant: every preset (fast_sync/low_memory/maximum_safety/auto/default) opens a working store; the Windows memory probe reports true host RAM or falls back to 4096 MB, never silently mis-sizing the cache.
sections.threat: R-33 — the pre-fix empty Windows branch gave every host the 4-8 GB config (OOM on small boxes, undersized cache on large ones).

sections.name: verify_or_stamp_schema_version
sections.invariant: a fresh DB is stamped; a matching version proceeds; missing-stamp-with-blocks, wrong-length, and future (stored > expected) all refuse to open; older runs a registered migration or fails.
sections.threat: silently mutating a mis-versioned DB (the "v1.1 upgrade bricked the testnet DB" failure mode).

sections.name: migrate_schema_v1_to_v2
sections.invariant: the state rewrite (supply u64→u128) and the v2 stamp share ONE synchronous batch — a failed migration leaves both the v1 record and the v1 stamp unchanged; an empty DB advances without inventing chain state.
sections.threat: a half-migrated DB stamped v2 over incomplete state → unloadable or wrong supply.

sections.name: migrate_legacy_db_to_v1
sections.invariant: a legacy (unstamped) DB is stamped v1 ONLY after the on-disk block-0 hash matches the caller-supplied expected genesis; an empty DB is rejected; the call is idempotent when already stamped; a failed migration writes no stamp.
sections.threat: stamping a wrong-network / forked / corrupt DB as canonical.

sections.name: apply_reorg_atomic
sections.invariant: output-index removals+additions, height sets, height removals, chain state, and tx-index add/remove all land in ONE fsync-durable transaction or none; a re-mined output (in BOTH removals and additions) is re-inserted with the NEW chain's entry; oldest-wins holds for a non-removed shared address.
sections.threat: R-68 — dropping a re-mined output_index entry makes ring-member lookups reject valid txs; a crash mid-reorg leaving a hybrid tip.

sections.name: commit_block_atomic
sections.invariant: the extend-path output-index + height→hash + chain state + tx-index commit atomically; the height index can never outrun committed state on reopen; oldest-wins on the output index.
sections.threat: a crash between the pre-fix five separate writes → height index ahead of state / orphaned output-index entries.

sections.name: index_tx
sections.invariant: the 12-byte height‖idx little-endian encoding round-trips; flush surfaces Ok on a healthy DB and best-effort never panics.
sections.threat: a mis-encoded tx index silently returns the wrong (height, idx).

sections.name: schema_version
sections.invariant: `schema_version` reads back the stamp of a successfully-opened DB; borsh (de)serialize map errors to a typed `SerializationError`; `stats` reports the nominal 8-field tree count (R-35, not the physical CF count).

sections.name: Db::open_path
sections.invariant: the monotonic counter is restored only from a canonical 8-byte value (any other length refuses to open, never silently truncates — R-49); each CF lazily gets its own CAS mutex (R-53); generate_id is strictly increasing.
sections.threat: R-49 — a truncated counter emits a non-monotonic id that collides a previously-issued one.

sections.name: Tree::insert
sections.invariant: sled `insert`/`remove` return the prior value; single-key writes are atomic at the CF level.
sections.threat: the get-then-put window is NOT a transaction — a concurrent writer makes the returned "old value" stale; current callers either ignore it or hold an external write lock.

sections.name: Tree::compare_and_swap
sections.invariant: CAS is a mutex-serialized read-then-conditional-write — expected-matches sets the new value, mismatch returns the current value untouched; this is the key-image double-spend guard (create-if-absent).
sections.threat: TOCTOU double-spend — without the per-CF lock two threads both see "unspent" and both mark spent; exactly one CAS must win.

sections.name: Tree::iter
sections.invariant: forward/reverse/`last` ordering is correct; `scan_prefix` excludes the next sibling via the computed exclusive `upper_bound`; range honors inclusive/exclusive bounds.
sections.threat: R-54 — a full-tree `.iter()` eagerly materializes every entry (OOM at mainnet UTXO scale); callers must bound with range/scan_prefix.

sections.name: transaction
sections.invariant: all trees commit or none (single RocksDB `WriteBatch`); the WAL is fsync'd before return (`set_sync(true)`, R-56); a closure `Err` aborts with zero mutation; TxTree reads see committed state, NOT staged writes.
sections.threat: R-56 — a non-synced consensus batch could disappear on power loss between commit and the next WAL sync; H4 — the prior `*mut RocksBatch` aliased mutably (UB).

sections.name: Tree::len
sections.invariant: len/is_empty track the CF contents; clear empties it.
sections.threat: R-51 — `len()` is O(N) (a multi-second scan on the UTXO tree); R-52 — `clear()` is NOT atomic vs a concurrent writer.

sections.name: IVec
sections.invariant: wraps `Box<[u8]>` so `as_ref()` resolves to a single `&[u8]` impl (sled parity); all conversions round-trip.

sections.name: get_state
sections.invariant: `total_supply` is `u128` (MAX_SUPPLY 10^20 exceeds `u64::MAX`); `get_state` decodes ONLY the current layout — the schema stamp, not trial decoding, selects the format, so a legacy (u64-supply) record is REJECTED by `get_state` and read only by the registered v1→v2 migration path.
