sections.threat: the old u64 aggregate overflowed and panicked `checked_add` at ~18.4M CYNC (height ~408k); a mis-stamped DB selecting the wrong record layout by luck.

sections.name: get_genesis_hash
sections.invariant: genesis hash starts unset and round-trips through set/get; overwrite is honored.
sections.threat: a missing/wrong genesis identifier defeating the network-match gate.

sections.name: add_checkpoint
sections.invariant: checkpoints are BE-keyed so iteration yields numeric-sorted heights (correct above 255); a malformed (non-8-byte) checkpoint key surfaces as `DatabaseError`, never a silent coercion to height 0.
sections.threat: A6 — a corrupted checkpoint attributed to genesis and then trusted by reorg validation.

sections.name: store_undo
sections.invariant: undo data is BE-keyed; `prune_undo` removes every entry strictly below `keep_from_height` and returns the count; DB read errors and malformed keys propagate rather than being silently dropped.
sections.threat: A6-DB-CORRUPT — a silently-coerced height-0 key queuing every genesis-height entry for deletion, or corrupt entries never cleaned → incomplete reorgs.

sections.name: put
sections.invariant: put/delete structurally REFUSE the reserved keys `chain_state` and `genesis_hash` (typed setters only); reads pass through for debugging.
sections.threat: R-41 — a raw write/delete to a reserved key corrupting the persisted `ChainStateData`/genesis, wedging the DB on next open (or making the loader treat it as a fresh install and wipe the chain).

sections.name: add_output
sections.invariant: the two UTXO-visible writes (`outputs` + `utxo_by_height`) land in ONE atomic batch, so a durable output is always reachable by its height prefix and vice-versa; the `height_counts` bump runs post-commit (at worst under-by-one on crash — a stat drift, never a UTXO-visibility bug, and it logs loudly).
sections.threat: R-43 — the pre-fix three sequential writes could crash mid-way, hiding an output from the height scan or skewing ring-decoy distribution.

sections.name: spend_output
sections.invariant: a single-key `compare_and_swap` on the key image is the atomic double-spend gate (exactly one caller wins); the 3-tree cleanup (`outputs` + `utxo_by_height` + `height_counts`, counter removed at zero) runs in ONE transaction after the CAS.
sections.threat: TOCTOU double-spend if check-then-set weren't atomic; if the cleanup tx fails the CAS still stands, so the chain stays consensus-consistent (key image spent) with only a stale entry.

sections.name: is_spent
sections.invariant: `is_spent` reflects the key image set; `mark_key_image` records a key image WITHOUT removing a UTXO (for checkpoint persistence) and is idempotent; no accidental cross-marking.
sections.threat: a mismarked/unmarked key image admitting a double-spend or dropping a valid spend.

sections.name: get_output
sections.invariant: `get_outputs_at_height` uses the BE-keyed `utxo_by_height` prefix scan (O(k), not a full table scan) and agrees with `get_height_count`; a malformed (non-8-byte) counter is treated as 0 with a loud corruption log, never silently overwriting the true count.
sections.threat: BUG-20 — LE height keys sorting wrong above 255; a corrupt counter destroying the true count.

sections.name: clear
sections.invariant: empties the `outputs`, `key_images`, and `height_counts` trees so counts/height lookups all read zero afterward.
sections.threat: a partial reset leaving phantom UTXOs or spent markers.

sections.name: EmissionPhase
sections.invariant: exactly three display phases (Distribution / Mature / Tail), each mapping to a stable string.
sections.threat: an explorer/label drift misreporting monetary regime.

sections.name: emission_phase
sections.invariant: classifies by the estimated reward at height — Tail at ≤ `TAIL_EMISSION`, Mature at ≤ 10·COIN, else Distribution; always consistent with the reward the estimate produces.
sections.threat: a phase label inconsistent with the actual subsidy.

sections.name: base_reward_from_supply
sections.invariant: `reward = max(TAIL_EMISSION, (cap − supply)/EMISSION_DIVISOR)`; the u128 `saturating_sub` means supply ≥ cap yields the tail floor, never a wrap or a sub-tail value.
sections.threat: over-emission above the 100M asymptote, or an underflow at/above the cap dropping reward below the perpetual 0.6 CYNC floor.

sections.name: base_reward
sections.invariant: reward is monotone non-increasing in height, starts at 50 CYNC at height 0, and never panics for any `u64` height.
sections.threat: overflow/panic on a large RPC-supplied height.

sections.name: estimate_supply_at_height
sections.invariant: result never exceeds `cap_atomic` (`.min(cap)`), stays within ~0.1% of a block-by-block integration, and the tail fast-path returns in O(1) once the asymptotic curve drops below `TAIL_EMISSION`.
sections.threat: `base_reward(u64::MAX)` DoS — a ~1.8e15-iteration loop if a height is routed in unbounded (fixed 2026-06-03).

sections.name: estimate_reward_at_height
sections.invariant: mirrors the §3 formula on the §5 supply estimate and is likewise floored at `TAIL_EMISSION`; used only for phase classification.
sections.threat: a phase estimate diverging from the reward formula.

sections.name: 1 Public re export surface
sections.invariant: the emission API exposed to the rest of the crate is exactly `curve::{base_reward, base_reward_from_supply, block_reward, emission_phase, EmissionPhase}` and `supply::{ calculate_supply_commitment, SupplyStats}`; the `kani_proofs` sibling is `cfg(kani)`-only so proof harnesses never touch the lockfile-locked `curve.rs`.
sections.threat: an unintended symbol or a proof-harness edit disturbing the consensus-hash-locked curve module.

sections.name: calculate_block_reward
sections.invariant: the height→`Amount` subsidy accessor delegates to `curve::base_reward(height)` and returns bit-identical results (thin inline wrapper); consensus-critical paths use `base_reward_from_supply` with real chain state instead.
sections.threat: the block template / explorer helper drifting from the canonical reward curve.

sections.name: SupplyStats
sections.invariant: the five fields form a self-consistent point-in-time supply snapshot; `Default` is all-zero / not-in-tail.
sections.threat: an uninitialized or partial snapshot misreporting supply to auditors.

sections.name: SupplyStats::new
sections.invariant: `circulating = emitted.saturating_sub(burned)`; burned > emitted clamps to zero, never underflows.
sections.threat: an underflow wrapping circulating supply to a near-`u64::MAX` phantom balance.

sections.name: calculate_supply_commitment
sections.invariant: the commitment is a pure function of the stats — identical stats always hash to identical bytes.
sections.threat: nondeterminism defeating independent auditor verification of the supply invariant.

sections.name: calculate_supply_commitment
sections.invariant: the digest covers emitted / burned / circulating / emission_remaining (changing any one changes the digest) and is domain-separated by the `COINCYNC_SUPPLY_COMMITMENT` tag; `in_tail` is NOT hashed.
sections.threat: a supply field silently tampered without changing the commitment.

sections.name: CandidateBlock::pow_inputs
sections.invariant: `pow_inputs` exposes `(anchor, tx_root, height)` exactly as the validator re-derives them, and `into_block` only stamps the winning nonce, leaving every other field untouched.
sections.threat: miner hashes different inputs than the validator → every solved block is rejected.

sections.name: submit_mined_block
sections.invariant: a mined block traverses the SAME validated `process_block` path as the `submit_block` RPC, then the mempool is realigned (drop confirmed, restore reorg-orphaned, advance height, shadow-evict invalid).
sections.threat: mempool drifts or the miner forks away from peers by accepting an unbroadcast local block.

sections.name: search_nonce
sections.invariant: threads partition the u64 nonce space without gaps and return the first nonce meeting `target`, or `None` once `stop` is set so a superseded candidate is abandoned.
sections.threat: miner spins forever, misses a valid nonce, or keeps mining a stale tip.

sections.name: build_candidate_block
sections.invariant: the reconstructed header (version-at-height, anchor, tx_root, magic) is byte-for-byte what the validator accepts from a rig-mined block, and every malformed template field errors instead of producing an invalid block.
sections.threat: builder/validator divergence → daemon rejects its own block.

sections.name: claimable_fees_for_block_size
sections.invariant: the coinbase claims only `distribute_fee`'s miner share at the block's congestion, sized via the validator's exact block-size formula; pre-activation height claims all fees.
sections.threat: coinbase over-claims fees → block invalid or silent over-emission.

sections.name: build_coinbase_with_fees
sections.invariant: coinbase pays `reward + fees` (saturating) to a fresh stealth address whose ephemeral secret comes from the OS CSPRNG (issue #46) — detectable by the view-key holder but not publicly linkable.
sections.threat: a payout-key-derived secret links every coinbase output to the miner.

sections.name: resolve_network_magic
sections.invariant: an unknown or cross-network magic and malformed tx hex are rejected/skipped, never silently mined into a block.
sections.threat: cross-network replay or a corrupt transaction packed into a candidate.

sections.name: Miner::stats
sections.invariant: the stub reports default (all-zero, not-mining) stats, never fabricated hashrate.
sections.threat: a TUI shows phantom mining activity from a node that is not mining.

sections.name: Miner::start
sections.invariant: the stubbed loop returns `Ok(())` immediately and spawns no work.
sections.threat: a caller believes it started a real miner and burns CPU or blocks.

sections.name: Miner::new
sections.invariant: constructor stores the shared chain and config without side effects.
sections.threat: construction mutates chain state.

sections.name: Miner::stop
sections.invariant: stop is a safe no-op on the stub.
sections.threat: stopping a non-running miner panics.

sections.name: MiningStats
sections.invariant: TUI live data types default to inert values.
sections.threat: uninitialized display fields render stale mining state.

sections.name: PoolServer::start
sections.invariant: the unwired reference server refuses to bind a public address without explicit operator acknowledgements (fail-closed).
sections.threat: someone accidentally runs a non-consensus pool that submits nothing to the chain.

sections.name: create_job
sections.invariant: a job is inserted under a random id with the miner's initial target and rendered as a Stratum V1 notification.
sections.threat: predictable/colliding job ids let a miner replay another's job.

sections.name: on_block_found
sections.invariant: the after-fee reward is split proportional to each login's share difficulty over the PPLNS window; an empty window or zero total difficulty pays nothing; shares beyond 2× the window are pruned.
sections.threat: payout theft or unbounded share-memory growth.

sections.name: process_payout
sections.invariant: a payout fires only above the configured minimum and clears the balance atomically; an unknown address yields `None`.
sections.threat: dust-spam payouts or a double payout.

sections.name: process_stratum_request
sections.invariant: `mining.submit` rejects unauthorized (24), unknown job (21), duplicate (22), malformed nonce/prev-hash/coinbase (20), and below-target (23) shares with the exact Stratum error codes.
sections.threat: an invalid or replayed share is credited → payout fraud.

sections.name: process_stratum_request
sections.invariant: subscribe and authorize set the connection flags; an unknown method returns `-1`.
sections.threat: an unauthenticated connection is treated as authorized.

sections.name: difficulty_to_target
sections.invariant: a share difficulty maps to the target hash used to accept/reject shares.
sections.threat: a miscomputed target credits below-work shares.

sections.name: PoolServer::new
sections.invariant: construction and defaults are inert and safe.
sections.threat: an unsafe default (e.g. public bind) ships silently.

sections.name: validate_stratum_exposure_policy
sections.invariant: a public bind is refused unless native TLS is configured or an explicit encrypted-transport / TLS-proxy ack is present (fail-closed).
sections.threat: plaintext miner credentials and shares exposed on a public interface.

sections.name: Worker::verify
sections.invariant: a submission is classified valid-block vs below-target against the block target; nbits decoding rejects a negative compact and clamps an over-wide one to easiest; requested difficulty clamps to the block target.
sections.threat: a below-work or malformed-target share is credited as valid.

sections.name: downgrade_stale_share
sections.invariant: a share solved against a rotated (no-longer-current) job is downgraded to stale, never credited as valid.
sections.threat: stale-job shares double-counted after a tip change.

sections.name: claim_canonical_nonce
sections.invariant: each canonical nonce is claimed at most once across workers, a stale job id is rejected WITHOUT clearing the ledger, and the ledger resets only on a genuine job rotation.
sections.threat: two workers both credited for one block nonce, or a stale claim wipes the accounting ledger.

sections.name: handle_stratum_message
sections.invariant: native submit rejects unauthenticated, bad-hex nonce, stale job, and duplicate nonce BEFORE running PoW, plus below-difficulty shares; a wrong-password login strikes and returns unauthorized.
sections.threat: unauthenticated or replayed submissions accepted, or wasted PoW verification on junk.

sections.name: handle_stratum_message
sections.invariant: `mining.subscribe` returns the extranonce1 + notify tuple, `mining.authorize` with a wrong password strikes/unauthorized, `mining.submit` rejects invalid-hex fields and unauthorized workers, keepalive/extranonce.subscribe return ok, and an unknown method returns the unknown-method error.
sections.threat: protocol confusion lets an unauthorized worker submit.

sections.name: register_stratum_strike
sections.invariant: repeated invalid or throttled submits accrue strikes to the ban threshold and can deauthorize; the banlist survives restart, a corrupt file loads as empty, and a persist write failure never panics.
sections.threat: an abusive miner is never banned, or a corrupt banlist crashes the server.

sections.name: submit_and_broadcast
sections.invariant: a solved block is submitted through the validated `block_builder` path and broadcast; with no candidate present it returns `false` instead of submitting garbage.
sections.threat: a spurious/empty submission, or a mined block that never reaches peers.

sections.name: share_tally
sections.invariant: `share_tally` weights valid shares per login and skips empty logins; the job updater rotates jobs on tip change.
sections.threat: mis-weighted payout accounting.

sections.name: create_coinbase_prefix
sections.invariant: the coinbase prefix/suffix layout and merkle branches match the Stratum V1 job the miner reassembles; difficulty→nbits guards zero and shift overflow; an empty mempool yields empty branches.
sections.threat: a miner reassembles a coinbase or root the validator rejects.

sections.name: congestion_pct_for_size
sections.invariant: block congestion percentage is the validator's exact integer formula (`size·100/MAX_BLOCK_SIZE`, u128 math, no f64).
sections.threat: builder/validator congestion drift → poison template that fails `validate_block` and stalls the chain.

sections.name: dynamic_min_fee
sections.invariant: per-tx congestion floor is bit-identical to the validator's `checked_mul` chain and returns `None` on the same overflow the validator treats as oversized.
sections.threat: fee-floor drift → assembled block rejected at submission.

sections.name: build_template_json
sections.invariant: emits the full header field set the standalone miner reconstructs; only chain-valid txs clearing the congestion floor are packed; template timestamp is strictly `> prev.timestamp`.
sections.threat: poison-template stall (same shape as the 2026-05-08 duplicate-key-image incident) or a same-second timestamp rejection.

sections.name: 4 fixpoint congestion pass
sections.invariant: recomputing the floor at the FINAL block size and dropping under-paying txs converges (each pass strictly shrinks the set).
sections.threat: early tx clears a low bucket but the final block crosses a higher bucket → template fails the block-level floor.

sections.name: BlockTemplate::new
sections.invariant: copies every header sub-field verbatim and flattens `checkpoint_vote` `(height, Hash)` to the `Hash`.
sections.threat: an external miner sees a template with defaulted/dropped commitment roots and mines an invalid block.

sections.name: BlockTemplate::update_nonce
sections.invariant: mutate the retained header's `nonce`/`timestamp` fields in place.
sections.threat: nonce/time rolling silently no-ops → miner cannot search the space.

sections.name: AggregateKernel
sections.invariant: the struct's fields are exactly the sum of every per-kernel excess point, signature component, and fee.
sections.threat: a mis-summed field would silently desynchronize the aggregate from its constituent kernels.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::aggregate
sections.invariant: every kernel's excess point and 64-byte `R || s` signature must decode as canonical curve/scalar values or the whole aggregation is rejected.
sections.threat: a malformed kernel silently ignored would let bad kernels into a sealed block's aggregate.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::aggregate
sections.invariant: the fee sum uses `checked_add` and errors rather than wraps.
sections.threat: silent `u64` wraparound would under-report the aggregate fee.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::aggregate
sections.invariant: the aggregate is a commutative fold; any permutation of the input kernel set yields an identical `AggregateKernel`.
sections.threat: order-dependence would make the aggregate depend on relay/mempool ordering rather than kernel content, breaking cross-node consensus.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::aggregate
sections.invariant: aggregating zero kernels yields the identity point, zeroed signature, and zero fee.
sections.threat: a non-identity result for an empty block would corrupt the block-scoped verification equation.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::verify
sections.invariant: `verify` returns `true` only when `s*G == R + c*X` holds for the aggregate excess, nonce, and response.
sections.threat: a bypassable check would let an unsigned/forged aggregate kernel pass block validation.

sections.name: BlockAggregator::verify
sections.invariant: the challenge `c` binds the verification to the specific block-scoped message; a signature valid for one message must not verify for another.
sections.threat: missing message binding would let an aggregate signed for one block be replayed against a different block.

sections.name: BlockFilter::from_block
sections.invariant: the filter encodes every output stealth address in the block, keyed deterministically off the block hash.
sections.threat: an address omitted from the filter set is a false negative — the owning personal node never learns to fetch the block.

sections.name: BlockFilter::match_any
sections.invariant: any address that was encoded into the filter must test positive against it.
sections.threat: a false negative here is a funds-visibility bug — the personal node silently misses a block that pays it.

sections.name: derive_sip_key
sections.invariant: the same block hash always derives the same key, and the same element under the same key always hashes to the same range value, for both the encoder and the matcher.
sections.threat: nondeterminism between encode-time and match-time hashing would make every filter a false negative for its own elements.

sections.name: gcs_encode
sections.invariant: hashed elements are sorted, deduplicated, and delta-encoded; an empty element set encodes to empty bytes.
sections.threat: an encoding bug (e.g. unsorted deltas) breaks the merge-join decoder in `gcs_match_any`, causing missed matches.

sections.name: gcs_match_any
sections.invariant: an empty filter or empty `n_elements` returns `false` immediately; otherwise every encoded element that is also queried is found by the merge-join walk.
sections.threat: a false negative allows a matching block to be skipped; a panicking or diverging decoder on truncated data is a DoS surface.

sections.name: golomb_rice_encode
sections.invariant: `decode(encode(v)) == v` for every representable value.
sections.threat: an asymmetric codec corrupts every delta after the first mismatch, silently producing false negatives across the whole filter.

sections.name: BitWriter
sections.invariant: bits written are read back in the same order and count, including a zero-padded final byte.
sections.threat: a bit-alignment bug corrupts every downstream Golomb-Rice value, not just the one being (de)serialized.

sections.name: BootstrapConfig::for_network
sections.invariant: mainnet/testnet/regtest each get their own seed list and P2P port; `Default` never leaks the testnet seed set onto a mainnet node.
sections.threat: mainnet node dials dead testnet seeds on the wrong port and finds zero peers (mainnet launch blocker).

sections.name: Bootstrapper::get_peers_with_proxy
sections.invariant: the OS DNS resolver is never queried while `onion_only` or `proxy_active`; when a proxy is supplied DNS is instead resolved via DNS-over-TCP through SOCKS5, otherwise DNS is skipped entirely.
sections.threat: CRIT-7 (DNS queries bypass SOCKS5/Tor, leaking the user's real IP to whoever runs their ISP's DNS resolver).

sections.name: AddressManager::addr_netgroup
sections.invariant: the netgroup key buckets IPv4 by /16 and IPv6 by /32 in disjoint namespaces, and no single netgroup may exceed its quota of the address book.
sections.threat: address-table eclipse attack (flooding the book with one netgroup to crowd out honest, diverse peers).

sections.name: AddressManager::add
sections.invariant: a known self-address is never re-admitted; a new address from an already-quota'd netgroup is rejected BEFORE any eviction runs; capacity eviction always removes the oldest entry by `last_seen`; operator `manual` peers bypass the netgroup quota.
sections.threat: self-dial waste on restart, and an attacker evicting honest diverse peers to seat its own flooded addresses.

sections.name: AddressManager::get_next
sections.invariant: dial priority is strictly manual peers, then anchors, then the discovered book sorted by `last_seen`; each tier is skipped once tried this cycle; self-addresses are never returned.
sections.threat: a large or stale discovered book starving the operator's manual peer or the persisted anchors out of the outbound dialer (2026-08-16 incident: 0 outbound for 90s+ against an up `--addnode` peer).

sections.name: AddressManager::mark_tried
sections.invariant: after `FAILURE_PURGE_THRESHOLD` consecutive failures with no intervening success, an address is purged from the pool entirely; `manual` peers are exempt; purging is not a permanent ban (re-gossip re-adds it fresh).
sections.threat: dead IPs gossiped forever starving outbound dial slots via the eclipse-defense subnet counter (2026-06-26 incident).

sections.name: AddressManager::mark_success
sections.invariant: a successful connect resets the per-address failure counter; the `tried` set never exceeds `MAX_TRIED`, evicting the oldest entry first.
sections.threat: M-8 (unbounded memory growth in `tried`, and eventual permanent outbound isolation once `get_next` always returns `None`).

sections.name: AddressManager::load_from_file
sections.invariant: an address-book file larger than `MAX_ADDRBOOK_BYTES` is rejected (and removed) before any read; a decoded entry count over `MAX_ADDRBOOK_ENTRIES` is rejected; an empty `[]` array loads cleanly with zero entries.
sections.threat: OOM-on-startup DoS via a multi-GB or N-billion-entry address book file dropped into the data dir by any actor with filesystem access.

sections.name: ShortTxId::from_tx_hash
sections.invariant: the short id is a deterministic function of `(tx_hash, nonce)`; distinct hashes under the same nonce yield distinct ids with overwhelming probability.
sections.threat: a colliding short id misroutes a mempool lookup onto the wrong transaction during reconstruction (see §6).

sections.name: CompactBlock::from_block
sections.invariant: the per-block nonce comes from the OS CSPRNG (`OsRng`), and the coinbase / index-0 transaction is always prefilled while every other transaction is represented only by its short id.
sections.threat: a predictable nonce lets an adversary precompute short-id collisions against the compact block before it is even sent.

sections.name: CompactBlock::savings_estimate
sections.invariant: compact size, full size, and the fractional savings follow the exact stated formula (`header(200) + 6·short_ids + avg·prefilled` vs `header(200) + avg·tx_count`).
sections.threat: a drifted estimate misleads bandwidth-mode heuristics elsewhere in the peer manager.

sections.name: BlockReconstructor::reconstruct
sections.invariant: `total_txs` is checked against the canonical `crate::constants::MAX_TXS_PER_BLOCK` before the per-tx reconstruction vector is allocated.
sections.threat: A5-CB-01 — an inflated tx count could either exhaust memory via an unbounded allocation, or (if a second, independently-drifted cap were used) accept a compact block the validator would reject. FIX #23 removed the standalone `MAX_COMPACT_BLOCK_TXS` constant to close the drift.

sections.name: BlockReconstructor::reconstruct
sections.invariant: every prefilled entry's `index` is `< total_txs`, and no two prefilled entries target the same index.
sections.threat: an out-of-bounds index or a silently-overwritten duplicate produces a reconstructed block whose ordering cannot match the real merkle root, surfacing only as a confusing downstream merkle-root mismatch instead of a clear rejection here.

sections.name: BlockReconstructor::reconstruct
sections.invariant: every remaining slot is filled from the mempool index by short id or else recorded in `missing`; reconstruction succeeds only when `missing` is empty. Reconstruction succeeding is NOT proof the filled transactions are the genuine ones — a short-id collision fills the slot with whatever mempool tx shares that id.
sections.threat: a short-id collision silently substitutes the wrong transaction into the rebuilt block; the header `tx_root` check is the only backstop that catches it.

sections.name: BlockReconstructor::add_transaction
sections.invariant: a late-arriving transaction is indexed under the same nonce the reconstructor was built with, so a subsequent `reconstruct` call can resolve it by short id.
sections.threat: indexing under a mismatched nonce would make the transaction permanently unreachable by short-id lookup.

sections.name: CompactBlockState
sections.invariant: compact blocks are only sent to a peer when both `supported` and `high_bandwidth` are true; `set_pending`/`clear_pending` keep `pending_block` and `missing_txs` in sync with each other.
sections.threat: sending compact blocks to a peer that can't reconstruct them, or leaving stale pending/missing state after a clear, wastes bandwidth or corrupts reconstruction bookkeeping.

sections.name: new
sections.invariant: a fresh tracker holds zero tracked IPs and its memory budget starts fully available.
sections.threat: a mis-initialized budget silently admits unbounded buffers.

sections.name: try_track_connection
sections.invariant: inbound connections from a single IP are capped; the (N+1)-th is refused.
sections.threat: one host opens unlimited sockets to eclipse/DoS the node.

sections.name: untrack_connection
sections.invariant: releasing a connection decrements the count and zero-count IPs are pruned, so slots and the map never leak.
sections.threat: leaked counts wedge the cap shut against honest peers.

sections.name: try_track_outbound_subnet*
sections.invariant: outbound connections per /16 (or v6 group) are capped and admission is atomic under races.
sections.threat: all outbound slots land in one attacker-controlled subnet (eclipse).

sections.name: reconcile_outbound_subnets
sections.invariant: reconciliation against the live set frees leaked subnet slots and an empty live set zeroes every counter.
sections.threat: leaked outbound counts permanently block new dials.

sections.name: allocate
sections.invariant: allocations never exceed the budget; a rejected growth leaves existing reservations intact.
sections.threat: an attacker forces unbounded inbound-buffer allocation (memory DoS).

sections.name: slot
sections.invariant: a reservation returns its bytes/slot exactly once on drop, including under panic and task cancel.
sections.threat: dropped-without-release reservations slow-leak the budget to zero.

sections.name: rotate_epoch
sections.invariant: stem/fluff mode and the 2 relay peers are chosen once per epoch via `OsRng`, never `ThreadRng`, so the choice cannot be predicted from observed process state.
sections.threat: a predictable relay/mode selection lets an observer fingerprint which peer a node picked as its stem relay, deanonymizing tx origin.

sections.name: relay_index_for_inbound
sections.invariant: an inbound peer is mapped deterministically to the same relay index for the life of the epoch, load-balanced across the two relays at first assignment.
sections.threat: inconsistent per-inbound routing would let an attacker replay the same tx from multiple inbound edges to map the stem graph.

sections.name: add_local_tx
sections.invariant: a locally-created tx always enters stem phase; a stem tx that loops back to a node already holding it is immediately fluffed; an already-fluffed tx is ignored, not re-inserted into the stempool.
sections.threat: a stem loop or duplicate re-entry either black-holes a tx forever or creates a re-broadcast amplification loop.

sections.name: random_embargo
sections.invariant: embargo and forward delays are drawn from an exponential (memoryless) distribution via `OsRng`, matching Monero's `CRYPTONOTE_DANDELIONPP_FLUSH_AVERAGE`. THREAT (H16-FIX): a fixed forwarding cadence gives every stem-forwarded tx the same timing signature, deanonymizing the origin node.

sections.name: tick
sections.invariant: a stem tx whose embargo deadline passes without diffusion confirmation is fluffed as a fail-safe; the random forward delay is applied only when a real stem target exists, never when falling back to immediate fluff.
sections.threat: an embargo that never expires lets a censoring stem path silently drop a transaction forever (A7-8 forward-delay regression).

sections.name: enforce_stempool_limit
sections.invariant: at capacity, eviction prefers the oldest PEER-SOURCED entry over LOCAL entries; local entries are only evicted once no peer-sourced entry remains. THREAT (P5-D2): pure oldest-first eviction let an attacker flood the stempool with fresh fake txs and evict the node's own (older) local txs first, silently killing the user's own transactions.

sections.name: has_adequate_privacy
sections.invariant: privacy is reported adequate only at `outbound_peers.len() >= MIN_PEERS_FOR_PRIVACY` (3), a strict `>=` gate.
sections.threat: operating Dandelion++ with too few outbound peers collapses the quasi-4-regular graph, making stem-path tracing tractable.

sections.name: key_image_stripe
sections.invariant: deterministic, uniformly distributed stripe assignment — the same key image always maps to the same stripe.
sections.threat: non-uniform or non-deterministic sharding would concentrate key-image lookups on fewer nodes, weakening the M-13 privacy mitigation this module exists to provide.

sections.name: node_stripe
sections.invariant: a node's identity deterministically maps to exactly one stripe assignment.
sections.threat: a predictable or colliding stripe assignment lets an attacker cheaply target the specific node(s) serving a given key image.

sections.name: is_responsible
sections.invariant: responsibility for a key image agrees exactly with the independent node-stripe and key-image-stripe computations.
sections.threat: a mismatched responsibility check silently drops a query at a node that doesn't actually serve that stripe (lookup denial).

sections.name: DhtState::new
sections.invariant: an explicit `config.dht_stripe` override always wins over the derived hash-based stripe.
sections.threat: a misconfigured/ignored override would silently serve the wrong stripe.

sections.name: DhtState::add_peer
sections.invariant: a peer is registered at most once per stripe, and fully removed from every stripe on disconnect.
sections.threat: duplicate or stale peer entries skew routing decisions and coverage statistics.

sections.name: DhtState::coverage_stats
sections.invariant: `stripes_covered` and `total_peers` are derived directly from `peers_by_stripe` (no separate counter that can drift).
sections.threat: inaccurate coverage stats mask an under-served stripe as a silent liveness gap.

sections.name: MAINNET_DNS_SEEDS
sections.invariant: mainnet seeds resolve only under `coincync.org` and testnet seeds only under `coincync.network`, so the two hostname sets can never overlap.
sections.threat: a shared/overlapping domain would let a mainnet DNS answer satisfy a testnet lookup (or vice versa), crossing network boundaries.

sections.name: MAINNET_FALLBACK
sections.invariant: every hardcoded fallback entry parses cleanly as `ip:port`.
sections.threat: a typo'd entry silently shrinks the fallback list at runtime (each unparseable entry is dropped rather than failing loud).

sections.name: TESTNET_FALLBACK
sections.invariant: the two parallel constants stay byte-for-byte identical.
sections.threat: drift between them reproduces the 2026-06-03 / 2026-06-21 incidents (operators bootstrap via a stale list while the other was updated).

sections.name: TESTNET_FALLBACK
sections.invariant: the fallback list matches the operator-side fleet topology, excluding the `api` role (nginx-only, no P2P listener).
sections.threat: a stale fallback list dials a decommissioned fleet while fleet-config.json has already moved on.

sections.name: TESTNET_FALLBACK
sections.invariant: the fallback list is never empty.
sections.threat: an empty fallback leaves new operators with no bootstrap path when DNS fails, defeating the whole subsystem's purpose.

sections.name: TESTNET_FALLBACK
sections.invariant: decommissioned/destroyed IPs from past incidents never silently re-enter the fallback list.
sections.threat: re-adding a dead IP wastes a connection slot and regresses a previously-fixed incident.

sections.name: netgroup
sections.invariant: keys IPv4 by /16 and IPv6 by /32, and the IPv4/IPv6 keyspaces are tagged so they can never collide.
sections.threat: a mis-keyed netgroup would let an attacker's addresses spread across "different" groups and evade concentration-based eviction.

sections.name: select_inbound_to_evict
sections.invariant: only inbound peers older than `MIN_AGE_BEFORE_EVICT` are ever eviction candidates; outbound (self-chosen) connections are never touched.
sections.threat: evicting an outbound peer or a still-handshaking inbound peer would waste both sides' connection setup work and could be steered by an attacker.

sections.name: 3 Per axis protection (age / activity / reputation)
sections.invariant: protection is purely RELATIVE (top-`PROTECT_PER_AXIS` per axis), never an absolute reputation floor.
sections.threat: audit M-1 — the former absolute `reputation < 80` floor exempted every peer at the default reputation (100), so an all-quiet inbound flood produced an empty candidate set and every new honest inbound was rejected — the exact eclipse this module exists to prevent.

sections.name: 4 Relay score protection axis
sections.invariant: up to `PROTECT_PER_AXIS` peers with `relay_scores.score(id) > 0` are protected, but this axis can never prevent eviction from a netgroup-concentrated flood, even if every flooder has earned score.
sections.threat: an eclipse attacker "buying" eviction-immunity by having every flood peer relay a few real blocks.

sections.name: 5 Netgroup concentration selection
sections.invariant: among the unprotected remaining candidates, the netgroup with the most members is selected as the eviction target.
sections.threat: without concentration-based grouping, an eclipse attacker filling all slots from one /16 would have its members evicted no more often than diverse, legitimate peers.

sections.name: 6 Within group evictee tie break
sections.invariant: within the targeted netgroup, the YOUNGEST (largest `connected_at`) peer is evicted first; ties break toward lower reputation, then toward keeping the encrypted peer (plaintext evicted first).
sections.threat: a LIFO-within-group policy makes churn attacks costly (the attacker's newest connections die first, not its oldest); preferring to keep encrypted peers biases eviction against low-cost plaintext bots.

sections.name: FaucetEntry
sections.invariant: an entry round-trips through JSON and an absent optional description deserializes cleanly.
sections.threat: a strict parser rejects valid signed directories, breaking the wallet faucet list.

sections.name: FaucetRegistry
sections.invariant: the payload implements the registry contract (network, schema, timestamp) correctly and round-trips with many entries.
sections.threat: a malformed payload passes verification or a valid one is dropped.

sections.name: 3 namespace isolation
sections.invariant: the faucet-registry signature namespace is distinct from the peer-snapshot namespace.
sections.threat: cross-service signature reuse lets a snapshot signature authorize a forged faucet directory.

sections.name: maintainer_pubkey_from_env
sections.invariant: only a well-formed 32-byte hex key is accepted; wrong lengths are rejected (returns `None`).
sections.threat: a truncated or garbage env key is silently treated as a valid trust anchor.

sections.name: fetch_verified_faucet_registry
sections.invariant: fetch delegates to the signed-registry verify path and is soft-fail (errors never crash the wallet).
sections.threat: an unreachable/hostile IPFS gateway takes down the wallet, or an unsigned directory is displayed as trusted.

sections.name: has_cap
sections.invariant: a capability check is a strict bitmask match; unknown bits present in `caps` never affect the result for a known `cap`.
sections.threat: capability confusion causing a node to assume an unsupported feature is present on a peer.

sections.name: local_capabilities
sections.invariant: the OR-set this node advertises in its own Flare exactly matches what it actually supports.
sections.threat: an advertised-but-unsupported capability would let a peer extend chain-work sync trust (Phase 2) to a node that can't honor it.

sections.name: 3 zero capabilities backward compatibility
sections.invariant: a peer that never sent a Flare (`capabilities == 0`) is reported as supporting zero features, and nothing disconnects for the missing Flare.
sections.threat: breaking interoperability with older nodes or external implementations that predate the capability layer.

sections.name: MessageFramer::read_message
sections.invariant: payload bytes are only ever grown incrementally (starting at a ≤64 KB initial allocation) rather than pre-allocated to the header's claimed length.
sections.threat: an attacker claiming a huge payload but never sending it would otherwise force large up-front memory commitment per connection.

sections.name: validate_wire_header
sections.invariant: a frame is rejected before its payload is read if the magic bytes mismatch, the wire length exceeds `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` or the per-type limit, or (when normalization is enabled) the size isn't a canonical bucket.
sections.threat: oversized/forged frames causing unbounded allocation or protocol confusion.

sections.name: decode_payload
sections.invariant: the payload's checksum must verify and its *decoded* (post-denormalize) length must still respect `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` and the per-type cap, even though the wire length already passed `validate_wire_header`.
sections.threat: A6 (denormalize inflating an accepted small wire frame into an oversized logical payload) plus generic bit-flip corruption.

sections.name: read_message_with_inactivity_timeout_inner
sections.invariant: header and payload bytes already pulled off the reader survive a dropped/cancelled future on `self.header_buf` / `self.payload_buf`, so a resumed call completes the same logical message instead of losing bytes and desyncing the stream.
sections.threat: `tokio::select!`-driven cancellation (e.g. outbound `rx.recv()` firing mid-read during IBD) silently dropping in-flight bytes, corrupting all subsequent frame parsing ("invalid magic" cascade).

sections.name: read_budgeted_message_timeout
sections.invariant: a payload byte is only ever counted against the connection's memory budget once, the reservation grows in step with bytes actually buffered, and it is released exactly once (on success, on budget-exceeded rejection, or on connection close) — never leaked and never double-counted across a cancellation.
sections.threat: per-connection memory-budget bypass / accounting drift leading to unbounded memory growth (DoS).

sections.name: write_message
sections.invariant: an outbound payload is rejected before any bytes reach the wire if it exceeds `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`, the per-type cap, or names an undefined message-type discriminant.
sections.threat: a local bug emitting an oversized or malformed frame that a remote peer's own header validation would otherwise have to catch.

sections.name: normalize_size_with_overhead
sections.invariant: normalizing a payload to a fixed bucket size and later denormalizing it recovers the exact original bytes, including at every bucket-size boundary.
sections.threat: size-based traffic-analysis leakage if normalization is skipped, or payload corruption if the round-trip isn't exact.

sections.name: read_message_with_inactivity_timeout
sections.invariant: a peer that stops sending mid-message (rather than closing the connection) is bounded by a per-chunk inactivity timer, not an unbounded wait.
sections.threat: Slowloris-style connection-slot exhaustion.

sections.name: EclipseDetector::record_connect
sections.invariant: connect/disconnect counters only ever increment within the current 5-minute window; `maybe_reset` clears them once the window has elapsed, so churn from a stale window never leaks into the current one.
sections.threat: undercounting real churn (window drift) or overcounting stale churn, either of which defeats the eclipse-attack signal.

sections.name: EclipseDetector::is_suspicious_churn
sections.invariant: the suspicious-churn signal fires only when BOTH recent connects and recent disconnects exceed 20 in the current window — a one-sided spike (e.g. many disconnects from a network blip) does not alone trigger it.
sections.threat: an eclipse attacker cycling connections to fill all peer slots with attacker-controlled peers; also guards against false positives from ordinary network instability.

sections.name: maybe_reset
sections.invariant: the reset check uses a fixed 300-second threshold (`last_reset.elapsed().as_secs() > 300`) applied identically on every `record_connect`/`record_disconnect` call, so the window length is deterministic and cannot be extended by caller timing.
sections.threat: an attacker pacing connection churn just under the reset boundary to stay under threshold indefinitely while still cycling peers.

sections.name: to_socket_addr
sections.invariant: port `0` and unspecified IPv6 are never converted to a dialable address; IPv4-mapped IPv6 is unwrapped to plain IPv4.
sections.threat: an undialable address occupying an address-book slot and padding an attacker's per-/16 quota with entries that can never become a useful outbound peer (H7 dial-starvation/eclipse).

sections.name: is_routable
sections.invariant: loopback, multicast, unspecified, RFC1918 private ranges, link-local, CGNAT (100.64/10), documentation/benchmark ranges, and the broadcast address are all rejected as non-gossip-worthy.
sections.threat: gossiping private/reserved addresses lets a peer waste other nodes' outbound slots on unreachable targets, or probe internal networks.

sections.name: is_routable
sections.invariant: ordinary public IPv4 addresses are accepted for gossip.
sections.threat: an overly broad reject list would starve the address book of legitimate peers, indirectly aiding eclipse by shrinking peer diversity.

sections.name: is_routable
sections.invariant: unique-local (`fc00::/7`), link-local (`fe80::/10`), documentation (`2001:db8::/32`), and IPv4-compatible (but not IPv4-mapped) IPv6 are all rejected.
sections.threat: same as §2 for the IPv6 address space — non-routable ranges gossiped as public peers waste dial attempts and probe local networks.

sections.name: is_routable
sections.invariant: ordinary global unicast IPv6 addresses are accepted for gossip.
sections.threat: as §3, an overly broad IPv6 reject list would shrink peer diversity and aid eclipse attempts.

sections.name: send_to_peer
sections.invariant: the returned bool exactly reflects delivery outcome — `true` only on a successful enqueue, `false` for a missing or closed peer channel, never a false positive.
sections.threat: a caller trusting a false "sent" result would believe a message reached a peer it never did (silent message loss).

sections.name: send_to_peer
sections.invariant: the DashMap shard guard is dropped before awaiting channel capacity, so a parked send never blocks unrelated map inserts/removes.
sections.threat: holding a shard lock across a bounded-channel `.await` would let one congested peer stall inserts for every other peer sharing that shard.

sections.name: send_to
sections.invariant: a missing peer is a silent no-op (`Ok(())`) while a closed channel surfaces as `Error::ConnectionFailed`, matching callers that need to distinguish "gone" from "never existed".
sections.threat: mis-signaling closed-vs-missing would cause callers to retry a dead peer forever or silently swallow a real disconnect.

sections.name: broadcast_raw
sections.invariant: no `.await` occurs while a DashMap iterator/entry guard is live, and one full/slow peer channel never blocks delivery to any other peer in the same broadcast pass.
sections.threat: a single congested peer stalling propagation to the whole mesh (the historical "sync-stall" class of bug this function's comments reference).

sections.name: broadcast_raw
sections.invariant: a peer whose send queue is full on `STALL_THRESHOLD` consecutive broadcasts is banned rather than retried forever.
sections.threat: an unresponsive or malicious peer permanently occupying a connection slot while contributing nothing to propagation.

sections.name: announce_chain_work
sections.invariant: the ChainWork advertisement is sent only to peers whose capability bitset actually has `CAP_CHAINWORK`.
sections.threat: broadcasting to non-capable peers wastes bandwidth and can confuse peers that don't understand the message type.

sections.name: queue_transaction
sections.invariant: a locally-originated transaction always enters the Dandelion++ stem phase (`add_local_tx`) rather than being flooded directly, preserving sender-anonymity intent.
sections.threat: skipping stem routing for local txs would deanonymize the broadcasting node as the transaction's origin.

sections.name: ChainShadow
sections.invariant: `seq` is the sole authority for acceptance ordering, not `height`, because a legitimate heavier-chain reorg may lower height (issue #249).
sections.threat: ordering updates by height alone would let a stale, still-taller pre-reorg snapshot win over the correct post-reorg one.

sections.name: ChainState::update
sections.invariant: an update is applied only if `seq > shadow.seq`; equal or lower sequences are rejected and leave the shadow untouched.
sections.threat: an out-of-order or duplicate publication (e.g. a delayed task) could regress the shared chain-tip view seen by sync and peer handshakes.

sections.name: ChainState::next_sequence
sections.invariant: sequence numbers are monotonically increasing per node instance via an atomic fetch-add, starting after 0.
sections.threat: a non-atomic or reused counter could hand out duplicate sequence numbers, defeating the ordering guarantee in §2.

sections.name: ChainStateReader::snapshot
sections.invariant: readers observe the same `(height, tip)` pair the writer last committed, never a torn read across the two fields.
sections.threat: a torn read could hand a consumer (e.g. handshake code) a tip hash that doesn't correspond to the reported height.

sections.name: normalize_noise_record
sections.invariant: a decrypted Noise record is accepted only at a canonical traffic-shaper bucket size; non-bucket sizes are rejected rather than silently accepted.
sections.threat: a malformed/padded record slipping through as valid plaintext, or a covert channel via off-bucket sizes.

sections.name: noise_bridge
sections.invariant: encrypt and decrypt directions run as two independent tasks, never inside one `select!`, because `read_encrypted`'s two sequential `read_exact` calls are not cancellation-safe.
sections.threat: a cancelled read mid-handshake permanently desyncs the AEAD nonce, silently breaking all subsequent decryption for the peer.

sections.name: cleanup_connection
sections.invariant: a peer/sender map entry is only removed by the connection task that still owns it (matched via `connection_token` / `same_channel`); a superseding reconnection is never evicted by its predecessor's teardown.
sections.threat: a slow-closing stale connection racing a fresh reconnect could delete the live peer's state and desync `PeerDisconnected` events.

sections.name: handle_connection
sections.invariant: when `trusted_peers` is configured, only a Noise-authenticated remote static key present in that allowlist may complete the connection; plaintext is rejected outright in that mode.
sections.threat: encryption bypass or impersonation of a trusted static key would let an unauthenticated attacker to reach a peer meant to be closed-set.

sections.name: handle_connection
sections.invariant: once a Noise handshake succeeds, `peer_id` is replaced by the authenticated remote static key everywhere (`info.id`, `peers`, `senders`) so `pick_scored_peer` and map lookups can't split identity.
sections.threat: a TCP-level id surviving alongside the Noise-derived id would let one physical peer register twice, subverting per-peer accounting (bans, eclipse slots, tx-absence scoping).

sections.name: handle_connection
sections.invariant: the read side always uses the inactivity-timed `read_budgeted_message_timeout` (never a bare read) so a peer trickling partial frames cannot pin the slot forever; writes never bypass `MessageFramer`'s framing/size checks.
sections.threat: A Slowloris-style partial-frame peer starving connection slots.

sections.name: COINCYNC_WIRE_TRACE
sections.invariant: the env-gated per-packet trace line is purely observational — it must never alter what is sent or change control flow when disabled or enabled.
sections.threat: a tracing hook accidentally gating or delaying real traffic would corrupt propagation timing it is meant only to observe.

sections.name: handle_get_addr
sections.invariant: address-book responses (Addr) are sent only to Noise-encrypted (authenticated) peers; a plaintext peer's GetAddr is silently ignored.
sections.threat: Firework Veil — a passive/unauthenticated observer mapping P2P topology without ever completing an authenticated connection.

sections.name: handle_addr
sections.invariant: oversized Addr payloads are rejected before deserialization and score OversizedMessage; nothing is added to the book.
sections.threat: P5-N-CLASS-A payload-size DoS / malformed-message spam poisoning the address book.

sections.name: handle_addr
sections.invariant: future-dated (`timestamp > now+600`) and stale (`age > 7d`) addresses are rejected and never enter the book.
sections.threat: clock-manipulation / stale-address pollution used to starve honest dial slots or resurrect dead peers.

sections.name: handle_addr
sections.invariant: unroutable IPs (e.g. loopback) are rejected and never enter the book.
sections.threat: an attacker padding the book with unroutable entries to waste dial slots and poison onward gossip.

sections.name: handle_addr
sections.invariant: an accepted address's `last_seen` is clamped to `min(claimed_timestamp, receive_time)`, so a peer-relayed address can never appear fresher than the moment we heard it.
sections.threat: H7 (dial starvation / eclipse) — a near-future timestamp (within the accepted `now+600` window) sorting ahead of honestly-observed peers for dial order and dodging last_seen-based eviction.

sections.name: handle_addr
sections.invariant: an address with port 0 is undialable and must never be added to the book.
sections.threat: H7 — a port-0 entry occupying a book slot and padding an attacker's per-/16 netgroup quota without ever being dialable.

sections.name: invblock_near_tip
sections.invariant: near-tip vs. deep-IBD classification is inclusive at the window boundary (`gap <= window`), so a node exactly at the edge is still treated as near-tip and kept on prompt catch-up.
sections.threat: CIP-019 (a boundary node misclassified as deep-IBD stays trapped a few blocks behind forever, wedging the miner's sync gate).

sections.name: handle_get_blocks
sections.invariant: oversized GetBlocks payloads are rejected before deserialization and produce no response; a valid request always gets a response, even with zero blocks found.
sections.threat: P5-N-CLASS-A oversized-payload exhaustion; a silently-dropped empty-result reply would strand the requester's download slots.

sections.name: handle_inv_block
sections.invariant: post-IBD unknown-block fetches never speculatively bump the peer's advertised height; only Version/Headers updates real heights.
sections.threat: the 2026-06-27 production sync-wedge — a speculative +1 height bump latched permanently when the announced block never arrived, pinning `is_synced()` false and requiring an emergency `COINCYNC_RIG_SKIP_SYNC_CHECK=1` bypass.

sections.name: handle_blocks
sections.invariant: each relayed block is rejected on wrong network magic and on RandomX PoW failure BEFORE reputation credit or `BlockReceived` emission; bad PoW triggers an instant ban and never credits or emits.
sections.threat: a malicious relay building peer reputation or injecting unvalidated blocks into the event pipeline / CPU-exhaustion via garbage blocks.

sections.name: handle_get_data
sections.invariant: oversized GetData payloads are rejected before deserialization/DB access; validated requests fetch and serialize blocks off the async worker thread via `block_in_place`.
sections.threat: P5-N-CLASS-A oversized-payload triggering unbounded DB reads.

sections.name: handle_block_data
sections.invariant: a single relayed block is rejected on wrong network magic and on PoW failure before its relay score is credited or it is emitted to the event pipeline.
sections.threat: same class as §4 — unvalidated single-block relay building relay reputation or reaching consensus without proof of work.

sections.name: handle_version
sections.invariant: oversized, unparseable, or `validate()`-failing Version messages score misbehavior and disconnect before any peer state is trusted; a self-connection nonce match disconnects WITHOUT scoring, since the nonce is replayable from any peer that saw our outbound Version.
sections.threat: NET-001 eclipse-attack surface (scoring a replayed nonce would let an attacker blacklist arbitrary addresses as "self"); M5 unbounded user_agent OOM.

sections.name: handle_version
sections.invariant: peer-supplied `user_agent` has control characters stripped before it is ever stored, and height/tip/state are recorded only after validation passes.
sections.threat: stored-XSS-class injection reaching any unescaped consumer of `get_peers` (explorer UIs, scripts, monitors).

sections.name: handle_flare
sections.invariant: Flare capability advertisement is advisory-only; oversized or malformed payloads are dropped silently and never cause a disconnect or misbehavior score.
sections.threat: a pre-Firework peer sending an unhandled/malformed Flare must not be penalized, or every legacy-compatible peer would be punished.

sections.name: handle_chain_work
sections.invariant: ChainWork is stored as an unauthenticated claim that only feeds peer-work/height bookkeeping for header-source selection; oversized or malformed payloads are silently dropped and never disconnect the peer.
sections.threat: a peer over-claiming cumulative work to bias header-fetch source selection (fork-choice adoption itself recomputes real PoW downstream).

sections.name: handle_verack
sections.invariant: handshake completion always sends GetAddr, and a behind peer gets at most one in-flight GetHeaders — a replayed Verack while a request is pending must not re-issue GetHeaders.
sections.threat: duplicate/uncapped GetHeaders requests wasting bandwidth or re-triggering a sync wedge.

sections.name: handle_ping
sections.invariant: a malformed (<8-byte) Ping scores ProtocolViolation and never elicits a Pong; a well-formed Ping echoes its nonce exactly; Pong itself is a no-op.
sections.threat: P5-N5 malformed-ping spam evading misbehavior scoring.

sections.name: handle_reject
sections.invariant: Reject only adjusts peer reputation by a fixed benign-disagreement penalty and never feeds the ban scorer.
sections.threat: legitimate protocol disagreement being over-penalized into an accidental ban.

sections.name: header_history
sections.invariant: walks parent hashes back at most `DIFFICULTY_LONG_WINDOW` blocks and errors on a missing ancestor rather than silently truncating.
sections.threat: an unbounded or silently-short ancestor walk feeds a wrong difficulty window into validation, letting forged targets slip through.

sections.name: validate_header_batch
sections.invariant: every header must match the chain's network magic, connect to a known parent, increment height by exactly one, and chain `prev_hash`-to-hash contiguously within the batch.
sections.threat: cross-network replay or a disjoint/forked batch being accepted as a valid extension of the chain.

sections.name: validate_header_batch
sections.invariant: header version never regresses below the height-activation floor or the parent's version; timestamp strictly advances past the parent and, once `MTP_WINDOW` history exists, past the median-time-past.
sections.threat: timestamp manipulation to bias difficulty retargeting or replay stale headers.

sections.name: validate_header_batch
sections.invariant: a hardcoded checkpoint mismatch rejects the header outright; otherwise the header's `target` must equal the chain's own `expected_next_target` for that history (single-sourced, not recomputed ad hoc).
sections.threat: a peer claiming an easier-than-valid target once difficulty is active, or a checkpoint-violating alternate history.

sections.name: validate_header_batch
sections.invariant: `verify_pow` must succeed against the header's bound anchor/nonce/tx_root/target before a header is accepted into `hashes`.
sections.threat: a structurally-valid header with forged or missing PoW being queued for sync.

sections.name: handle_get_headers
sections.invariant: oversized `GetHeaders` payloads are dropped and scored before parsing; the response is bounded to `MAX_HEADERS_RESPONSE` headers starting from the first locator match.
sections.threat: a giant or unbounded GetHeaders request driving unbounded disk reads or an oversized response.

sections.name: handle_headers
sections.invariant: an inbound `Headers` response is honored only for the peer it was issued to, and a nonce is consumed on first (even empty) use, never on a cross-peer or replayed attempt.
sections.threat: eclipse-style cross-peer nonce spoofing or nonce replay poisoning `ChainSync` state.

sections.name: handle_headers
sections.invariant: malformed borsh and rejected header batches both score the peer via `record_misbehavior` with the classified offense, and a rejected batch never reaches `queue_headers_from_peer`.
sections.threat: unscored garbage or invalid-header spam from a misbehaving peer.

sections.name: unix_now
sections.invariant: returns whole seconds since the Unix epoch and never panics under a normal system clock.
sections.threat: a `duration_since` panic (clock set before the epoch) crashing the router on every message that needs a timestamp (e.g. Dandelion routing).

sections.name: process_message
sections.invariant: a `Padding` message is discarded before peer activity/byte accounting or scoring ever sees it.
sections.threat: cover-traffic packets polluting peer stats or being misrouted into a real handler.

sections.name: process_message
sections.invariant: `GetFilters`/`GetOutputDigests`/`GetFilterCheckpoints`/ `GetKeyImageStatus` payloads over `MAX_LIGHT_QUERY_PAYLOAD` are dropped and scored `OversizedMessage` before reaching the per-handler backstop in `query.rs`.
sections.threat: DoS amplification via oversized DHT/light-client queries on a path with no framing-level per-type cap (audit R3-4).

sections.name: process_message
sections.invariant: any message type other than the handshake set (`Version`/`Verack`/`Ping`/`Pong`/ `Flare`) is ignored for a peer that hasn't reached `PeerState::Connected`.
sections.threat: pre-auth attack surface exploitation by an unauthenticated peer (H-3).

sections.name: process_message
sections.invariant: every known `MessageType` discriminant routes to exactly one handler, and an unrecognized discriminant fails via `MessageType::try_from` rather than panicking or falling through.
sections.threat: an unhandled or misrouted message type crashing the connection loop or reaching the wrong handler.

sections.name: bounded_height_range
sections.invariant: the returned range never exceeds `requested_end`, `chain_tip`, or `start + max_items - 1`, and `start > requested_end`, `start > chain_tip`, or `max_items == 0` yields `None` rather than an inverted or unbounded range.
sections.threat: an inverted or unbounded height range driving unbounded per-height disk reads and filter/digest recomputation.

sections.name: handle_get_filters
sections.invariant: accumulated *encoded* filter bytes never exceed `MAX_QUERY_RESPONSE_BYTES`, regardless of how many items `bounded_height_range` would otherwise allow.
sections.threat: an output-dense height range producing a response near `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` despite the item-count cap.

sections.name: handle_get_output_digests
sections.invariant: the request range is capped at `MAX_DIGEST_BLOCKS_PER_REQ` and the response at `MAX_QUERY_RESPONSE_BYTES`; the server never learns which specific outputs interest the requesting wallet, only the height range.
sections.threat: a light-wallet privacy leak (address-set exposure as in BIP-157) or unbounded per-request disk/CPU amplification.

sections.name: handle_get_filter_checkpoints
sections.invariant: checkpoints are rebuilt at most once per 1000-block bucket (`CHECKPOINT_CACHE`) and the response is capped at `MAX_CHECKPOINTS` entries.
sections.threat: a zero-body, cheap-to-send request being replayed to force repeated O(chain_height) disk reads and filter recomputation.

sections.name: handle_get_key_image_status
sections.invariant: a payload over `MAX_KI_QUERY_PAYLOAD` is rejected before `borsh::from_slice` runs, so a large declared length can't force an oversized allocation ahead of the `take(100)` truncation.
sections.threat: a crafted length-prefixed payload triggering a large pre-parse allocation regardless of the eventual 100-item cap.

sections.name: handle_get_key_image_status
sections.invariant: at most 100 key images are checked per request, and a valid request receives a `KeyImageStatus` response.
sections.threat: unbounded per-request DB lookups from an oversized key-image list.

sections.name: handle_response
sections.invariant: response-typed messages (`Filters`/`OutputDigests`/`FilterCheckpoints`/`KeyImageStatus`) are a pure no-op on a full node and never fall through into request-handling logic.
sections.threat: request/response message-type confusion enabling a reflection or double-processing path.

sections.name: handle_inv_tx
sections.invariant: an `InvTx` payload over `MAX_INV_PAYLOAD` is dropped and scored `OversizedMessage` before any borsh decode is attempted.
sections.threat: unbounded deserialization work from an oversized inventory message (P5-N8 / P5-N-CLASS-A).

sections.name: handle_inv_tx
sections.invariant: a tx-absence record is only consulted for the peer that reported it; one peer's `NotFound` never stops requesting the same hash from another peer.
sections.threat: an attacker suppressing network-wide tx propagation by claiming absence on hashes other peers actually have (N-1).

sections.name: handle_not_found
sections.invariant: `NotFound` hashes are recorded as absent only against the reporting peer's id, never globally.
sections.threat: an unsolicited `NotFound` spray from one peer suppressing relay from honest peers.

sections.name: handle_get_txs
sections.invariant: every requested hash not present in the mempool is echoed back via an explicit `NotFound` response instead of silently omitted.
sections.threat: peers repeatedly re-requesting the same absent hashes, wasting bandwidth/CPU on both sides.

sections.name: handle_txs
sections.invariant: a transaction is routed to Dandelion/relay only after it passes both the cheap structural check (`validate_transaction_basic`) and the full UTXO-backed `chain.validate_transaction`; a failure at either gate is scored and the tx is never relayed or credited as a successful relay.
sections.threat: a cryptographically forged (structurally valid) tx being fluffed to every peer before any node fully validates it — network-wide invalid tx amplification.

sections.name: handle_txs
sections.invariant: a `StemAction::Stem` result never inserts the tx into the local mempool; only `StemAction::Fluff` broadcasts an `InvTx` to all peers and emits `NodeEvent::TransactionReceived`.
sections.threat: a stem-phase tx entering the mempool prematurely, defeating Dandelion++ origin-hiding.

sections.name: handle_not_found
sections.invariant: each handler rejects and scores payloads above its own size cap (`MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` / `MAX_GETTXS_PAYLOAD`) before parsing.
sections.threat: unbounded borsh decode of an oversized wire message.

sections.name: spawn_maintenance
sections.invariant: if the inner maintenance loop ever exits (panic, clean return, or cancellation not caused by shutdown), a CRITICAL log line fires so the condition is externally observable; it never fails silently.
sections.threat: a poisoned lock or panic inside the loop killing ping/dandelion /scoring/ban-flush while `systemd is-active` still reports healthy — the 2026-06-19 production silent-hang incident this comment documents.

sections.name: run_ping_tick
sections.invariant: every ping interval, a keepalive is sent to all current senders and expired tx-absence entries are pruned, using a best-effort send (dead channels don't abort the tick).
sections.threat: without periodic pings, `PEER_TIMEOUT`-based liveness on the remote side evicts us even on a healthy link; without pruning, the tx-absence cache grows unbounded between hard-cap evictions.

sections.name: run_dandelion_tick
sections.invariant: locally-queued transactions are drained into the stem pool, the live outbound peer set is refreshed before each tick, and `stem_relay`/`fluff` actions are sent to exactly the target peer (stem) or all peers (fluff) with no duplication.
sections.threat: stalled or misrouted Dandelion++ actions would either leak the originating peer (broken stem privacy) or fail to propagate a transaction at all.

sections.name: run_cleanup_tick
sections.invariant: peers idle past `PEER_TIMEOUT` are fully torn down (tracker/sync/orphan-flood/event) each cleanup interval, and peer scores decay/auto-ban/expire on the same cadence.
sections.threat: a peer that silently stopped responding but never explicitly disconnected would occupy a connection slot indefinitely, and unbounded score/ban-list growth would eventually exhaust memory.

sections.name: run_tip_announce_tick
sections.invariant: the current tip is re-announced via `InvBlock` on a fixed interval, and is a no-op when the tip is still the zero hash (no chain yet).
sections.threat: the 2026-06-27 gossip bug this fixes — peers that missed the original tip announcement (e.g. connected after it fired) would never learn the current tip and stall in sync.

sections.name: flush_ban_list
sections.invariant: the ban list is persisted to disk every interval regardless of whether it changed; a save failure is logged, never panics the maintenance loop.
sections.threat: an unpersisted ban list is lost on restart, letting a previously-banned peer reconnect immediately after a crash.

sections.name: rotate_outbound_peer
sections.invariant: when more than 3 outbound peers are connected, the single longest-connected outbound peer is dropped each rotation interval; 3 or fewer outbound peers is a no-op.
sections.threat: a patient eclipse attacker holding long-lived outbound slots indefinitely; periodic forced churn bounds how long any one outbound peer set can persist. Closes audit MEDIUM #28.

sections.name: emit_heartbeat
sections.invariant: one INFO line per tick reporting a monotonically increasing counter and current peer/outbound counts, so an external watchdog can detect a frozen maintenance loop.
sections.threat: the silent-hang failure mode from §1 going undetected for hours (17h in the referenced production incident) instead of ~30s.

sections.name: spawn_listener_acceptor
sections.invariant: concurrent inbound connection *tasks* (including those still mid-Noise-handshake) are bounded at `MAX_INBOUND + INBOUND_HANDSHAKE_SLACK` via an owned permit taken at accept time, independent of the post-handshake `MAX_INBOUND` peer count.
sections.threat: an IP-diverse half-open flood spawning unbounded handshake tasks (each holding ~64 KiB buffers) that `MAX_INBOUND` alone can't see.

sections.name: spawn_listener_acceptor
sections.invariant: when inbound is at `MAX_INBOUND`, a new connection is only admitted if `select_inbound_to_evict` names a more-evictable existing peer to drop first; otherwise the newcomer is rejected.
sections.threat: an attacker filling all inbound slots from one /16 to pin the node and block honest inbound peers (eclipse via slot exhaustion).

sections.name: spawn_outbound_connector
sections.invariant: the connector never dials its own listen port, never redials an address with a live peer, and honors both the 30s min-reconnect-delay and per-address exponential backoff.
sections.threat: without these gates the connector self-connects, thrashes a single peer in a connect/disconnect loop, or burns Noise handshake slots retrying too fast — starving real address-book progress.

sections.name: spawn_outbound_connector
sections.invariant: an attacker controlling one /16 cannot hold more than `MAX_OUTBOUND_PER_SUBNET` of our outbound slots, and the slot always releases on task exit (clean, error, or panic) via `Drop`.
sections.threat: eclipse attack via subnet-concentrated outbound peers.

sections.name: save_anchors_to_disk
sections.invariant: only `Connected` outbound peers are persisted as anchors; a missing or malformed anchor file falls back to an empty list rather than erroring.
sections.threat: losing all outbound peers on a hard kill (SIGKILL/OOM/power loss) would force a slow full re-bootstrap instead of fast reconnect.

sections.name: ban_peer
sections.invariant: banning commits scorer + tracker state (address ban, connection untrack) before the peer/sender map entries are removed, so a reconnect racing the cleanup still observes the ban.
sections.threat: a reconnect slipping through during ban teardown would let a banned peer re-establish before the ban becomes visible.

sections.name: disconnect_peer
sections.invariant: a normal disconnect removes tracker/peer/sender/dandelion/sync state and emits `PeerDisconnected` without applying the reputation penalty `ban_peer` applies.
sections.threat: conflating normal disconnects with bans would over-penalize honest peers that merely dropped connection (e.g. restart, network blip).

sections.name: pick_scored_peer
sections.invariant: weighted selection uses each connected peer's composite score (floor 0.05) so no connected peer is ever mathematically unreachable, with a uniform fallback if the scorer lock can't be acquired or all weights are zero.
sections.threat: a scoring bug that zeroes out weights entirely would make relay/target selection silently starve, biasing propagation or making Dandelion routing predictable.

sections.name: NodeRuntime::shutdown
sections.invariant: every tracked task is given up to a 5-second deadline to join after the shutdown signal fires; a task that misses the deadline is aborted and awaited rather than left to run forever.
sections.threat: an unbounded join would let a stuck task hang node shutdown indefinitely, blocking process exit or restart.

sections.name: wait_for_shutdown
sections.invariant: if the shutdown flag is already set when checked, returns immediately instead of waiting on a `changed()` that may never fire again (a `watch` channel only reports one edge per waiter).
sections.threat: waiting on `changed()` after the flag was already flipped could deadlock a task that starts polling late.

sections.name: spawn_padding_broadcast
sections.invariant: the padding loop's own `AtomicBool` shutdown flag is set before the task returns on the `wait_for_shutdown` branch, so `run_padding_loop_broadcast` observes cancellation even though it's driven by a separate flag from the `watch::Receiver`.
sections.threat: forgetting to propagate the signal into the padding loop's own flag would leave the traffic-shaping padding task running after shutdown, delaying process exit.

sections.name: spawn_message_processor
sections.invariant: `rate_trackers` is pruned of any peer no longer present in `processor_peers` every `RATE_PRUNE_EVERY` (1000) messages, bounding its size to roughly the live peer set.
sections.threat: pre-fix, entries were inserted per peer but never removed on disconnect, so a long-running node with peer churn leaked memory unboundedly (P5-N3).

sections.name: spawn_message_processor
sections.invariant: a peer that exceeds its per-message-type rate limit has the offending message dropped (not processed) and is scored `MisbehaviorType::MessageFlood`, but the processor loop itself keeps running.
sections.threat: without the drop-and-continue behavior, a flooding peer could either starve the queue for other peers or crash/stall the single processor task shared by all peers.

sections.name: spawn_message_processor
sections.invariant: the processor task exits when either the shutdown signal fires or every message producer drops its sender (channel closes) — whichever comes first, checked with `biased` select so a pending shutdown always wins a simultaneous race.
sections.threat: an ambiguous or unbiased exit condition could leave the processor task running after node shutdown, or exit it prematurely while producers still expect it to drain.

sections.name: SyncDriverState::emergency_recovery_due
sections.invariant: emergency Tier-3 recovery fires only after `EMERGENCY_T3_NO_PROGRESS_SECS` of no height advance, and re-fires at most every `EMERGENCY_T3_REPEAT_SECS` thereafter — never every tick.
sections.threat: 2026-06-02 orphan-fetch cascade (coincync-lon, 22+h stuck) where the sync engine looked internally busy so `is_stalled` never fired; without the repeat-throttle, an unthrottled version would log-flood at tick rate.

sections.name: run_headers_tick
sections.invariant: the tick loop checks `headers_request_pending()` and returns early rather than issuing a second concurrent GetHeaders.
sections.threat: Finding #3 headers-request flood — the pre-fix loop sent GetHeaders unconditionally every tick (~4 Hz hammer) while stuck on a fork, exhausting CPU.

sections.name: spawn_sync_driver
sections.invariant: when the chain has not advanced for `EMERGENCY_T3_NO_PROGRESS_SECS` despite `is_stalled()` reporting false, the driver forces a deep reset (clear tried-list, drop expired orphans, reset headers timeout, force `SyncState::Headers`) using the max of `target_height` and live connected-peer heights as the ground-truth "are we behind" signal.
sections.threat: 2026-07-09 idle/limp-while-behind — `peer_heights`-derived `is_synced()`/`target_height` empties under connection churn and every recovery path stops firing, leaving the node idle indefinitely.

sections.name: stall_count
sections.invariant: escalation counters reset on real progress and only climb on consecutive no-progress firings; Tier-3 backoff pauses 30s after `N_T3_BEFORE_BACKOFF` consecutive no-progress escalations to stop hammering peers and flooding logs.
sections.threat: 2026-06-01/02 (barns1253, coincync-lon) — Tier-2 alone cycled thousands of times without ever clearing a stuck sync.

sections.name: send_block_spans
sections.invariant: block-hash spans are only distributed to peers whose advertised height is strictly greater than local height.
sections.threat: 2026-08-16 — a same-height stuck follower peer received part of the request span, answered empty, and IBD wedged permanently with no recovery tier able to clear it.

sections.name: live_block_peers
sections.invariant: only peers that are `Connected`, have an open (non-closed) sender channel, and are not `GetBlocks`-banned by the scorer are offered as IBD block sources; peers with a closed sender are pruned from the map.
sections.threat: sending GetBlocks to a dead or banned peer wastes a download slot and delays legitimate catch-up.

sections.name: run_synced_tick
sections.invariant: a `Synced` node whose `true_best_height` is more than 2 blocks above local (or local is 0 with peers present) re-triggers a resync rather than sitting idle.
sections.threat: a node that settles into `Synced` prematurely (e.g. after a peer_heights reset) would otherwise never re-check for real work.

sections.name: TxAbsenceCache
sections.invariant: absence is scoped per reporting peer, never globally by hash alone.
sections.threat: N-1 — an unauthenticated `NotFound` from one malicious peer would otherwise suppress relay of a targeted transaction from ALL honest peers for the TTL window (indefinitely refreshable), a targeted mempool-censorship primitive.

sections.name: mark_absent
sections.invariant: an entry is reported absent only while within its TTL from insertion, and only for the exact `(peer, hash)` pair recorded.
sections.threat: a stale or cross-hash "absent" result would cause the node to either wrongly skip re-requesting an available transaction or spam redundant requests.

sections.name: mark_absent
sections.invariant: once `max_size` is reached, a prune is attempted first and, if still at capacity, the single oldest entry is evicted to admit the new one — the cache never grows past `max_size`.
sections.threat: unbounded growth (e.g. an attacker cycling many distinct hashes per peer) exhausting memory.

sections.name: prune
