sections.invariant: `prune` removes exactly the entries whose TTL has elapsed and returns the count removed; live entries are untouched.
sections.threat: a prune that removed live entries would defeat §1's per-peer scoping (nothing left to consult); a prune that never removes anything would defeat §3's memory bound between hard-cap hits.

sections.name: ChainUpdateToken
sections.invariant: a token is single-use and `#[must_use]`, so a caller cannot silently drop a captured publication order without it being flagged at compile time.
sections.threat: a discarded or reused token would let a chain-state publication commit out of the order it was captured in, reopening the issue #249 stale-write race that `ChainState::update` guards against.

sections.name: NodeEvent
sections.invariant: `BlockReceived`/`TransactionReceived` always carry their relay/source `PeerId` (or `None`) alongside the payload, so downstream consensus feedback can attribute misbehavior/invalidity to the correct peer.
sections.threat: dropping the peer attribution would make invalid-block/invalid-tx scoring blind, letting a misbehaving peer resend indefinitely without penalty.

sections.name: NodeConfig::default
sections.invariant: defaults derive from `NetworkType::Mainnet.params()` and the shared `MAX_PEERS`/`MAX_OUTBOUND` constants, so the facade and its config never drift apart.
sections.threat: a hand-duplicated default that skews from the real constants could silently under- or over-provision peer slots.

sections.name: NetworkStats
sections.invariant: these are plain aggregate snapshots with no derived/cached fields that could go stale relative to the live counters they summarize.
sections.threat: a stale cached counter could misreport peer/memory pressure to operators relying on these stats for capacity decisions.

sections.name: P2PNode::new
sections.invariant: if the identity file exists but fails to load, the node logs loudly and still starts rather than halting; only a genuinely missing file takes the silent fresh-install path.
sections.threat: silent ephemeral fallback on a transient read error changes our peer_id, losing accumulated peer reputation and presenting as a Sybil twin (P5-N1).

sections.name: query_key_images_via_dht
sections.invariant: the `parking_lot::Mutex` guard over DHT stripe state is dropped before any `.await`; sends clone the `mpsc::Sender` out of the peer `DashMap` before awaiting it.
sections.threat: holding a sync lock or a DashMap shard guard across an `.await` deadlocks every other task touching the same state (P5-N2).

sections.name: publish_chain_state
sections.invariant: chain-tip publication is serialized under `chain_publication` and only the highest-sequence `ChainUpdateToken` commits; no `.await` occurs between the shadow commit and the sync-state update, so cancellation cannot leave `ChainState` ahead of `ChainSync`.
sections.threat: an out-of-order or cancelled publication could regress the node's advertised height/tip and desynchronize sync progress (issue #249).

sections.name: notify_block_invalid
sections.invariant: `MissingParent` never scores or bans a peer; every other classified offense is scored and, past threshold, bans.
sections.threat: scoring `MissingParent` as misbehavior banned our own miner during a legitimate deep reorg and partitioned the fleet for ~20 hours (2026-07-04 incident).

sections.name: notify_block_orphan
sections.invariant: orphan rate-tracking (`orphan_flood`) is recorded for observability only and is never fed to the peer scorer.
sections.threat: scoring orphan floods as misbehavior banned our own miner sending legitimate blocks from a heavier chain, causing an 18-hour partition (2026-06-22 incident).

sections.name: notify_block_accepted
sections.invariant: draining orphans of a connected hash re-emits each via `NodeEvent::BlockReceived` exactly once, terminating the cascade rather than looping.
sections.threat: undrained orphans stalled sync for up to the 30-minute orphan TTL on out-of-order/reorg delivery.

sections.name: start
sections.invariant: all fallible resource acquisition (address book/ban list load, bootstrap, socket bind/listen) completes before `running` becomes visible or any task is spawned; a failed `start` can be retried, but a successful one is one-shot.
sections.threat: publishing `running = true` before resource acquisition succeeds would let callers observe a half-started node; allowing a second start after success would double-spawn tasks over the same state.

sections.name: stop
sections.invariant: `running` flips false and all runtime tasks are joined/aborted before address book, ban list and anchors are persisted, so no in-flight task can mutate state after it's saved.
sections.threat: persisting before shutdown could race a still-running task's writes, corrupting the on-disk address book or ban list.

sections.name: broadcast_context
sections.invariant: any DashMap iteration used to build a send fan-out is collected into a `Vec` (dropping the iterator/shard locks) before the per-peer `.await`.
sections.threat: holding a DashMap shard lock across an await blocks every other task touching that shard — a runtime-wide futex-park cascade.

sections.name: ConnectionTracker
sections.invariant: per-IP connection limits are enforced and released correctly; default `NodeConfig` matches the documented peer-count constants.
sections.threat: an unenforced per-IP cap enables connection-slot exhaustion by a single host.

sections.name: write_secret_file
sections.invariant: node identity secrets are created/left with owner-only permissions (mode 0o600 on Unix, ACL-restricted via icacls on Windows), with no TOCTOU window where a wider-permission file is briefly readable.
sections.threat: local-user secret-key disclosure (P5-No1).

sections.name: NodeIdentity::generate
sections.invariant: the X25519 transport secret and Ed25519 anchor-signing secret are independent, persisted separately, and never reloaded as all-zeros.
sections.threat: a zeroed or shared secret would collapse Noise key agreement or anchor-signature unforgeability.

sections.name: NodeIdentity::sign_anchor_payload
sections.invariant: anchor signatures are domain-separated (`ANCHOR_SIGN_DOMAIN`) so they can never be replayed as a valid signature under a different protocol context.
sections.threat: cross-protocol signature confusion / replay.

sections.name: NoiseHandshake::execute
sections.invariant: the Noise_XX 3-message handshake completes only with a mutually authenticated, non-all-zeros remote static key before transitioning to transport mode.
sections.threat: unauthenticated or null-key peer acceptance would let an attacker impersonate a peer or downgrade to an unencrypted channel.

sections.name: NOISE_HANDSHAKE_FRAME_MAX
sections.invariant: a pre-authentication handshake frame is capped at 8 KB, far below the 65535-byte snow/Noise ceiling.
sections.threat: unauthenticated peer forcing a 64 KB allocation per handshake attempt (memory-exhaustion DoS before any identity is verified).

sections.name: NoiseTransport::write_encrypted
sections.invariant: every transport message is bounded by `MAX_NOISE_PAYLOAD`, and each Noise nonce is advanced exactly once per `write_message`/`read_message` call (snow's internal counter), so a nonce is never reused for two distinct plaintexts.
sections.threat: nonce reuse under a fixed key breaks ChaChaPoly confidentiality/integrity; unbounded payload size enables memory exhaustion.

sections.name: read_message
sections.invariant: any tampering with ciphertext or its Poly1305 tag is detected and surfaced as a decryption error, never silently accepted or decoded as different plaintext.
sections.threat: message forgery / bit-flipping attack on the encrypted P2P channel.

sections.name: add
sections.invariant: the pool never holds more than `MAX_ORPHAN_SIZE` entries; once at capacity, `evict_oldest` runs before the new block is inserted.
sections.threat: an unbounded orphan pool lets an attacker flood a node with parentless blocks to exhaust memory.

sections.name: evict_oldest
sections.invariant: eviction always removes the entry with the smallest insertion sequence number (strict oldest-first LRU), via the `oldest_first` BTreeMap index rather than a linear scan.
sections.threat: evicting anything other than the true oldest entry would let a flood of new orphans push out arbitrary (possibly still-relevant) entries, or regress to the prior O(n²) scan under load.

sections.name: take_children
sections.invariant: reconnecting a parent's children removes each returned block from all three indices (`by_parent`, `parent_by_hash`, `seq_by_hash`/`oldest_first`) together, leaving no dangling entries.
sections.threat: a partial removal would leak index entries, letting a stale `parent_by_hash`/`seq_by_hash` pair reference a block no longer in `by_parent`, corrupting later `contains`/eviction decisions.

sections.name: expire
sections.invariant: only entries received strictly before `current_height - ORPHAN_TTL_BLOCKS` are dropped, and only after `current_height >= ORPHAN_TTL_BLOCKS` (no underflow on a young chain).
sections.threat: an unguarded subtraction would underflow `current_height` on a short chain (panic/wraparound); no TTL at all would let stale orphans accumulate forever.

sections.name: generate_peer_id
sections.invariant: peer IDs are generated with a cryptographically secure RNG (`OsRng`), never a predictable source.
sections.threat: a guessable peer ID could be leveraged to impersonate or collide with another peer's identity.

sections.name: PeerState
sections.invariant: a peer's state is a strict 3-stage progression `Connecting → VersionReceived → Connected`; no other transition is reachable in the current codebase.
sections.threat: a stray transition (e.g. skipping version negotiation) would let an unauthenticated connection be treated as fully handshaked.

sections.name: PeerInfo::adjust_reputation
sections.invariant: reputation is always clamped to `[-100, 100]`; no update can push it outside that range.
sections.threat: unclamped reputation would let either a sybil flood of positive updates make a peer un-bannable, or a single burst of negative updates have unbounded lasting effect.

sections.name: PeerInfo::should_ban
sections.invariant: a peer is banned iff `reputation <= -50`, a fixed inclusive threshold.
sections.threat: an off-by-one or non-strict boundary would let a just-below-threshold malicious peer keep connecting indefinitely.

sections.name: PeerInfo::decay_reputation
sections.invariant: reputation decays monotonically toward (never past) the given neutral value, regardless of whether it starts above or below neutral.
sections.threat: without decay, a single transient issue (or a single act of goodwill) would permanently pin a peer's reputation, defeating the purpose of a recoverable trust score.

sections.name: PeerInfo::eclipse_slot
sections.invariant: the per-/16 outbound slot's lifetime is bound to the `PeerInfo` entry via `Arc`; it is released exactly when the entry is removed or overwritten, never leaked or double-freed.
sections.threat: a leaked slot lifetime (tied to the spawn task instead of the map entry) would let eclipse-defense accounting drift, eventually starving legitimate outbound slots on a subnet.

sections.name: PeerConnection::run
sections.invariant: inbound bytes are capped by both a 10 MB/s rate limit and a rolling 60s / 100 MB window; outbound messages over `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` are dropped without disconnecting. THREAT (H-7): unbounded per-connection throughput allows a single peer to exhaust bandwidth/memory; a lifetime-cumulative cap (the pre-fix behavior) would instead break legitimate long-running IBD transfers.

sections.name: verify_signature_with
sections.invariant: the signature must be exactly 64 raw Ed25519 bytes and must verify over `SIGNATURE_NAMESPACE || snapshot_bytes`, not over the bare snapshot bytes.
sections.threat: without domain separation, a signature the maintainer produced for another artifact (release tag, checkpoint) could be replayed as a fake peer snapshot.

sections.name: validate_snapshot
sections.invariant: a snapshot is accepted only if `snapshot.network == expected_network`.
sections.threat: a mainnet snapshot accepted on testnet (or vice versa) would hand a node peer addresses for the wrong chain.

sections.name: validate_snapshot
sections.invariant: a snapshot claiming a timestamp more than 5 minutes in the future is rejected.
sections.threat: an unbounded future timestamp would let a malicious or compromised producer make a stale/poisoned snapshot always look freshest.

sections.name: validate_snapshot
sections.invariant: on a non-fresh cold start, the snapshot's `unix_ts` must be strictly newer than `last_seen_snapshot_ts`.
sections.threat: without strict-newer replay defence, an attacker who once captured a valid signed snapshot could keep re-serving it indefinitely.

sections.name: maintainer_pubkey_from_env
sections.invariant: an unset, empty, or non-32-byte-hex env value returns `None` (snapshot fallback disabled), never a partially-decoded or defaulted key.
sections.threat: falling back to a wrong-length or garbage key would either panic downstream or silently accept snapshots nothing actually signed.

sections.name: fetch_bounded
sections.invariant: a response is rejected (via `Content-Length` when present, and always via a post-read length check) once its size exceeds the caller-supplied `max_bytes` cap, before the full body is used.
sections.threat: an unbounded gateway response (malicious or misconfigured IPFS gateway) could exhaust memory or smuggle an oversized payload past `MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`.

sections.name: fetch_from_gateways
sections.invariant: gateways are tried in a fixed order and the function only errors (`AllGatewaysFailed`) after every configured gateway has failed to serve both the snapshot and signature bytes.
sections.threat: giving up after a single gateway failure would let one compromised or offline gateway effectively deny the bootstrap fallback.

sections.name: connect_peer
sections.invariant: when `proxy.onion_only` is set but the proxy is not active, ALL connection attempts are refused — there is no fallback branch that reaches direct `TcpStream::connect`.
sections.threat: CRIT-8 (clearnet fallback silently deanonymizing a Tor-only user by leaking their real IP to a peer).

sections.name: connect_peer
sections.invariant: direct `TcpStream::connect` is only reached when the proxy is absent/inactive AND `onion_only` is false, i.e. the user has not opted into Tor-only mode.
sections.threat: unintended clearnet connections for a user who believes proxy routing is mandatory.

sections.name: connect_via_proxy
sections.invariant: only `ProxyType::Socks5` is accepted; SOCKS4/HTTP are rejected with `ConfigError` before any connection attempt.
sections.threat: silently downgrading to an unauthenticated or unsupported proxy protocol that doesn't provide the expected anonymity properties.

sections.name: connect_onion
sections.invariant: connecting to a `.onion` address requires both an active proxy and `ProxyType::Socks5`, and the address must literally end in `.onion` before being forwarded.
sections.threat: attempting onion routing over a non-Tor-capable proxy, or forwarding a non-onion hostname through the onion-only code path (DNS-leak / protocol-confusion risk).

sections.name: is_onion_address
sections.invariant: the `.onion` suffix check operates on the hostname portion only (after stripping a trailing `:port`), so `notreal.onion.example.com` style strings are not misclassified as onion addresses.
sections.threat: routing decisions (onion vs. clearnet) being spoofed by a crafted hostname, potentially sending onion-destined traffic clearnet or vice versa.

sections.name: PeerTarget::parse
sections.invariant: `.onion` addresses are parsed via `rsplitn` on the LAST colon (correct for `<56-char-onion>.onion:port`, which contains no other colons), and non-onion input is parsed as a strict `SocketAddr`, with malformed input rejected rather than silently defaulting.
sections.threat: a malformed peer-address string being misinterpreted as a different (possibly attacker-chosen) host/port.

sections.name: ProxyConfig::url
sections.invariant: `url()` never includes the username/password even when set; credentials are only obtainable via the separate `credentials()` accessor.
sections.threat: proxy password leaking into logs or diagnostics that print the proxy URL.

sections.name: RelayScoreMap::credit_block
sections.invariant: deposits saturate at `RELAY_SCORE_MAX` and are only ever reachable from the block-receive path (no transaction observation feeds this map).
sections.threat: an un-poisonable score requires the *only* input to be public, provably-costly-to-fake data (an actually-relayed valid block).

sections.name: RelayScoreMap::evaporate
sections.invariant: each round multiplies by `EVAP_NUM/EVAP_DEN` (keep 90%) with no `u32` overflow at the max score, and zero-score peers are dropped from the map entirely.
sections.threat: an un-evaporated score would let a peer that relayed once keep permanent eviction protection long after it stops being useful.

sections.name: RelayScoreMap::forget
sections.invariant: unconditionally removes a peer's score (used on disconnect) so stale entries don't linger.

sections.name: RelayScoreMap::score
sections.invariant: an unknown peer returns `0` rather than panicking, so callers never need a fallible lookup.

sections.name: RelayScoreMap::top
sections.invariant: deterministic ordering — descending by score, ties broken ascending by `PeerId` — so eviction's protection set is reproducible across runs.

sections.name: 6 Prime invariant (block only input) as consumed by eviction
sections.invariant: `eviction.rs`'s relay-score protection axis stays bounded (`PROTECT_PER_AXIS`) and never overrides netgroup-concentration eviction, so a sybil that "earns" relay score by flooding one netgroup is still evicted.
sections.threat: turning an anti-poisoning measure into an eclipse assist would be worse than not having the axis at all.

sections.name: MisbehaviorType::penalty
sections.invariant: penalties are calibrated tiers toward the -50 ban threshold; `OrphanFlood`/`MissingParent` stay at zero and can never accumulate to a ban.
sections.threat: misclassifying legitimate reorg/mining behavior as an attack caused two testnet chain-partition stalls (2026-06-22, 2026-07-04).

sections.name: classify_invalid_block_reason
sections.invariant: reason-string classification routes genuine protocol/PoW/proof violations to instant-ban categories while routing non-fault causes (missing-parent reorg race, our own system-clock error) away from instant-ban.
sections.threat: F32 (SEV-B) — an overly broad `"timestamp"` substring match instant-banned every peer when OUR clock failed; the 2026-07-04 misclassification of `MissingParent` as `InvalidBlockProofs` banned our own miner during a legitimate reorg.

sections.name: classify_invalid_tx_reason
sections.invariant: oversized-payload rejections map to `ProtocolViolation`, fee-floor rejections map to the low-weight `LowFeeFlood` bucket (dynamic fee floor can legitimately exceed a relaying peer's estimate), everything else maps to `InvalidTransaction`.
sections.threat: HIGH #13 — sybil spam below the dynamic fee floor must accumulate to a ban without punishing honest fee-estimator drift.

sections.name: PeerScore
sections.invariant: `composite_score` is a bounded `[0,1]` weighted blend; `decay` converges monotonically to neutral; `should_ban` fires exactly at reputation `<= -50`.

sections.name: record_empty_blocks_response
sections.invariant: empty `Blocks` replies below `EMPTY_BLOCKS_BAN_THRESHOLD` never erode reputation; at/after the threshold the peer is temporarily banned from `GetBlocks` selection and reputation charges begin; the ban auto-expires and resets the counter.
sections.threat: eclipse via speculative/fabricated IBD hashes driving an honest bystander to the disconnect floor; the "stall pathology" wedge observed 2026-05-04/05 where an unhelpful peer never got demoted.

sections.name: record_misbehavior
sections.invariant: all misbehavior scoring flows through `record_misbehavior`, which both deducts reputation and emits a debug trace; the earlier bypassing `record_protocol_violation` method was removed so no code path silently changes reputation without observability.
sections.threat: F2 — divergent call sites causing a silent observability gap on 9 of 24 protocol-violation call sites.

sections.name: PeerMessageRateTracker
sections.invariant: every table entry corresponds to a real `MessageType` discriminant, and every attacker-amplification message type is present in the table.
sections.threat: F21 (SEV-A) — a stale hex-literal table let GetBlocks/GetData floods bypass `MessageFlood` detection entirely (unbounded CPU-burn attack surface).

sections.name: OrphanFloodTracker
sections.invariant: per-peer isolated sliding window; flags at most once per window when the threshold is crossed.
sections.threat: orphan-flood CPU-recheck DoS, while not penalizing peers that legitimately fan out orphans during a deep reorg.

sections.name: PeerScorer
sections.invariant: `ban` opportunistically prunes expired entries and removes the peer's score; the on-disk ban list round-trips exactly through save/load.

sections.name: top_peers_for_download
sections.invariant: both selectors return only `validated` peers, regardless of composite score or latency.

sections.name: 1 Ed25519 signature verification
sections.invariant: a payload verifies only when namespace, payload bytes, and key all match; any mismatch is rejected.
sections.threat: a forged or cross-namespace signature authorizes a malicious payload.

sections.name: 2 signature length gate
sections.invariant: a signature that is not exactly 64 bytes is rejected before any curve operation.
sections.threat: malformed-length input triggers a panic or an accidental accept.

sections.name: 3 network / schema binding
sections.invariant: a payload for the wrong network or an unexpected schema version is refused.
sections.threat: a mainnet-signed (or future-schema) payload is replayed onto testnet clients.

sections.name: 4 anti replay freshness gate
sections.invariant: a payload older than the last-seen timestamp is rejected, while a strictly fresher one is accepted.
sections.threat: an attacker replays a stale-but-valid directory to roll back the view.

sections.name: 5 NTP clock slack
sections.invariant: a timestamp within the NTP slack window is accepted but one beyond the future bound is rejected.
sections.threat: a far-future timestamp poisons the replay gate against all later honest payloads.

sections.name: 6 cold start replay gate
sections.invariant: with no prior last-seen the replay gate is skipped so a fresh install can bootstrap.
sections.threat: cold-start deadlock leaves a new node unable to accept any directory.

sections.name: RegistryPointer
sections.invariant: the pointer parses with optional fields absent and fetch returns only a fully verified payload.
sections.threat: a strict parser breaks fetch, or an unverified payload reaches the caller.

sections.name: resolve_via_socks5
sections.invariant: the function refuses to run when `proxy.is_active()` is false, and never returns an empty `Ok(vec![])` (empty results are upgraded to `Err`).
sections.threat: silently falling through to un-proxied resolution, or callers mistaking "no records" for "resolved to nothing" and skipping the hardcoded-seed fallback.

sections.name: query_one
sections.invariant: every DNS query and response leaves/enters the process only through the SOCKS5 tunnel (`Socks5Stream::connect[_with_password]`) — there is no direct-socket code path to the resolver.
sections.threat: DNS-leak (the exact bug this module fixes, see module docs) — a leaked DNS query would deanonymize a Tor-mode user's bootstrap lookups.

sections.name: query_one
sections.invariant: the RFC 7766 2-byte length prefix on both the outbound query and the inbound response is validated against `(0, MAX_DNS_RESPONSE]` before any `read_exact`/`write_all` of the body, so a malicious or buggy resolver can never force an unbounded allocation via `resp_len`.
sections.threat: memory-exhaustion DoS from a compromised/malicious DNS resolver or a MITM on the exit hop.

sections.name: build_query
sections.invariant: hostname length (`<= 253`) and each DNS label length (`<= 63`, RFC 1035 §2.3.4) are enforced before any bytes are placed on the wire.
sections.threat: a malformed/oversized hostname producing a malformed DNS query the resolver could misparse or hang on.

sections.name: parse_response
sections.invariant: every offset walked while parsing the header, question, and answer sections is checked against `buf.len()` before being dereferenced; a truncated or lying `ANCOUNT`/`RDLENGTH` is rejected rather than over-read.
sections.threat: a malicious resolver response causing an out-of-bounds read / panic (DoS) or memory disclosure.

sections.name: parse_response
sections.invariant: a response whose ID doesn't match the query's is rejected outright; NXDOMAIN (RCODE 3) is treated as an empty, non-error result distinct from a resolver-side failure.
sections.threat: DNS response spoofing/injection (off-path or malicious-resolver) being accepted as authoritative.

sections.name: skip_name
sections.invariant: name traversal is bounded by both `buf.len()` and a fixed step counter (256), so a crafted compression-pointer cycle cannot loop forever.
sections.threat: a malicious response with a self-referential/cyclic compression pointer hanging the resolver-response parser (DoS).

sections.name: refresh_best_known
sections.invariant: `best_known_height == max(local_height, max(peer_heights))`, a TRUE recompute on every mutation, never a one-way ratchet.
sections.threat: phantom `target_height` wedge — a stale/departed peer's claim pins the sync target above local forever, `is_synced()` stays false, the miner refuses to mine (2026-06-27 production incident).

sections.name: recompute_best_difficulty
sections.invariant: `best_known_difficulty == max(local_total_difficulty, max(peer_difficulties))`, recomputed (not ratcheted) so it can shrink.
sections.threat: difficulty-side analogue of the height wedge — a stale high work-claim latches `best_known_difficulty` above local and blocks catch-up detection from ever clearing.

sections.name: work_behind_substantiated
sections.invariant: an unsubstantiated work-behind veto self-heals after `WORK_SUBSTANTIATION_GRACE_SECS` unless our own cumulative work is actually rising; a persistent liar re-advertising the same claim cannot restart the grace window.
sections.threat: incident H6 — a peer that merely claims a heavier chain pins the miner off indefinitely even though it never delivers blocks.

sections.name: update_peer_height_for
sections.invariant: a peer height claim more than 10,000 above local is REJECTED outright, never clamped-and-stored.
sections.threat: 2026-06-06 "phantom +10_000" fleet-wedge — clamping stored a poisoned value that re-propagated via gossip across the whole fleet and survived restarts.

sections.name: MAX_ORPHANS_PER_PEER
sections.invariant: a single peer's orphan deliveries are never silently dropped by a per-peer cap; only the total-pool cap (`MAX_ORPHAN_BLOCKS`) plus LRU eviction bounds memory.
sections.threat: incident F24 (2026-07-04 SEV-A) — a per-peer cap of 50 silently dropped 578 of 628 intermediate blocks during a legitimate deep reorg, so the reorg could never complete.

sections.name: mark_block_failed
sections.invariant: a block sitting in `downloading` with no matching `pending_requests` entry past `STUCK_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS` is detected and re-queued, not left to rot.
sections.threat: Bug 3 (NYC stuck at height 12) — a download that lost its request-tracking entry would otherwise never be retried.

sections.name: queue_headers_inner
sections.invariant: one peer's queued headers are capped so it cannot fill the 50K-slot pending-header pool and starve other peers' headers.
sections.threat: v1.0.13 #4 — a single peer winning the GetHeaders nonce race floods the pool with bogus hashes, blocking legitimate peers.

sections.name: begin_headers_request
sections.invariant: a Headers response is accepted only if its nonce is outstanding AND was issued to that exact peer AND belongs to the current generation.
sections.threat: Jun #2 (cross-peer response) — a different peer answering (or griefing) a request never sent to it must not be honoured.

sections.name: normalize_size
sections.invariant: payloads pad to the smallest fitting standard bucket and round-trip exactly; an unmarked payload is rejected.
sections.threat: packet length leaks message type (block vs tx) to a passive observer.

sections.name: apply_jitter
sections.invariant: when disabled the shaper is a pure pass-through (no correctness change), and shaping only pads/delays.
sections.threat: timing correlation across nodes, or shaping corrupting the payload.

sections.name: generate_padding_packet
sections.invariant: padding packets are correctly framed with the network magic and randomized per call.
sections.threat: predictable/static padding is trivially filtered out by a DPI box.

sections.name: run_padding_loop
sections.invariant: the loop emits per-peer packets each tick, honors the enabled flag, and never blocks on a slow peer.
sections.threat: a full/slow peer stalls the whole constant-rate cover.

sections.name: DummyTrafficPacer::submit
sections.invariant: exactly one packet leaves per slot, real traffic preferred and dummy used only as filler.
sections.threat: bursty output re-exposes the activity the padding hides.

sections.name: 6 pacer bounded queue / overflow
sections.invariant: the pacer queue is bounded; on overflow it signals the caller to direct-send rather than dropping silently.
sections.threat: unbounded queue growth (memory DoS) or dropped real messages.

sections.name: explorer_html
sections.invariant: the served page is assembled from compile-time embedded HTML/CSS/JS and is non-trivial.
sections.threat: a missing or empty embedded asset serves a broken explorer.

sections.name: 2 JS ↔ server method pinning
sections.invariant: every `rpc('…')` the explorer JS calls corresponds to a method registered on the JSON-RPC server.
sections.threat: a future explorer rewrite calls an unregistered method → silent runtime breakage and server/UI drift.

sections.name: 3 supply display precision
sections.invariant: aggregate supply values render through JS `BigInt`, not `f64`.
sections.threat: large supply totals lose precision or overflow in the UI.

sections.name: 4 external origin allowlist
sections.invariant: the embedded HTML enumerates its external CDN origins explicitly.
sections.threat: an un-audited external script origin slips into the page.

sections.name: scan
sections.invariant: scans with the VIEW key only, enforces a hard max-blocks-per-request cap, rejects invalid view/spend hex, and saturates start-height arithmetic; returned outputs are candidates the wallet must verify.
sections.threat: DoS via unbounded scan ranges, integer overflow, or malformed keys crashing the endpoint.

sections.name: submit_transaction
sections.invariant: rejects non-hex and undecodable-borsh payloads and surfaces the mempool's rejection reason instead of swallowing it.
sections.threat: a malformed tx crashes the endpoint, or a rejection is hidden from the wallet.

sections.name: chain_info
sections.invariant: `chain_info`'s ring size is height-aware for the NEXT block, and `estimate_fee` is `size · MIN_FEE_PER_BYTE` plus a 20% buffer.
sections.threat: a wallet builds a tx with a wrong ring size or an underpaid fee and the block/mempool rejects it.

sections.name: get_digests
sections.invariant: the block-digest range is saturating and returns only blocks that exist.
sections.threat: an out-of-range request overflows or fabricates digests.

sections.name: find_fork_point
sections.invariant: returns the last common ancestor from the reorg journal (tip when fully canonical, `None` on empty / no-canonical), skipping unknown heights.
sections.threat: a wrong fork point makes a light wallet rescan from the wrong height and miss or double-count outputs.

sections.name: compute_view_tag
sections.invariant: the view tag is deterministic and index-dependent, output matching uses the canonical ECDH scan, and public-key parsing rejects non-32-byte or non-hex input.
sections.threat: mis-tagged outputs are missed or misattributed, or a malformed key is accepted.

sections.name: coin_info
sections.invariant: the served coin specification is correct.
sections.threat: wrong coin metadata misconfigures a connecting wallet.

sections.name: rpc_methods_doc
sections.invariant: the discovery document is well-formed JSON with the `rpc.discover` info/methods shape.
sections.threat: a malformed discovery doc breaks clients that introspect via `rpc.discover`.

sections.name: 2 method catalog coverage
sections.invariant: each entry documents a method's name, parameters, and return type.
sections.threat: the published catalog drifts from the server's actual registered surface.

sections.name: check
sections.invariant: requests within a window count atomically and excess is blocked; the window resets and re-admits after it elapses.
sections.threat: rate-limit bypass through miscounting or a race.

sections.name: check_sync
sections.invariant: the sync path matches the async path on ban/permanent/window decisions and fails CLOSED on lock contention; loopback is whitelisted.
sections.threat: a lock-contention path silently disables rate limiting.

sections.name: ban
sections.invariant: a ban blocks until expiry then re-admits; exceeding max bans yields a permanent block that survives LRU eviction.
sections.threat: a repeat abuser evades bans by waiting them out or forcing eviction of their record.

sections.name: 4 LRU eviction (memory bound)
sections.invariant: tracked IPs are capped by LRU; expired entries evict first and eviction is refused when all entries are active.
sections.threat: memory-exhaustion DoS from many distinct source IPs.

sections.name: 5 whitelist
sections.invariant: whitelisted IPs bypass the limit and adding an entry dedupes.
sections.threat: an operator IP is throttled, or duplicate entries bloat state.

sections.name: remaining
sections.invariant: `remaining` reports the correct quota (and whitelist), `stats` account accurately, and `cleanup` retains banned and recent entries.
sections.threat: inaccurate accounting, or cleanup dropping an active ban.

sections.name: 7 config presets
sections.invariant: `strict` / `relaxed` / `default` presets are distinct policies.
sections.threat: a preset silently equals another → the wrong policy is applied.

sections.name: rpc_proxy
sections.invariant: only allowlisted read-only RPC methods are forwarded; sensitive methods are blocked; backend error codes map to HTTP status; an unreachable backend returns a sanitized 502; oversize bodies 413 and invalid JSON 400; a configured bearer is forwarded.
sections.threat: an attacker reaches a write/operator method or leaks backend internals through the proxy.

sections.name: 2 privacy field stripping
sections.invariant: forwarded `get_info`/status/network responses strip privacy/operator fields and ring correlators.
sections.threat: the public explorer leaks operator-only or deanonymizing data.

sections.name: enforce_fixed_window_limit
sections.invariant: per-window and per-IP fixed-window limits return 429 under burst, the client IP is taken from forwarded headers ONLY when proxy trust is enabled, and stale entries prune at cap.
sections.threat: DoS, or IP spoofing via a forged `X-Forwarded-For` to evade the limit.

sections.name: validate_hex_hash
sections.invariant: hex-hash params are validated, pagination clamps to bounds, and search rejects empty/overlong/no-match queries.
sections.threat: injection or resource abuse through malformed path/query params.

sections.name: get_supply
sections.invariant: circulating supply parses without precision loss and formats correctly above `u64`, rejecting lossy or invalid RPC values.
sections.threat: a supply above `u64` truncates → wrong economic display.

sections.name: 6 block / tx / mempool read handlers
sections.invariant: block-by-hash/height, block-transactions, transaction, recent-blocks, and mempool endpoints return the expected shapes and 400/404 on bad or missing input.
sections.threat: a malformed lookup 500s or leaks.

sections.name: submit_transaction
sections.invariant: rejects non-hex and oversize payloads with 400 and rate-limits submissions.
sections.threat: malformed or flooded tx submissions abuse the write path.

sections.name: health
sections.invariant: liveness returns 200 regardless of backend; readiness returns 503 when the backend is unreachable.
sections.threat: a load balancer routes traffic to a node whose backend is dead.

sections.name: ws_per_ip_check_and_increment
sections.invariant: per-IP WS connections count up to a cap then reject, and decrement on drop; ping/pong works.
sections.threat: WS connection exhaustion from a single IP.

sections.name: 10 CORS / assets gone / emission / events / anonymity
sections.invariant: CORS allows known origins and omits unknown; removed asset endpoints return 410 Gone; emission/events/anonymity return valid payloads.
sections.threat: a stale asset route or permissive CORS leaks data cross-origin.

sections.name: start_rpc_server
sections.invariant: the server refuses to start with TLS enabled (unsupported here), with auth enabled but no API key, or on a non-loopback bind lacking an API key and a TLS ack; loopback with a key and auth disabled warns but starts.
sections.threat: an unauthenticated RPC exposed on a public interface.

sections.name: BearerValidator
sections.invariant: bearer tokens are compared by hash and plaintext is never retained; a wrong/absent token is 401; a WS-upgrade GET with a valid token passes while a non-upgrade GET and PUT/DELETE without auth are rejected; OPTIONS preflight is exempt; the previous key is accepted during rotation.
sections.threat: auth bypass or token leakage via retained plaintext.

sections.name: 3 public bind auth enforcement
sections.invariant: on a public bind `get_peers` requires a bearer, a plain GET without upgrade is rejected, and a WS-upgrade GET is rejected without a bearer but not unauthorized with one.
sections.threat: unauthenticated access to peer/topology data.

sections.name: client_ip_from_request
sections.invariant: `X-Forwarded-For` is honored ONLY when the proxy-ack env is set; otherwise the socket IP is used.
sections.threat: IP spoofing to evade rate limits or forge a request origin.

sections.name: serialize_peer_info
sections.invariant: on a public bind peer info is metadata-minimized (sensitive fields redacted) by default and exposed only on loopback or under an explicit override; the public response shape is privacy-safe.
sections.threat: leaking peer IPs/topology that deanonymize the network.

sections.name: rpc_clamp_audit_range
sections.invariant: audit/range RPCs clamp the span to the max audit block span and reject inverted or oversized ranges, saturating near `u64::MAX`.
sections.threat: a resource-exhaustion DoS via an enormous range scan.

sections.name: submit_block
sections.invariant: both reject garbage/empty hex and enforce a hex-length cap; an already-known block returns already-known.
sections.threat: a malformed or oversized payload crashes or floods the node.

sections.name: 8 nullifier / spark serial spent queries
sections.invariant: `is_nullifier_spent` and `is_spark_serial_spent` require a 32-byte hex argument, rejecting too-long/non-32-byte/non-hex input.
sections.threat: a malformed key-image query panics or bypasses validation.

sections.name: 9 block/tx read methods + param validation
sections.invariant: `get_block_by_height` / `get_block_by_hash` / `get_transaction` validate their params (string/negative/no-params/`0x`-prefix/non-hex/too-long/future height) and return well-formed errors rather than panicking; an unknown method returns a JSON-RPC error.
sections.threat: a malformed query 500s or is silently mishandled.

sections.name: 10 info / supply / stratum posture reporting
sections.invariant: `get_info` / `get_blockchain_info` / `get_supply_info` expose the full documented field set, supply decimals preserve values above `u64`, and the info reports the runtime hardening and stratum posture honestly (hardened vs unhardened by bind/TLS).
sections.threat: a misreported supply, or a falsely "hardened" posture masking an exposed node.

sections.name: get_block_template
sections.invariant: `get_block_template` embeds the correct network magic (mapping back to a known network) per chain, the deprecated `get_decoys` returns a deprecation error, and decoy locators are bound to a snapshot.
sections.threat: a cross-network template mined, or a stale/unbound decoy set leaking correlation.

sections.name: generate_self_signed_cert
sections.invariant: generates an ECDSA P-256 self-signed cert + key only when absent, with a valid future expiry.
sections.threat: an unexpected regeneration silently breaks a client's pinned fingerprint.

sections.name: set_restrictive_permissions
sections.invariant: the private-key file is written owner-only.
sections.threat: a world-readable RPC key leaks the server's TLS identity.

sections.name: load_pem_cert_and_key
sections.invariant: parses PKCS8/PKCS1/SEC1 key tags and rejects empty or missing PEM blocks.
sections.threat: silently loading no key or a garbage key → server comes up with broken TLS.

sections.name: load_server_tls_config
sections.invariant: builds the rustls server config from the loaded cert/key pair.
sections.threat: a misconfigured server config serves without the intended cert.

sections.name: load_client_tls_config
sections.invariant: a pinned fingerprint is enforced and a mismatch is rejected, an invalid fingerprint string errors, and the no-pin path uses default verification.
sections.threat: a MITM cert accepted because pinning is bypassed or mis-compared.

sections.name: cert_fingerprint
sections.invariant: computes the BLAKE3 certificate fingerprint used for pin comparison.
sections.threat: a wrong digest breaks the pin match on both ends.

sections.name: BlockInfo
sections.invariant: serializes and deserializes with no field loss or wire-shape change.
sections.threat: wire drift breaks explorer/wallet block parsing.

sections.name: BalanceInfo
sections.invariant: stable serde roundtrip.
sections.threat: a client misreads a balance field.

sections.name: TransactionInfo
sections.invariant: stable serde roundtrip.
sections.threat: tx fields silently reordered/renamed on the wire.

sections.name: UtxoInfo
sections.invariant: stable serde roundtrip.
sections.threat: a wallet miscounts spendable outputs.

sections.name: TransferRequest
sections.invariant: stable serde roundtrip for the send-request payload.
sections.threat: a malformed request field is silently accepted.

sections.name: NetworkInfo
sections.invariant: optional fields serialize distinctly as `null` versus `0`.
sections.threat: a client conflates "unknown" with "zero".

sections.name: 7 error code contract
sections.invariant: RPC error codes match the JSON-RPC contract constants.
sections.threat: a client cannot distinguish error classes.

sections.name: SubscriptionManager::subscribe
sections.invariant: subscription creation enforces the per-client and global caps atomically, with no TOCTOU window under concurrent subscribes.
sections.threat: memory-exhaustion DoS via unbounded subscriptions.

sections.name: broadcast
sections.invariant: an event reaches only subscribers of its event type plus the global receiver, and a lagging/full receiver never stalls the others.
sections.threat: cross-subscription leakage, or one slow client wedging the broadcast fan-out.

sections.name: unsubscribe
sections.invariant: unsubscribe decrements the client count and removes the entry at zero.
sections.threat: leaked subscription slots let a client evade the per-client cap.

sections.name: Event
sections.invariant: `new_block` / `new_transaction` / `sync_progress` / `wallet_update` build correctly-typed, serializable events.
sections.threat: a mislabeled event is routed to the wrong subscribers.

sections.name: WsMessage
sections.invariant: subscribe/unsubscribe/ping deserialize and bad or unknown control messages are rejected.
sections.threat: a malformed control frame confuses or crashes the handler.

sections.name: subscription_count
sections.invariant: accessors report accurate live counts and hand out a working global receiver.
sections.threat: inaccurate accounting undercounts against the caps.

sections.name: compute_root
sections.invariant: one root definition shared by `new` / `open_with_db` / `append` / `rewind`, so an identical kernel set yields an identical root regardless of construction path.
sections.threat: a fresh vs replayed empty store diverging (the latent bug this fixes — `new` once hard-coded `[0;32]`).

sections.name: append
sections.invariant: a kernel is appended at its dense vector index and mirrored to `mw_kernels`; a borsh-serialize or RocksDB write failure PANICS (with structured context) rather than continuing in-memory-only.
sections.threat: **R-61** — a silent persistence gap diverges the replayed kernel set from the committed `mw_kernel_root` after restart.

sections.name: checkpoint_at_height
sections.invariant: a checkpoint records the pre-block `kernels_len`; the stack caps at `MAX_REORG_CHECKPOINTS` (1000); `checkpoint_count` feeds the chain's cross-store invariant (shielded/spark/kernel stacks must agree in length).
sections.threat: uneven cross-store unwind leaving the three Phase-2 stores at different effective heights.

sections.name: rewind
sections.invariant: pops the guarding checkpoint, truncates kernels to `kernels_len` BEFORE recomputing the root (in-memory ordering is crash-safe), then removes the dropped keys `split_at..old_len` from `mw_kernels`; empty stack ⇒ `false`; per-item remove failures are surfaced loudly (not silently discarded).
sections.threat: **R-62** — a crash mid-rewind leaving in-memory root and on-disk kernels inconsistent (documented atomicity gap, batch-delete deferred); **R-63** — orphan kernels replayed on next open corrupt the committed root.

sections.name: open_with_db
sections.invariant: a reopened store replays `mw_kernels` in key order into the rewound (not pre-rewind) state; the in-memory-only checkpoint stack starts empty (no rewind past a restart); repeated per-session reorgs leave no cruft.
sections.threat: reorg cruft over-counting kernels after restart.

sections.name: 6 concurrency / lock graph
sections.invariant: `kernels` → `root` and `checkpoints` → `kernels` → `root` are a strict acquisition order with no cycle; concurrent readers + writer(s) never deadlock or panic.
sections.threat: a lock-order cycle hanging block processing.

sections.name: can_prune
sections.invariant: a protected block is never prunable; `Archive` prunes nothing; `KeepRecent(n)` keeps the `n`-block recency window via `saturating_sub`; `Custom` honors `min_blocks`, `keep_after_height`, and checkpoint protection.
sections.threat: a still-needed block pruned away.

sections.name: can_prune
sections.invariant: checkpoint protection is gated on `checkpoint_interval > 0`, so `height % interval` never divides by zero; interval 0 means "no checkpoint protection."
sections.threat: **R-59** — a `PruningRules{ checkpoint_interval: 0 }` caller panics on the hot pruning-decision path, taking down the prune thread.

sections.name: prunable_heights
sections.invariant: `prunable_heights` returns exactly the `can_prune` heights in a half-open `from..to` window (empty/inverted ranges yield nothing, no panic); `estimate_savings` is an O(1) per-mode estimate consistent with the recency/min-blocks boundary.
sections.threat: an over-aggressive plan, or a div-by-zero / overflow in the estimate.

sections.name: record_prune
sections.invariant: prune counters accumulate monotonically and `last_pruned_height` tracks the most recent prune; the clock read uses `unwrap_or(0)` for pre-epoch safety (never panics).
sections.threat: A6-CLOCK — a system-clock anomaly panicking the stats update.

sections.name: create_plan
sections.invariant: the plan starts after `last_pruned_height`, is archive-empty, and is bounded by `batch_size` and the mode's max-prune height.
sections.threat: **R-60** — a drifted `last_pruned_height` re-prunes or strands blocks; mitigated because `db/pruning.rs::execute_plan` (R-36) only bumps the counter after both writes succeed.

sections.name: append_commitment
sections.invariant: appends assign dense positions `0..tree_size` and are mirrored to `shielded_entries`; a nullifier already present is rejected as a double-spend and never re-inserted; the root changes on every append.
sections.threat: shielded double-spend, or an anchor/root that omits a minted note.

sections.name: append_commitment
sections.invariant: a borsh-serialize failure or a RocksDB write failure on a consensus commitment/nullifier PANICS rather than continuing with in-memory-only state.
sections.threat: **R-61** — a silent persistence gap diverges the replayed tree from the committed anchor after restart.

sections.name: checkpoint_at_height
sections.invariant: the side-table checkpoint is pushed ONLY if the BridgeTree accepted its own checkpoint (`tree_checkpointed` gate), both are held under one guard, and both cap at `MAX_CHECKPOINTS` (1000, covering testnet max_reorg_depth); a non-monotonic id is declined by both.
sections.threat: **R-65** — the two stacks desync so `rewind` rolls the side tables to a boundary the tree never reverts to.

sections.name: rewind
sections.invariant: a rewind pops the side-table checkpoint, rewinds the BridgeTree, drops entries at positions `>= entries_len`, drops nullifiers spent at height `>= restore.height`, AND removes both from the backing column families; empty stack ⇒ `false`; a tree/side-table desync still aligns the side tables (warn) since leaving them ahead is strictly worse.
sections.threat: after a reorg, `tree_size` over-counts, disconnected nullifiers read as spent, and a restart replay resurrects the disconnected block.

sections.name: open_with_db
sections.invariant: a reopened store replays `shielded_entries` in position order and `shielded_nullifiers`, reconstructing an identical root and nullifier set; the in-memory-only checkpoint stack starts empty (no rewind past a restart).
sections.threat: durability regression — a restarted node diverges from the on-disk state.

sections.name: witness_path
sections.invariant: `entry_at` is dense over `0..tree_size` and `None` at/after the frontier; a marked leaf's authentication path survives later appends and spans the full tree depth.
sections.threat: a spend proof anchors against a wrong or stale path.

sections.name: compute_root
sections.invariant: one root definition shared by `new` / `open_with_db` / `add_coin` / `rewind`, so an identical coin set produces an identical root regardless of construction path (fresh, replayed, forward-appended, or rewound).
sections.threat: a fresh vs replayed empty store diverging (the latent bug `rewind` would have made reachable).

sections.name: add_coin
sections.invariant: each coin is appended in `coin_id` order and each spent serial records its spend height; both are mirrored to disk; a spent serial reads back as spent (double-spend surface).
sections.threat: Spark serial/coin double-spend, or a root that omits a minted coin.

sections.name: add_coin
sections.invariant: a borsh-serialize or RocksDB write failure on a consensus coin/serial PANICS rather than continuing in-memory-only.
sections.threat: **R-61** — a silent persistence gap diverges the replayed accumulator from the committed root after restart.

sections.name: checkpoint_at_height
sections.invariant: a checkpoint records `(height, coins_len)` taken BEFORE the block applies; the stack caps at `MAX_REORG_CHECKPOINTS` (1000); heights are strictly monotonic in production.
sections.threat: **R-67** — a height regression means the orchestrator pushed when it should have rewound (consensus ordering bug), breaking the rewind restore math; logged at error level.

sections.name: rewind
sections.invariant: pops the guarding checkpoint and truncates coins to `coins_len`, drops serials spent at height `>= restore_height`, recomputes the root via §1, and removes the dropped coins/serials from the backing column families; empty stack ⇒ `false`; locks taken coins → serials → root (no cycle vs `add_coin`).
sections.threat: a reorg leaving coins/serials/root or on-disk state ahead of the tree, resurrected on restart.

sections.name: open_with_db
sections.invariant: a reopened store replays coins by `coin_id` and serials, reconstructing the rewound (not pre-rewind) state; the in-memory-only checkpoint stack starts empty on open (no rewind past a restart); coin-id reuse across a shorter fork leaves no orphaned coins on disk.
sections.threat: reorg cruft over-counting the accumulator after restart.

sections.name: 7 concurrency / lock graph
sections.invariant: the `RwLock`-guarded fields compose without a lock-order cycle under concurrent readers + writer(s); nothing panics or corrupts.
sections.threat: a deadlock edge that would hang block processing under RPC read load.

sections.name: add_output
sections.invariant: every output lands in all five indexes (primary, height, locator, stealth, output_index); the stealth/output indexes keep the OLDEST output per stealth address (`or_insert` oldest-wins), so an immature/colliding coinbase can never displace a mature entry; `is_coinbase` is carried for maturity checks.
sections.threat: CRIT-5/HIGH-4 — a ring member bypasses coinbase maturity, or a later output steals an earlier one's index slot.

sections.name: spend_output
sections.invariant: key-image insert is check-then-set atomic under the caller's write lock (second attempt ⇒ `false`); removing the output also clears its height and stealth entries — no dangling references.
sections.threat: A6-STEALTH-IDX — a stale stealth entry lets a spent coinbase satisfy a maturity check.

sections.name: mark_key_image_spent
sections.invariant: ring-sig chains record only the key image (output stays in the set as a decoy); double-mark ⇒ `false`; removal un-marks for disconnect.
sections.threat: double-spend admitted, or a reorg leaves an input permanently unspendable.

sections.name: remove_output
sections.invariant: the stealth / output_index entry is cleared ONLY when it actually references the removed key (`stealth_index.get == Some(&key)`), and the removal is propagated to the on-disk `output_index`.
sections.threat: **H2** cross-node divergence + frozen funds — a colliding coinbase disconnect erasing the victim's oldest-wins entry makes the victim's output vanish on reorged nodes and splits the chain; **R-68** — an on-disk entry surviving a reorg lets a disconnected UTXO act as a valid decoy on other nodes.

sections.name: locator_index
sections.invariant: `(height, ordinal)` is stable and insertion-order-independent (BTreeSet ordering); entries survive spends and are dropped only on disconnect; duplicate or out-of-range locators are rejected.
sections.threat: decoy set diverges between nodes ⇒ ring-member validation forks the chain.

sections.name: total_outputs_ever
sections.invariant: `total_outputs_ever` is MONOTONIC (never decrements, even on reorg); reorg disconnects are counted separately so availability = `ever − disconnects` is reorg-history-independent.
sections.threat: **L2** — decrementing on reorg made two nodes on the same tip compute different ring sizes (ring-size determinism launch-blocker).

sections.name: evict_old_outputs
sections.invariant: eviction keeps only the `keep_depth` window in memory (older fall back to on-disk DB); `checkpoint` persists key_images + output_index and returns Err if ANY per-item write failed (no silent partial checkpoint).
sections.threat: **R-70** — a partial checkpoint reported Ok, then a restart admits a double-spend (lost key_image) or a stale ring member (lost output_index).

sections.name: apply_batch
sections.invariant: connect and disconnect batches are EXACT inverses (outputs + key-image state restored); order is add → spend → remove → un-mark.
sections.threat: **R-71** — the batch is NON-atomic (sequential loop, no txn boundary): a panic mid-batch leaves partial mutations; do not assume all-or-nothing.

sections.name: next_batch_range
sections.invariant: a batch never runs past `target_height` and returns `None` once caught up, paused, or stopped, so sync only advances while actively syncing.
sections.threat: scanning past the tip or a busy-loop after a stop.

sections.name: update_progress
sections.invariant: progress counters and `blocks_per_second` reflect the work done and surface stashed error/reorg state to the UI.
sections.threat: a stalled or mis-reported sync the operator cannot diagnose.

sections.name: rewind_to
sections.invariant: on a reorg the manager only moves `current_height` backward (forward targets are a no-op) and re-enters `Syncing` so it re-scans from the new height, even from a prior `Complete` state.
sections.threat: stale/lost owned outputs kept after a chain reorg.

sections.name: scan_block_v2
sections.invariant: the default reorg-aware wrapper delegates to legacy `scan_block` and reports `Scanned`, so non-reorg scanners keep working unchanged.
sections.threat: a silent behavior change for legacy scanners.

sections.name: handle_reorg_recovery
sections.invariant: recovery hooks fail closed by default (`Err` / zero position), so a scanner that has not wired the full rewind machinery cannot silently fast-skip recovery.
sections.threat: a half-implemented scanner corrupting wallet state on a reorg.

sections.name: try_reorg_recovery
sections.invariant: a resolved fork point rewinds the scanner and returns stats (with `reorg_at_height` backfilled); a fork point below the searchable window returns `Ok(None)` to force a full rescan rather than a partial recovery.
sections.threat: resuming on a divergent chain and keeping orphaned outputs.

sections.name: record_reorg_stats
sections.invariant: reorg stats are stashed and surfaced through the next `progress()` so the UI can render the reorg banner.
sections.threat: a silent balance change with no user notification.

sections.name: spendable
sections.invariant: a UTXO counts as spendable only if it is unspent, past `min_age` (coinbase maturity), past its `lock_height`, and not held by an active reservation; the age check uses `saturating_add` so it never underflows an immature output into the spendable set.
sections.threat: spending an immature/locked/reserved output → invalid or double-spending tx.

sections.name: total
sections.invariant: sums only unspent UTXOs (including immature + reserved, which still belong to the wallet) with a saturating fold so a crafted overflow cannot panic or wrap.
sections.threat: negative/overflowed balance or double counting.

sections.name: available_utxos
sections.invariant: the available set is exactly the spendable UTXOs; locked reports unspent outputs still held back by `lock_height`, with no overlap or double counting.
sections.threat: offering a locked output for selection.

sections.name: reserve_utxos
sections.invariant: reservation is atomic — if ANY requested UTXO is already reserved the call returns `Err` and inserts nothing; expiry is honored dynamically at the block boundary and a reserved UTXO is excluded from selection.
sections.threat: two in-flight txs selecting the same input → double spend.

sections.name: release_reservations_by_tx
sections.invariant: release affects only the caller's `by_tx`; expired reservations are swept; restore skips already-expired entries.
sections.threat: freeing another tx's inputs or resurrecting stale reservations.

sections.name: remove_outputs
sections.invariant: a reorg rewind drops orphaned UTXOs while also clearing the key-image reverse index and any reservation; missing keys are skipped silently; `mark_spent` clears the satisfied reservation.
sections.threat: stale UTXO or a dead reverse-index pointer surviving a reorg.

sections.name: add_utxo
sections.invariant: the key-image reverse index stays consistent — a duplicate key replaces without double counting, `lookup` hides spent UTXOs yet the index entry survives so a reorg can `unmark` (restore) the spend.
sections.threat: index corruption leaving funds unrecoverable after a reorg.

sections.name: ChurnConfig::validate
sections.invariant: rejects a zero or inverted interval window, any `*_amount_pct` outside `1..=100` (or `min > max`), and an empty `node_url`, so the engine can never start with a nonsensical schedule.
sections.threat: a churn loop that never fires or self-sends 0%/>100%.

sections.name: next_interval_secs
sections.invariant: an exponential draw is clamped to the configured `[min, max]` window and sampled from `OsRng`, keeping the privacy-affecting timing unpredictable yet bounded.
sections.threat: predictable or out-of-window churn timing aiding traffic analysis.

sections.name: pick_churn_amount
sections.invariant: percentage math is done in u128 (no overflow), the drawn amount stays within `[min_pct, max_pct]`, a fee reserve is always kept back (`amount + fee <= spendable`), and a zero balance yields 0.
sections.threat: an over-spend leaving no fee, or an arithmetic overflow.

sections.name: execute_churn
sections.invariant: the churn is a self-send to the wallet's own current keys (value is preserved, not leaked), requires at least 2 mature UTXOs, and caps the amount by both mature-spendable and the two-largest-input sum.
sections.threat: deanonymizing the wallet or spending immature outputs.

sections.name: ChurnEngine::new
sections.invariant: construction re-validates the config and builds the node coordinator up front; `stats` returns a consistent locked clone.
sections.threat: an engine running against an invalid config or a torn stats read.

sections.name: run
sections.invariant: the loop checks the shutdown flag before and after each sleep, and accumulates completed/failed/total counters with saturating adds.
sections.threat: churn continuing after shutdown, or a stats counter overflow.

sections.name: real-set match
sections.invariant: the supplied real outputs must equal the request's real locators as an ordered set.
sections.threat: substituting or reordering the real member being spent.

sections.name: real identity binding
sections.invariant: each real output's resolved public key and commitment must equal the wallet-supplied identity, and no two reals may share a public key.
sections.threat: a forged or mismatched real member slips into the ring.

sections.name: candidate filtering
sections.invariant: decoys above `max_decoy_height` (min-age) or locked at the spend height are excluded.
sections.threat: immature or locked decoys produce invalid rings or leak spend timing.

sections.name: identity-point exclusion
sections.invariant: an all-zero (identity-point) public key or commitment is never placed in a ring, mirroring the CLSAG verifier.
sections.threat: the genesis placeholder in a ring fails the whole input's signature.

sections.name: decoy uniqueness / sufficiency
sections.invariant: each decoy public key is used at most once across the transaction; too few candidates or a size overflow are rejected, never panicked.
sections.threat: cross-ring decoy reuse links inputs.

sections.name: real member placement
sections.invariant: every ring has the same ring size and the real member sits at a uniformly random secret index within bounds.
sections.threat: a predictable real position defeats ring privacy; ring-size divergence (incident 1d27d3c8).

sections.name: snapshot-stage variants
sections.invariant: every malformed-snapshot condition (policy, height ordering, bucket bounds, pool overflow) has a distinct fail-closed variant.
sections.threat: silently sampling from an invalid distribution.

sections.name: request-stage variants
sections.invariant: malformed covered requests (missing/duplicate real, out-of-snapshot, capacity/size overflow, ring size) each map to a specific variant.
sections.threat: building a ring from an invalid request.

sections.name: response-stage variants
sections.invariant: a mismatched node response (snapshot, length, locator, height) yields a distinct rejection.
sections.threat: accepting a substituted or reordered response.

sections.name: allocation-stage variants
sections.invariant: every allocation failure (real-set/identity mismatch, duplicate real key, ring size/count/input mismatch) is a distinct variant.
sections.threat: emitting a ring that fails to bind the real member.

sections.name: InsufficientDecoys
sections.invariant: an undersized eligible pool is reported with available/needed counts, never panicked.
sections.threat: an under-mixed ring or a panic.

sections.name: From<DecoySelectionError> for WalletError
sections.invariant: each variant maps to a stable `WalletError` category while preserving its message.
sections.threat: losing error context at the wallet boundary.

sections.name: sample_candidate_locators
sections.invariant: decoy ages are drawn from the Gamma(19.28, 1/1.61) log-seconds age distribution (converted to blocks), so the real spend's age is statistically indistinguishable from its decoys.
sections.threat: biased age sampling makes the real input identifiable by age; ring-selection determinism regressions (incident 1d27d3c8).

sections.name: min_age eligibility
sections.invariant: only outputs at least `min_age` blocks old, measured at the next spend height, are eligible as decoys.
sections.threat: too-young decoys shrink the anonymity set and leak spend timing.

sections.name: build_covered_request
sections.invariant: real locators are padded with unique decoys up to `COVERED_LOOKUP_SIZE`, shuffled, and bound to the snapshot id and ring policy.
sections.threat: unbound or duplicated locators reveal which ring member is real.

sections.name: request bounds
sections.invariant: real locators must exist in the snapshot and required slots must not exceed `COVERED_LOOKUP_SIZE`.
sections.threat: out-of-snapshot or overflowing requests yield malformed rings.

sections.name: pick_nearest_locator
sections.invariant: a sampled target age maps to the nearest eligible height, breaking ties uniformly at random.
sections.threat: deterministic tie-breaking biases decoy positions.

sections.name: pick_ordinal
sections.invariant: every chosen decoy is unique — never a real, excluded, or already-selected output.
sections.threat: duplicate/real reuse links the transaction's inputs.

sections.name: policy version
sections.invariant: a snapshot is rejected unless its `policy_version` equals `DECOY_LOCATOR_POLICY_VERSION`.
sections.threat: sampling under a stale or foreign locator policy.

sections.name: spend_height derivation
sections.invariant: spend height is `snapshot_height + 1` with the increment overflow-guarded.
sections.threat: an overflow or wrong spend height corrupts all age math.

sections.name: non-empty buckets
sections.invariant: every height bucket must have a count greater than zero.
sections.threat: an empty bucket breaks selection and cumulative counts.

sections.name: strictly increasing heights
sections.invariant: bucket heights are strictly increasing.
sections.threat: unordered buckets break binary search and the cumulative-count index.

sections.name: height <= snapshot
sections.invariant: no bucket height exceeds the snapshot height.
sections.threat: future outputs enter the decoy pool.

sections.name: cumulative counts
sections.invariant: prefix output counts accumulate without `usize` overflow (`PoolSizeOverflow` guarded).
sections.threat: overflow miscounts the eligible pool.

sections.name: SnapshotId
sections.invariant: snapshot identity (height, hash, policy version) is shared by snapshot, request and response, so all three refer to the same chain state.
sections.threat: mixing metadata from different snapshots.

sections.name: ValidatedDecoySnapshot::eligible_*
sections.invariant: eligible height and output counts include only heights `<= spend_height - min_age`, via prefix cumulative counts.
sections.threat: an off-by-one admits too-young outputs.

sections.name: contains_locator
sections.invariant: a locator is in-snapshot only if its height exists and its ordinal is below that height's count.
sections.threat: accepting a real locator outside the snapshot.

sections.name: RingPolicy::try_new
sections.invariant: ring size must be at least 2, and the policy captures ring size and `min_output_age` together.
sections.threat: a degenerate ring size (0 or 1) provides no privacy.

sections.name: CoveredRequest
sections.invariant: constructible only by the sampling module; it guarantees a `COVERED_LOOKUP_SIZE` set of unique locators that contains every real locator.
sections.threat: pairing arbitrary locators with an unrelated snapshot or policy.

sections.name: AllocatedRing
sections.invariant: rings are constructible only by the allocator, fixing a uniform ring size and the real member's secret position.
sections.threat: hand-built rings bypassing the decoy invariants.

sections.name: snapshot match
sections.invariant: the response's snapshot id must equal the request's.
sections.threat: a response resolved against a different snapshot.

sections.name: length match
sections.invariant: the response output count equals the requested locator count.
sections.threat: a truncated or padded response.

sections.name: locator match
sections.invariant: each output's locator equals the requested locator in order.
sections.threat: reordered or substituted outputs.

sections.name: height match
sections.invariant: each output's redundant height field matches its locator height.
sections.threat: inconsistent output metadata.

sections.name: unique index
sections.invariant: the locator→index map is built from unique locators.
sections.threat: duplicate locators alias distinct outputs.

sections.name: validate_covered_response
sections.invariant: a `ValidatedCoveredResponse` is returned only when snapshot, cardinality, ordering and heights all pass (fail-closed).
sections.threat: a partially-validated response reaches allocation.

sections.name: TxStatus::from_confirmations
sections.invariant: status derives from confirmation count against `unlock_height`, and a record is spendable only once confirmed AND unlocked.
sections.threat: showing locked/unconfirmed funds as available.

sections.name: incoming
sections.invariant: each record captures its direction, amount, and fee at construction so aggregates stay correct.
sections.threat: a mislabeled record skewing totals.

sections.name: add
sections.invariant: the store is consistent and `recent` honors its limit/ordering for pagination.
sections.threat: dropped or mis-ordered history entries.

sections.name: remove_incoming_outputs
sections.invariant: incoming records whose `tx_hash` appears in the orphaned-output list are removed, deduped by `tx_hash`, and the pass is idempotent.
sections.threat: stale incoming history surviving a reorg.

sections.name: revert_outgoing_above_height
sections.invariant: outgoing records confirmed above `new_height` reset to pending (`block_height = 0`) while incoming records are left untouched, so a re-scan can re-confirm them.
sections.threat: an orphaned confirmation shown as final.

sections.name: mark_spent_by_key_image
sections.invariant: the spent flag is set/cleared by key image, and unmark restores records whose spend came from a now-orphaned block.
sections.threat: history showing a spend that the canonical chain no longer contains.

sections.name: total_received
sections.invariant: totals sum only matching-direction records, and `has_address` is a bookkeeping helper over explicitly-tagged `recipient_address` fields, NOT a privacy gate (R-91).
sections.threat: relying on `has_address` for address- reuse protection and missing an untagged incoming address.

sections.name: ScopedViewKey::from_epoch
sections.invariant: a scoped view key covers exactly the inclusive `[from_height, to_height]` block range and nothing outside it (an inverted range covers nothing).
sections.threat: over-broad scope would disclose transaction history beyond what the holder voluntarily surrendered (e.g. a tax year).

sections.name: ScopedViewKey::to_json
sections.invariant: the exported JSON carries the scope bounds plus the spend/view public keys and the scoped view secret.
sections.threat: a malformed export would fail to reconstruct the scoped view capability at the auditor's side.

sections.name: ViewOnlyEpoch
sections.invariant: a view-only epoch structurally carries the view secret and only the PUBLIC spend key — no spend secret exists to sign with.
sections.threat: any spend-secret material here would let a view-only export spend.

sections.name: KeyEpoch
sections.invariant: a full epoch pairs a spend keypair with a view keypair; secrets are wiped via the field `SecretKey` drop chain (the custom `Drop` only clears the non-secret `epoch` field).
sections.threat: R-72 — relying on a phantom defense-in-depth wipe that does not exist.

sections.name: SpendKey::to_full_viewing_key
sections.invariant: the FVK is a deterministic function of the spend key — the same `SpendKey` always derives the same `ak`/`nk`/`rivk`.
sections.threat: non-determinism would make an FVK un-reproducible, breaking auditor hand-off and recovery.

sections.name: FullViewingKey::to_incoming_viewing_key
sections.invariant: IVK and OVK are distinct deterministic derivations from the FVK, and the IVK scalar exposes no path back to the master spend key.
sections.threat: if a view-only key derived spend authority, sharing an audit key would surrender spend power.

sections.name: IncomingViewingKey::to_payment_address
sections.invariant: distinct diversifiers yield distinct, unlinkable payment addresses that all funnel to the one wallet.
sections.threat: colliding/linkable diversified addresses would deanonymize the recipient across payments.

sections.name: IncomingViewingKey::view_tag
sections.invariant: the 1-byte view tag is a deterministic function of the IVK and ephemeral key.
sections.threat: a non-deterministic tag would make fast-scan reject the recipient's own outputs.

sections.name: PaymentAddress::to_bech32
sections.invariant: encode/decode round-trips exactly and a corrupted bech32m checksum is rejected, not silently accepted.
sections.threat: a mangled address accepted as valid could send funds to a wrong or burn destination.

sections.name: SpendKey::to_spark_spend_key
sections.invariant: the Spark scan key detects incoming Spark coins but cannot spend them, and Spark addresses round-trip with checksum tamper rejected.
sections.threat: a scan key that could spend, or a silently-mangled Spark address, breaks the exchange/auditor custody boundary.

sections.name: BlockDigest::from_block
sections.invariant: a digest is an output-only summary and scanning is local, so a range request leaks only the block height RANGE to the server, never the wallet's address set (strictly stronger than BIP-157; see `docs/security/LIGHTSYNC_AUDIT.md`).
sections.threat: address-set deanonymization by the serving node.

sections.name: scan_digest
sections.invariant: only outputs that pass the view-tag prefilter AND ECDH-decrypt as ours are returned, each with its amount and canonical locator; empty scan keys find nothing without panicking.
sections.threat: false-positive ownership or a panic on an empty key set.

sections.name: scan_output_digest
sections.invariant: a forged encrypted amount is dropped, a subaddress match preserves its index, and a coinbase plaintext amount is read correctly.
sections.threat: crediting a forged amount or losing the subaddress attribution.

sections.name: scan_digests_parallel
sections.invariant: the batch is validated for height contiguity and `prev_hash` linkage BEFORE any scan, and an invalid batch returns `Err` leaving `last_scanned` untouched.
sections.threat: advancing past unscanned blocks (missed owned outputs) on a gapped/forged batch.

sections.name: SyncCheckpoint::authenticate
sections.invariant: a server checkpoint is trusted for fast-skip only when its hash matches a hardcoded `CONSENSUS_CHECKPOINTS` entry (`Authenticated`); a mismatch is `Forged` and an unknown height is `Unverifiable`, both of which must fall back to a full scan.
sections.threat: a forged checkpoint making the wallet skip real blocks and miss owned incoming txs.

sections.name: SyncCheckpoint::verify_hash
sections.invariant: computes a self-consistency hash only (tamper on any field changes it); it proves integrity in transit, NOT authenticity — that is §5's job.
sections.threat: mistaking a self-consistent but forged checkpoint for a trusted one.

sections.name: estimate_bandwidth
sections.invariant: byte estimate scales linearly with block count and average outputs per block.
sections.threat: a wildly wrong budget that breaks the per-request cap.

sections.name: LightSyncStats
sections.invariant: scan stats accumulate across digests (including coinbase); a known lock-height correctness hole is pinned by a regression test.
sections.threat: silent miscount of found outputs.

sections.name: WalletMnemonic::generate
sections.invariant: produces a valid 24-word (256-bit entropy) BIP39 mnemonic that re-parses successfully.
sections.threat: a malformed generated phrase would be un-restorable, orphaning the wallet.

sections.name: WalletMnemonic::from_phrase
sections.invariant: the BIP39 checksum and wordlist are enforced — a bad-checksum, out-of-wordlist, or empty phrase is rejected, never silently accepted.
sections.threat: accepting a corrupt phrase derives a wrong wallet and silently loses funds.

sections.name: WalletMnemonic::to_seed
sections.invariant: seed derivation is deterministic — same phrase + passphrase → same 64-byte seed; a different passphrase → a different seed.
sections.threat: non-deterministic seeds break reproducible recovery.

sections.name: WalletSeed::from_bytes
sections.invariant: a seed is exactly 64 bytes and splits into a 32-byte master key + 32-byte chain code; non-64-byte input is a flagged corruption path (R-78).
sections.threat: silent zero-pad/truncate would derive wrong keys with no error.

sections.name: DerivationPath
sections.invariant: all path components are hardened, and parse ↔ render is faithful (`m/44'/888'/…`).
sections.threat: M-6 — an unhardened or mis-rendered path misleads external BIP32 tools and diagnostics.

sections.name: derive_child_key
sections.invariant: HD derivation is deterministic and path-sensitive — distinct paths from one seed yield distinct child keys.
sections.threat: path collisions would reuse addresses / cross-link accounts.

sections.name: generate_shares
sections.invariant: keygen parameters are validated — `threshold >= 2`, `total >= threshold`, `total <= 255` — so only a genuine t-of-n scheme is produced.
sections.threat: a degenerate `1-of-1` or `t > n` "multisig" would silently drop the threshold guarantee.

sections.name: verify_shares
sections.invariant: every share must agree on the group config; a tampered `group_public_key` is rejected.
sections.threat: mismatched shares would build an unusable or attacker-substituted group key.

sections.name: signing_round1
