sections.invariant: a valid signature requires a full quorum of the threshold; a below-threshold or duplicate-participant set does not yield a verifying signature.
sections.threat: partial/insufficient signatures forging a spend below quorum.

sections.name: signing_round2
sections.invariant: `Round1Secret` is consumed by value so FROST nonces are used at most once, and signing with a mismatched round-1 secret never yields a valid group signature.
sections.threat: nonce reuse leaks a participant's signing share (RFC 9591).

sections.name: verify_signature
sections.invariant: a signature verifies only against the exact message it signed.
sections.threat: message malleability would let a signature authorize a different transaction.

sections.name: reconstruct_group_secret
sections.invariant: Lagrange interpolation over any threshold-sized subset reconstructs the SAME secret (the discrete log of the group key); signing shares must be exactly 32 bytes and duplicate participant IDs are rejected.
sections.threat: silent share truncation (C35) or a degenerate basis producing a wrong key.

sections.name: clsag_sign_multisig
sections.invariant: the reconstruct-sign-zeroize path produces a standard CLSAG signature that verifies against the ring and pseudo-output, indistinguishable from single-signer, and fails a different message.
sections.threat: a threshold spend that fails to verify (funds stuck) or leaks the transiently-held group key.

sections.name: new
sections.invariant: an empty/whitespace endpoint is rejected, and any `COINCYNC_RPC_API_KEY` is attached as a sensitive `Authorization: Bearer` header that never prints in logs.
sections.threat: unauthenticated or misconfigured client silently talking to the wrong node.

sections.name: submit_transaction
sections.invariant: a node result is mapped to exactly one of `Accepted`, definitive `Rejected`, or retryable `Unknown`; a remote JSON-RPC error is a definitive rejection while transport/protocol failures stay `Unknown`.
sections.threat: a rejected tx treated as accepted (funds/inputs mis-tracked), or a maybe-delivered tx treated as failed (double submission).

sections.name: submission_was_accepted
sections.invariant: acceptance is recognized from either a bare `true` or `{"accepted": true}`; anything else is not accepted.
sections.threat: ambiguous node reply read as success.

sections.name: submission_rejection_reason
sections.invariant: the human-readable reason is preferred (`reason`/`message`/`error`), so operators see why a tx was rejected.
sections.threat: opaque rejections that hide a fee/validity problem.

sections.name: encode_transaction
sections.invariant: a local borsh/hex encoding failure is definitive (no request reached the node) so callers must not open an in-flight reservation for it.
sections.threat: phantom reservation on a tx that was never sent.

sections.name: decoy_distribution
sections.invariant: locators are resolved against the exact snapshot `(height, hash, policy_version)` they were built from, so metadata cannot be mispaired.
sections.threat: decoy set built against a stale/foreign snapshot.

sections.name: endpoint
sections.invariant: returns the configured endpoint verbatim.
sections.threat: n/a (read-only accessor).

sections.name: encrypt
sections.invariant: encryption is authenticated (XChaCha20-Poly1305) so any ciphertext tamper is rejected on decrypt rather than silently accepted.
sections.threat: an attacker mutating the wallet file to corrupt or forge secrets undetected.

sections.name: save_wallet
sections.invariant: a saved wallet round-trips losslessly, is only loadable with the correct password, and a truncated/oversized/empty body errs cleanly (no panic).
sections.threat: secrets recoverable without the password, or a malformed file crashing the loader.

sections.name: derive_key
sections.invariant: the Argon2id KDF is deterministic and stable, derives distinct keys, and errs (not panics) on a degenerate zero memory cost.
sections.threat: a weak or crashing KDF undermining at-rest encryption.

sections.name: save_v4
sections.invariant: the v4 format round-trips and rejects a tampered header or a truncated HMAC.
sections.threat: a forged v4 file passing integrity checks.

sections.name: load_wallet
sections.invariant: loading a v3 wallet and saving upgrades it to v4 while preserving contents and the wrong-password error behaviour.
sections.threat: an upgrade silently altering or weakening a wallet.

sections.name: change_password
sections.invariant: a password change is atomic across the main file and sidecars — a corrupt sidecar aborts the whole change rather than half-applying it.
sections.threat: a partial re-encryption leaving the wallet unloadable.

sections.name: save_wallet
sections.invariant: a save writes via a temp file and atomic rename, leaves no temp file on success, uses a fresh nonce and salt each save, and a crash mid-rename leaves the previous wallet loadable.
sections.threat: an interrupted save destroying the only copy of the wallet, or nonce/salt reuse.

sections.name: decrypt_sidecar_with_fallback
sections.invariant: sidecar decryption falls back to legacy v2 KDF params when the current params fail, so older sidecars remain readable.
sections.threat: an upgrade orphaning previously encrypted sidecar state.

sections.name: generate_mnemonic
sections.invariant: a generated mnemonic round-trips back to the same seed.
sections.threat: a mnemonic that cannot restore the wallet it was issued for.

sections.name: create_deniable_wallet
sections.invariant: deniable-wallet creation is disabled and writes nothing, and the loader falls back to a standard single region.
sections.threat: a half-implemented deniable mode silently persisting or exposing a hidden region.

sections.name: validate
sections.invariant: the body checksum detects corruption of an unencrypted body, and WalletData drop zeroizes the mnemonic phrase without panicking.
sections.threat: silent acceptance of corrupted plaintext state, or secret material lingering in freed memory.

sections.name: scan_output
sections.invariant: an output is attributed to the wallet IFF its one-time stealth (or subaddress) address matches under the view key, and a forged/identity commitment or corrupt encrypted amount is dropped rather than accepted.
sections.threat: mis-detecting foreign outputs as owned (phantom balance) or missing genuinely owned funds.

sections.name: scan_transaction
sections.invariant: every candidate output in a tx is scanned, and outputs past the u8 index limit (255) are skipped without panic.
sections.threat: index overflow panic or skipped owned outputs.

sections.name: scan_block_with_result
sections.invariant: a block that does not extend the current tip is recognised as a reorg (prev-hash mismatch or equal-height sibling) and triggers a journal rewind, falling back to full rescan when the fork is deeper than the journal.
sections.threat: applying a fork on top of stale state, leaving orphaned owned outputs.

sections.name: rewind_to_height
sections.invariant: a rewind removes exactly the owned outputs added above the target and unmarks exactly the spends journaled above it, in reverse application order, leaving position at the target; it errs (not silently) above the tip or outside the journal window.
sections.threat: stale or lost owned-output state after a reorg.

sections.name: record_journal_entry
sections.invariant: the per-block journal is bounded at capacity, exports height/hash pairs oldest-first, and covers the largest network reorg cap; recording a spend on an empty journal is a no-op returning false.
sections.threat: unbounded journal growth, or an un-recoverable reorg.

sections.name: scan_blocks_parallel
sections.invariant: the parallel path returns the identical decrypted-output set as the serial path, dedups duplicate txs across blocks, drops forged commitments, and does not advance on an empty slice.
sections.threat: parallelism diverging from serial detection (missed/duplicated funds).

sections.name: scan_output
sections.invariant: coinbase outputs are detected across old (plaintext) and new (ECDH, no view-tag gate) formats, a short encrypted amount yields zero rather than panicking, and coinbase to a subaddress is not mis-attributed to the primary.
sections.threat: coinbase-format confusion crediting or crashing the scanner.

sections.name: encrypt_amount
sections.invariant: amount encryption round-trips and the view tag is a deterministic fast-filter derived from the shared secret.
sections.threat: view-tag mismatch causing owned outputs to be filtered out.

sections.name: decrypted_to_utxo
sections.invariant: converting a decrypted output to a UTXO derives its key image and carries the correct lock height, account and subaddress index.
sections.threat: a wrong key image breaking spend/double-spend detection, or a lost lock height letting locked funds be spent.

sections.name: scan_and_persist
sections.invariant: the background scanner advances and persists scan state so it round-trips across a restart.
sections.threat: re-scanning from zero or losing detected outputs on restart.

sections.name: WalletSyncService::run
sections.invariant: the sync service drains its block channel and honours shutdown.
sections.threat: a stuck or never-terminating sync loop.

sections.name: set_position
sections.invariant: setting position round-trips and a rescan from the same position is idempotent.
sections.threat: position drift double-counting or skipping blocks.

sections.name: build_prepared_privacy_transaction
sections.invariant: value is conserved — `sum(inputs) == sum(payment outputs) + change + fee` exactly for every shape.
sections.threat: value silently created or destroyed at assembly → fund loss / inflation.

sections.name: UniformDripPair
sections.invariant: two equal outputs, NO change output, excess folds into the fee to preserve output uniformity.
sections.threat: a change output breaks drip-pair uniformity and links the spend.

sections.name: UniformStandard
sections.invariant: change ≥ `MIN_OUTPUT_AMOUNT` becomes a real change output; below it, a dummy is emitted and the change folds into the fee.
sections.threat: dust change output degrades privacy / is unspendable.

sections.name: Legacy
sections.invariant: change ≥ MIN is its own output (fee unchanged), plus 0..=2 random dummy outputs; conservation still holds.
sections.threat: pre-activation path miscomputes change/fee → rejected or lossy tx.

sections.name: add_prepared_inputs
sections.invariant: rings are consumed only when their count, size and real-output identities match the prepared inputs (one snapshot).
sections.threat: recombining rings across snapshots → unprovable / rejected ring signatures.

sections.name: drip_pair_final_fee
sections.invariant: excess folds to fee only while `change ≤ total_send`; a larger excess fails closed rather than burning more to fee than is sent.
sections.threat: silent catastrophic fund loss (burn-to-fee footgun).

sections.name: estimate_tx_size
sections.invariant: size is a deterministic, conservative (`×2` margin) function of input/output/ring counts, monotonic in each.
sections.threat: under-estimate → fee too low → validator rejects the tx.

sections.name: scaled_fee
sections.invariant: `fee == size·MIN_FEE_PER_BYTE·mult/100` with saturating integer math (no overflow, no f64 drift) and monotone in size.
sections.threat: wallet estimate vs validator divergence → honest txs rejected.

sections.name: FeeMultiplier::from_f64
sections.invariant: multiplier is clamped to `[1.0, 100.0]`; NaN and negatives collapse to the neutral 1.0 floor.
sections.threat: NaN/negative multiplier panics or produces a zero/absurd fee.

sections.name: calculate_fee
sections.invariant: unscaled fee at a height is `size·MIN_FEE_PER_BYTE` and always strictly positive for a real tx.
sections.threat: zero fee → tx rejected as underpaying.

sections.name: estimate_fee_with_multiplier
sections.invariant: ring size is bound to `ring_size_at_height`, so the estimate matches what the validator charges.
sections.threat: stale/wrong ring size → fee mismatch → rejection.

sections.name: prepare_input
sections.invariant: the derived one-time secret satisfies `x·G == P` for the output's stealth key, so the spend is provable.
sections.threat: a wrong secret makes owned funds unspendable (CLSAG rejects).

sections.name: prepare_input
sections.invariant: subaddress outputs thread the per-subaddress offset `m` (`x = H(shared) + b + m`); main outputs stay byte-identical.
sections.threat: W-A — omitting `m` yields the wrong key image → funds unspendable.

sections.name: prepare_input
sections.invariant: an output with no canonical locator is refused, forcing a full rescan before it can be spent.
sections.threat: spending without a canonical locator would leak identity via a lookup.

sections.name: add_prepared_inputs
sections.invariant: the number of rings must equal the number of prepared inputs, else the call fails closed.
sections.threat: count mismatch → an input signs against the wrong ring.

sections.name: add_prepared_inputs
sections.invariant: every ring's size equals the context's `expected_ring_size` (the consensus size at that height).
sections.threat: a wrong-sized ring is rejected by the validator → fork/liveness edge.

sections.name: add_prepared_inputs
sections.invariant: rings are accepted only when their real outputs equal the prepared inputs' — no recombining across snapshots.
sections.threat: mixing rings from another snapshot → unprovable ring signature.

sections.name: create_transaction
sections.invariant: it still produces a structurally valid tx (recipient output + change output) so legacy callers keep compiling.
sections.threat: this path emits placeholder commitments — must never reach consensus.

sections.name: 2 balance guard
sections.invariant: it errors with `InsufficientBalance` when available spendable funds are below `total_send + fee`.
sections.threat: over-spend / building a tx that cannot be funded.

sections.name: 3 change output
sections.invariant: change is `input_sum - total_needed` and is emitted only when it reaches `MIN_OUTPUT_AMOUNT`; the fee is always strictly positive.
sections.threat: dust change output, or value silently lost.

sections.name: prepare_privacy_transaction_with_options
sections.invariant: the positional-arg shim builds an equivalent `SendRequest` and delegates unchanged.
sections.threat: shim drift silently changes send semantics for legacy callers.

sections.name: prepare_privacy_transaction
sections.invariant: on success `sum(inputs) == total_send + change_amount + estimated_fee` exactly.
sections.threat: value created or destroyed before signing → fund loss / inflation.

sections.name: 3 shape classification / output_count
sections.invariant: the transfer shape fixes the output count (uniform ⇒ standard count; legacy ⇒ `payments + padding`).
sections.threat: wrong shape → wrong fee/output layout → rejected or de-anonymised tx.

sections.name: 4 fee multiplier handling
sections.invariant: a NaN multiplier warns and falls back to the neutral 1.0 before selection.
sections.threat: NaN multiplier yields a zero/absurd fee → rejection.

sections.name: 5 fee growth re selection loop
sections.invariant: the loop re-selects and grows `required` until `input_sum ≥ total_send + fee`, so the added-input fee is always covered.
sections.threat: settling with inputs that under-cover the grown fee → rejected tx.

sections.name: 6 overflow / reservation safety
sections.invariant: a saturating `total_send + fee` never wraps to a satisfiable target, and prepare never writes a balance reservation.
sections.threat: wrap-around funds a tx that should fail; stray reservation locks funds.

sections.name: select_utxos
sections.invariant: accumulates UTXOs until `sum ≥ target`, else errors; an empty pool fails with `NoOutputsAvailable`.
sections.threat: returning an under-funded selection → unbalanced / rejected tx.

sections.name: select_utxos_uniform
sections.invariant: refuses to proceed with fewer than `STANDARD_INPUT_COUNT` UTXOs.
sections.threat: a single-input uniform tx breaks the fixed-shape anonymity model.

sections.name: select_utxos_uniform
sections.invariant: if even the largest pair cannot reach the target, it fails with a `NoUtxoPairCovers` diagnostic (no silent shortfall).
sections.threat: emitting a pair that under-covers the target → rejected tx.

sections.name: select_utxos_uniform
sections.invariant: picks among pairs within a small band of the minimum excess, favouring the tightest cover, not just the largest.
sections.threat: over-large excess is force-folded to fee → avoidable value burn.

sections.name: no_pair_covers_error
sections.invariant: the error reports target, utxo count, total, largest pair, and the max-safe amount after the fee reserve.
sections.threat: an opaque failure leaves the user unable to act (consolidate/split).

sections.name: ensure_spendable
sections.invariant: distinguishes `BalancePendingMaturity` (funds exist but are immature) from true `InsufficientBalance`, never over-reporting spendable funds.
sections.threat: spending immature outputs, or a misleading insufficient-funds error.

sections.name: Payment
sections.invariant: `is_subaddress` is stored faithfully; `new` defaults to a main address, `new_subaddress` sets the flag.
sections.threat: a mis-set flag makes a subaddress payment undetectable/unspendable.

sections.name: SpendContext::with_ring_size
sections.invariant: rejects a ring size below 2 and derives `min_output_age` from the target height.
sections.threat: a degenerate ring (<2) provides no privacy.

sections.name: effective_ring_size
sections.invariant: wherever the wallet can build a ring, its `ring_size_at_height` equals the size consensus requires.
sections.threat: 1d27d3c8-class fork surface — wallet emits a tx the validator rejects on ring size.

sections.name: TransferShape::classify
sections.invariant: classifies pre-activation sends as `Legacy`, a same-destination pair as `UniformDripPair`, and a single recipient as `UniformStandard`.
sections.threat: mis-classification → wrong output shape → rejection or de-anonymisation.

sections.name: SendRequest
sections.invariant: defaults to a neutral 1.0 fee multiplier, no memo and empty extra; builder setters only override what is set.
sections.threat: a bad default (e.g. zero fee) silently mis-fees every send.

sections.name: 6 prepared transaction accessors
sections.invariant: `real_outputs`, `ring_size`, and `input_count` on `Prepared{Privacy,Vesting}Transaction` reflect the selected inputs/context.
sections.threat: a stale accessor feeds the wrong rings/size into assembly.

sections.name: prepare_vesting_transaction
sections.invariant: the positional-arg shim builds an equivalent `VestingRequest` and delegates to `prepare_vesting` unchanged.
sections.threat: shim drift silently changes vesting semantics for legacy callers.

sections.name: prepare_vesting
sections.invariant: on success `sum(inputs) == amount + estimated_fee + change_amount` exactly.
sections.threat: value created or destroyed before signing → fund loss / inflation.

sections.name: prepare_vesting
sections.invariant: re-selects and grows `required` until inputs cover `amount + fee`, since each added input raises the fee.
sections.threat: settling under-funded → a rejected tx.

sections.name: build_prepared_vesting_transaction
sections.invariant: exactly one output carries `lock_height == unlock_height`.
sections.threat: a missing/wrong lock lets vested funds be spent early.

sections.name: build_prepared_vesting_transaction
sections.invariant: change ≥ MIN is a real output (fee unchanged); below MIN it folds into the fee, plus 0..=2 dummy outputs.
sections.threat: dust change output, or value silently lost.

sections.name: 6 lock height spendability
sections.invariant: the balance layer treats a vesting output as unspendable before `unlock_height` and spendable at/after it.
sections.threat: early spend of still-locked funds.

sections.name: build_privacy_transaction
sections.invariant: consumes the session and performs exactly one covered lookup bound to that session's snapshot, so a retry must start from a fresh node snapshot and inputs cannot be recombined across snapshots.
sections.threat: cross-snapshot ring mixing or silent input rediscovery that deanonymizes the spender.

sections.name: prepare_privacy_transaction
sections.invariant: the selected inputs equal payments + change + fee before any ring work, and insufficient funds error without reserving.
sections.threat: value creation or an unbalanced transaction.

sections.name: build_covered_request
sections.invariant: the single lookup's request and response are pinned to the session snapshot id, policy version and height ordering, and reject a real locator outside the snapshot.
sections.threat: a swapped or misordered decoy set.

sections.name: allocate_unique_rings
sections.invariant: the real output sits at a secret index in every ring, matched to its real identity, with no decoy public key repeated across rings.
sections.threat: real-output linkage or decoy reuse that breaks unlinkability.

sections.name: BuiltSpend
sections.invariant: the built spend seals selected outputs, key images, the canonical tx hash and encoded payload with a target height matching the snapshot, so submission cannot drift to different inputs.
sections.threat: build/submit input drift or a mismatched payload.

sections.name: submit_reserved
sections.invariant: inputs are reserved and persisted before any transaction bytes leave the process, and reservations are released only on a definitive rejection while an indeterminate result retains them.
sections.threat: broadcasting without a durable reservation, so a crash strands or double-spends the inputs.

sections.name: 2 reservation conflict guard
sections.invariant: an input already reserved by another transaction aborts before submission, leaving the prior claim untouched.
sections.threat: double-reservation of one UTXO across two spends.

sections.name: 3 persist before broadcast rollback
sections.invariant: a failed reservation persist releases the reservation in memory and reports the rollback without broadcasting anything.
sections.threat: a silent broadcast after persistence failed.

sections.name: 4 empty bindings guard
sections.invariant: a built spend with no input bindings is rejected before anything is reserved.
sections.threat: reserving or submitting a spend that binds no wallet inputs.

sections.name: validate_input_bindings
sections.invariant: every bound key image still maps to its exact bound wallet output under the same exclusive borrow used to reserve, else the caller must rebuild.
sections.threat: a build/submit race that rediscovers or rebinds different inputs.

sections.name: self.rpc.submit_encoded_transaction
sections.invariant: the outcome flows through the typed coordinator RPC, which maps a remote error to a definitive rejection but keeps transport/protocol failures Unknown so their reservations are retained.
sections.threat: a misclassified network result that releases reservations prematurely.

sections.name: SpendIntent
sections.invariant: an intent carries only user-level payment data with neutral fee/memo/extra defaults, folded into a `SendRequest` bound to the session's context.
sections.threat: fee or metadata drift from the caller's expectation.

sections.name: SpendSession
sections.invariant: not caller-constructible; obtainable only from `SpendCoordinator::begin`, binding snapshot identity, target height, ring size and maturity floor together.
sections.threat: a forged or mismatched session that recombines snapshots or uses a stale maturity floor.

sections.name: BuiltSpend::try_new
sections.invariant: sealing verifies the target height equals the snapshot-derived height and seals the canonical tx hash and encoded payload exactly once.
sections.threat: snapshot/height drift or a mismatched submission payload.

sections.name: bind_transaction_inputs
sections.invariant: exactly one binding per selected output paired to its key image, order preserved, with no duplicate output or key image.
sections.threat: double-reservation, input duplication or reordering.

sections.name: SpendInputBinding
sections.invariant: a binding pins one wallet output to the exact key image in the signed transaction, created only while sealing.
sections.threat: rebinding a key image to a different output at submit time.

sections.name: SpendSubmission
sections.invariant: a typed outcome enum where `MempoolAccepted` and `Unknown` retain reservations and are distinct from `Rejected`.
sections.threat: treating an indeterminate result as a rejection and releasing reservations into a double-spend.

sections.name: begin
sections.invariant: every session is bound to exactly one freshly validated decoy snapshot, with target height and maturity floor derived from that snapshot so later build/submit steps cannot recombine across snapshots.
sections.threat: cross-snapshot decoy mixing or a stale maturity floor that deanonymizes the real input.

sections.name: new
sections.invariant: a coordinator wraps exactly one typed `NodeRpcClient`, so all node I/O flows through the typed transport.
sections.threat: an untyped or duplicate transport path that bypasses submission classification.

sections.name: rpc
sections.invariant: exposes a shared read-only borrow of the client for diagnostics, never a second mutable transport.
sections.threat: an aliased client that could submit outside the reservation path.

sections.name: SubaddressManager::generate_at
sections.invariant: derivation is deterministic and distinct per `(account, index)` — each subaddress gets a unique spend key `D_i` and a distinct, unlinkable view key `C_i = a·D_i`.
sections.threat: colliding or linkable subaddresses would deanonymize a wallet's receiving addresses.

sections.name: SubaddressManager::generate_next
sections.invariant: allocates the next sequential index in an account (skipping the main `0/0`).
sections.threat: index reuse would collide two receive addresses.

sections.name: find_by_spend_public
sections.invariant: every generated subaddress (main + derived) is recoverable by spend key on scan, mapping back to its exact index.
sections.threat: a missing scan key means an owned output is never detected.

sections.name: compute_subaddress_spend_secret
sections.invariant: the subaddress spend secret `x_i = x + m` reproduces exactly the subaddress spend public `D_i`, and the main `0/0` secret is returned unchanged.
sections.threat: a mismatched offset (W-A) would make every subaddress output silently unspendable.

sections.name: pregenerate_lookahead
sections.invariant: extends the generated range to exactly `highest_used + lookahead`, clamped to `MAX_SUBADDRESSES_PER_ACCOUNT - 1`, starting from index 1 on a fresh account.
sections.threat: too small a gap window misses funds after a seed restore; an unclamped one derives out-of-range indices.

sections.name: export
sections.invariant: export→import round-trips labels and used flags and regenerates byte-identical spend keys deterministically.
sections.threat: a non-deterministic restore would leave the wallet not controlling its own subaddresses.

sections.name: Subaddress::address
sections.invariant: the wallet and the audit/view-key path derive identical keys per `(account, index)`, the main `0/0` is never double-counted, and a subaddress encodes to a distinct, round-tripping address.
sections.threat: Jun #26 — divergent formulas would make an auditor's key unable to scan any wallet subaddress.

sections.name: create
sections.invariant: a wallet built from a seed or mnemonic re-derives exactly the same primary keys and address, and a restore rescans to rediscover prior funds.
sections.threat: silent key divergence loses access to funds on restore.

sections.name: create_watch_only
sections.invariant: a watch-only wallet carries only a view secret (no spend secret), so it can detect incoming funds but can never sign.
sections.threat: a view-only export leaking spend authority.

sections.name: unlock
sections.invariant: unlock reconstructs live secrets from the encrypted file and lock zeroizes balance, history and subaddress caches back to a safe locked state.
sections.threat: plaintext secrets or stale balances surviving a lock.

sections.name: create_transfer
sections.invariant: a transfer is refused unless the wallet is unlocked and NOT watch-only, and the assembled tx conserves value (inputs == recipients + change + fee) with change returning to the sender.
sections.threat: watch-only spend attempts, or value creation/loss in assembly.

sections.name: create_vesting
sections.invariant: a vesting output stamps the requested unlock height onto the output lock-height and is unspendable until that boundary.
sections.threat: locked funds spendable early, or the lock never applied.

sections.name: export_view_key
sections.invariant: the confirmed export is password-gated and returns the view key for the named epoch only.
sections.threat: unauthenticated disclosure of the view key (history linkage).

sections.name: reserve_utxos
sections.invariant: reserved UTXOs are excluded from the available set atomically and reservations expire deterministically.
sections.threat: double-selecting the same UTXO into two concurrent txs.

sections.name: mark_spent_by_key_image
sections.invariant: marking by key image removes an output from spendable balance and unmarking restores it (the reorg-unspend path).
sections.threat: stale spent flags after a reorg permanently hiding recovered funds.

sections.name: revert_outgoing_above_height
sections.invariant: on a rewind only outgoing records above the new height are reset; incoming history and below-height records are untouched.
sections.threat: reorg corrupting confirmed history.

sections.name: derive_next_epoch
sections.invariant: rotating to a new key epoch advances the current epoch while retaining prior epochs so their funds stay detectable and spendable.
sections.threat: key rotation orphaning funds locked to an older epoch.

sections.name: save
sections.invariant: save writes encrypted sidecars whose reload losslessly reconstructs balance, history and scanned height.
sections.threat: a save that drops or corrupts UTXO/reservation state.

sections.name: record_incoming
sections.invariant: history records incoming and outgoing transactions and memos independently and correctly.
sections.threat: misattributed or lost transaction records.

sections.name: spendable_balance
sections.invariant: an output is spendable only once it clears min-output-age / coinbase maturity at the current height, with a saturating boundary that never underflows.
sections.threat: spending immature outputs that a later reorg could orphan.

sections.name: address
sections.invariant: address formatting is correct and distinct for primary vs subaddress and per network.
sections.threat: cross-network or primary/subaddress address confusion sending funds astray.

sections.name: new
sections.invariant: key derivation is deterministic in the master seed — the same seed reproduces the same epoch-0 keys, and distinct seeds produce distinct keys.
sections.threat: non-reproducible derivation would make seed backup / restore fail to recover the wallet's funds.

sections.name: derive_epoch
sections.invariant: spend and view secrets use distinct HMAC domain tags, so within an epoch they are cryptographically independent — the view secret is not the spend secret and cannot reproduce it.
sections.threat: a shared/derivable spend secret would let a shared view key spend.

sections.name: derive_epoch
sections.invariant: distinct epoch numbers derive fully independent spend AND view key material.
sections.threat: epoch collisions would defeat key rotation, linking rotated identities.

sections.name: watch_only
sections.invariant: a watch-only wallet is flagged watch-only yet initialized, carries no usable spend authority, and holds the `[0xFF; 32]` seed sentinel (never a real seed).
sections.threat: a watch-only wallet that could spend, or leaked a real seed, breaks the view-only custody boundary.

sections.name: master_seed_for_backup
sections.invariant: backup returns `Some(seed)` only for a real wallet and `None` for watch-only, so the `[0xFF; 32]` sentinel is never serialized as if it were a seed.
sections.threat: R-75 — backing up the sentinel silently produces a well-formed but WRONG restored wallet.

sections.name: set_mnemonic_phrase
sections.invariant: the phrase a wallet was created from is stored (in a `Zeroizing<String>`) and read back, or `None` when the wallet never carried one.
sections.threat: R-115 — losing the phrase across save cycles breaks mnemonic backup.

sections.name: supply_conservation
sections.invariant: total_supply + total_burned == Σ block reward over the canonical chain (no inflation, no lost coins)

sections.name: work_positive
sections.invariant: cumulative chain work is always strictly positive

sections.name: height_tip_agreement
sections.invariant: the reported chain height equals the tip block's own height (no split-state)
